POSITION OVERVIEW
At BDC, the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, your work contributes directly to the success of small and medium-sized businesses across Canada. As a KYC Analyst, you will provide administrative and analytical support to the Financing team by managing the Know Your Client (KYC) process for loan applications. You will review client files, gather and analyze KYC documentation, identify potential compliance concerns, and work closely with the Business Development Lead (BDL) and Underwriter to ensure complete and accurate submissions. At BDC, we value inclusion, equity, and diversity, and you can be yourself at work.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Lead the KYC process from end to end, ensuring the timely collection, review, analysis, and validation of required KYC documentation.
Review customer files to understand the overall financing request and identify missing information or documentation.
Analyze KYC information and documentation to identify potential non-compliance issues, risks, or concerns.
Escalate KYC-related findings and concerns to the Business Development Lead (BDL) as required.
Follow up directly with clients to obtain required information and documentation.
Manage multiple KYC files simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.
Collaborate closely with the Business Development Lead, Underwriter, and internal partners to ensure all KYC requirements are met.
Submit complete and error-free KYC documentation in accordance with established policies, procedures, and standards.
Provide timely, accurate, and professional service to existing and prospective clients.
Build and maintain effective working relationships with clients and internal stakeholders.
Stay up to date on changes to KYC policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, and industry trends that may impact BDC.
Support BDC's commitment to delivering a high-quality experience to Canadian entrepreneurs.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration or a related field.
Ability to analyze and interpret financial statements.
Strong business acumen.
Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional attention to detail.
Client service orientation with the ability to listen, identify issues, and support resolution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and manage multiple responsibilities simultaneously.
Ability to work independently and meet tight deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including:
Microsoft Word
Microsoft Excel
Microsoft Outlook
Ability to review, analyze, and validate KYC documentation and information.
Availability to work on-site a minimum of three (3) days per week.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting KYC (Know Your Client), compliance, anti-money laundering (AML), customer due diligence (CDD), or lending-related processes.
Experience working in a financial services, banking, lending, or commercial financing environment.
Demonstrated teamwork and collaboration skills.
Flexibility and adaptability in a fast-paced environment.
Creative problem-solving skills.
Bilingualism in English and French

POSITION OVERVIEW
BDC Capital
With more than $6 billion under management, BDC Capital is the investment arm of BDC and a strategic partner to Canada’s most innovative and high-potential companies. As Canada’s largest and most active technology investor, BDC Capital provides equity, venture capital, and growth and transition capital to help Canadian entrepreneurs build globally competitive companies.
BDC’s Defence Platform will mobilize an additional $6 billion in financing, investment and advisory solutions to support Canadian businesses and strengthen Canada’s defence and security ecosystem. Within the Platform, BDC Capital is investing through direct and indirect strategies to accelerate defence innovation, strengthen Canadian capabilities and support technologies with defence-focused or dual-use applications.
Reporting to the Managing Director, Fund Investments, the
Associate Director / Director, Fund Investments
will play a leading role in sourcing, underwriting, executing and managing investments in venture capital and private equity funds aligned with Canada’s defence and national-sovereignty priorities.
Your primary focus will be the Defence Fund Investments mandate. You will also contribute to BDC Capital’s broader fund-investment activities across stages, sectors and regions in Canada.
You will lead substantial components of the investment process, develop and defend investment recommendations, manage selected GP relationships and portfolio responsibilities, and guide Associates and Analysts. You will combine institutional fund-investing judgment with a growing understanding of dual-use technologies, defence markets, procurement pathways and the Canadian and allied defence ecosystem.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Investment Sourcing and Underwriting
Help source and assess high-quality venture capital and private equity fund investment opportunities, with a particular focus on defence, dual-use and deep technology.
Lead significant components of GP due diligence, including assessment of investment strategy, team, track record and attribution, portfolio construction, sourcing capabilities, fund economics, terms, risks and expected returns.
Analyze underlying portfolios and pipelines to assess strategy execution, concentration, market exposure and alignment with BDC’s mandate.
Prepare investment memoranda and present and defend recommendations to the BDC Capital Funds Investment Committee.
Guide Associates and Analysts in the analysis and execution of investment opportunities.
Transaction Execution and Portfolio Management
Participate in negotiations with fund managers and work with Legal and other internal teams on LPAs, side letters and investment documentation.
Manage an assigned portfolio of fund investments and maintain strong relationships with GPs.
Monitor financial performance, portfolio developments, organizational changes, strategy execution and emerging risks.
Develop recommendations on re-ups, amendments, consents and other portfolio decisions.
Assess portfolio construction, concentration, pacing, cash flows and risk/return trends to inform future capital allocation.
Represent BDC, as appropriate, on LPACs and other investor-governance forums.
Collaboration and Market Presence
Collaborate closely with BDC Capital’s Fund Investments and direct-investing teams and with colleagues across BDC involved in the Defence Platform.
Develop relationships with fund managers, institutional investors and other ecosystem participants and represent BDC Capital at relevant industry events.
Share market intelligence and insights that support BDC’s broader investment and strategic objectives.
Coach and support the development of Associates and Analysts.
Defence and Dual-Use Specialization
Prior defence-investing experience is an asset, not a prerequisite. We are looking for an a person with the curiosity, judgment and commitment to develop meaningful expertise in Canada’s defence and dual-use investment ecosystem.
Develop strong knowledge of dual-use and defence technologies, defence procurement cycles, deep-tech commercialization and the role of prime contractors, integrators and government customers.
Assess fund managers’ defence-sector expertise, networks, technical-diligence capabilities and ability to support portfolio companies in accessing Canadian and allied defence markets.
Evaluate relevant indicators including procurement traction, technology and manufacturing readiness, supply-chain resilience and commercial-market potential.
Contribute to defence-specific portfolio monitoring and reporting, including financial performance, strategic alignment and material risks.
Build relationships across the Canadian and allied defence, investment, government and innovation ecosystems.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
5–7 years of relevant investment experience, including at least 2 years of direct experience underwriting and/or managing venture capital or private equity fund investments, or in a closely related institutional manager-selection role.
Strong understanding of venture capital and/or private equity fund structures, economics, performance analysis and portfolio management.
Experience leading significant components of investment due diligence and developing recommendations for an investment committee or equivalent decision-making body.
Familiarity with fund documentation and commercial negotiations.
Strong financial, analytical, written and verbal communication skills.
Sound investment judgment, intellectual curiosity and the ability to manage multiple workstreams with appropriate autonomy.
Strong relationship-management skills and the ability to work effectively with senior internal and external stakeholders.
Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, science, engineering, law or another relevant discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Fluency in both Canadian official languages (English & French) is an asset.

title: Senior Associate, Listed Real Estate - Equities Analyst (London or Toronto)
description:
Purpose. Performance. People.
Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
As an Equity Analyst on the Listed Real Estate team, you will conduct rigorous fundamental research and valuation analysis to support a concentrated, long-only portfolio of high-conviction investments. Working within a small, collaborative team, you will lead coverage of selected UK and European real estate subsectors, with potential exposure to India and the United States, and translate your research into recommendations that inform portfolio construction and investment decisions.
The Team
Real Assets invests globally across real estate, infrastructure, and conventional and renewable energy assets, supporting the Fund’s long-term investment objectives. Within Real Assets, the Listed Real Assets group invests across listed real estate, energy and infrastructure. The Listed Real Estate team manages a concentrated, long-only strategy built on fundamental research, deep valuation analysis and high-conviction portfolio construction.
Accountabilities
Conduct detailed fundamental research and financial modelling to evaluate opportunities across the listed real estate universe
Lead coverage of designated regional subsectors, with an initial focus on the UK and Europe and potential coverage of India and the United States
Develop company-level valuations using long-term cash flow forecasts and relative-value frameworks, identifying price-to-value divergences and potential catalysts
Monitor industry trends, market dynamics and company-specific developments to inform investment recommendations
Prepare clear, high-quality investment memoranda and portfolio updates for internal committees
Collaborate across Private Real Estate, Active Equities and Listed Real Assets, while supporting portfolio reviews, data analysis and performance attribution.
What You Bring
Relevant equity research or investment experience, ideally covering publicly listed real estate companies, including REITs and developers, across multiple European sectors
Strong financial modelling, accounting and equity valuation capabilities, combined with advanced Excel skills; familiarity with Capital IQ or similar tools is an asset
A genuine interest in investing and a disciplined, fundamentals-driven approach to valuation
Intellectual curiosity and the ability to distinguish key investment drivers from market noise
Adaptability to a structured investment process and openness to learning and applying the team’s valuation framework
Clear analytical and communication skills, with the ability to present and constructively challenge investment ideas
A collaborative and humble approach, with a willingness to support shared team outcomes and travel occasionally
You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to
high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.
We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.
Inclusion & Accessibility
CPP Investments is committed to
equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.
Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud
CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.
CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.
#LI-ONSITE

title: Managing Director, Credit Restructuring
description:
Purpose. Performance. People.
Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
Credit Investments (CI) is seeking an experienced restructuring professional to strengthen its capability to manage underperforming, stressed and distressed credit investments as the portfolio grows in scale and complexity.
The Managing Director, Restructuring will provide dedicated senior creditor-side expertise across workouts, liability management exercises (LMEs), restructurings, liquidity solutions and other stressed situations. The role will partner with CI investment teams to preserve investment value, maximize recoveries and support effective positioning ahead of key events.
The Team
Credit Investments currently manages assets in excess of $80.5 billion; investment deal sizes range from $50M to over $1B. The Credit Investments team has over 147 investment professionals across North America, Europe and Asia.
Reporting to the Head of Credit Strategy, the role will work closely with CI investment teams, Legal, Portfolio Management and senior leadership, and will contribute to broader CPP Investments matters where restructuring expertise can add value. The role is expected to be based in Toronto or New York.
Accountabilities
Lead Restructuring Strategy and Execution
Serve as CI's senior restructuring expert and provide commercial leadership and decision-making authority on material stressed and distressed investments.
Partner with investment teams to develop and execute restructuring strategies designed to protect investment value and maximize recoveries. The restructuring lead and relevant deal team will be co-accountable, with the deal team retaining ownership of the ultimate investment outcome.
Lead negotiations involving amendments, waivers, recapitalizations, exchange offers, LMEs, rescue financings, asset sales, refinancings and formal restructuring processes.
Assess alternative restructuring pathways and advise on likely outcomes, negotiating leverage, new-money requirements, timing and execution risk, drawing on relevant market precedents and judgment on key economic terms.
Support investment teams in anticipating potential creditor actions and positioning CI effectively ahead of key events.
Provide Senior Commercial Judgment
Provide independent challenge and advice on capital structure, liquidity, valuation, recovery scenarios, financing alternatives and strategic options in distressed situations.
Help teams identify and use sources of negotiating leverage, including opportunities to build alignment with other stakeholders, while engaging constructively and credibly with borrowers, sponsors, shareholders and other creditors.
Advise on creditor-group formation, steering committees and lender-coordination processes, and support the selection and efficient direction of external restructuring bankers, financial advisers and other specialists.
Bring current restructuring market intelligence, conventions and precedents to portfolio-management decisions.
Assess proposed outcomes across recovery value, incremental capital, time to resolution, external costs, reputational considerations and demands on deal-team capacity. Success will be measured primarily through avoided losses and recoveries achieved rather than direct AUM attribution.
Partner with Deal Teams and Legal
Work alongside existing deal teams as athe lead restructuring specialist adviser rather than operating as a separate distressed-investing team; deal teams remain actively involved and accountable for the investment outcome.
Work closely with CI Legal, including dedicated restructuring legal resources, to integrate commercial, negotiating and legal strategy. Legal will advise on documentation, contractual rights and available legal pathways, while this role will lead the commercial strategy and value-maximizing trade-offs informed by that advice.
Partner with Portfolio Management and senior CI leadership to identify situations requiring early intervention and build strong working relationships across CI and, where appropriate, other CPP Investments departments.
Strengthen CI's Restructuring Platform
Play a leadership role in CI's restructuring panel, including triaging situations, challenging strategies and mobilizing resources.
Establish regular watchlist triage to identify situations where specialist involvement can add value before a formal default or restructuring.
Develop restructuring playbooks, precedent libraries, market intelligence and other institutional resources; lead post-mortems and transfer lessons across CI investment teams.
Coach and develop investment professionals to increase restructuring knowledge and judgment and help build a scalable capability for a substantially larger CI portfolio. The role will have no direct people-leadership responsibilities initially, although this may change as the portfolio and workout activity grow.
Broader Contribution
During periods of lower restructuring activity, contribute to broader CI strategic and portfolio initiatives where restructuring, capital-structure, valuation, transaction or market expertise can add value.
Where appropriate, provide restructuring expertise to other parts of CPP Investments and represent CPP Investments credibly with borrowers, sponsors, banks, advisers and institutional creditors in complex and sensitive situations.
What You Bring
Significant restructuring experience gained as a banker or adviser at a leading restructuring advisory firm, or investment bank.
Senior-level experience (approximately 15 years) consistent with a Managing Director appointment, with a demonstrated ability to lead complex restructuring processes and advise sophisticated institutional clients.
Deep creditor-side experience representing lenders, bondholders, creditor groups and/or institutional investors.
Extensive experience with LMEs, complex out-of-court restructurings and formal restructuring processes.
Strong expertise in liquidity analysis, capital structures, valuation, recovery analysis, financing alternatives and transaction execution.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with sponsors, companies, creditor groups and advisers in high-stakes situations.
Strong knowledge of restructuring market conventions, precedents and creditor dynamics.
Meaningful familiarity with restructuring documentation and legal concepts, and the ability to work effectively with counsel.
Strong executive presence and judgment, with the ability to influence senior investment professionals while operating in a collaborative, advisory capacity.
Ability to move between detailed transaction execution and broader strategic judgment, with a collaborative mindset suited to CI's deal-team ownership model.

You will use AI, automation, and data tools to redesign manual and repetitive workflows, strengthen controls, and make the platform more scalable. Own the ongoing management and monitoring of structured credit investments and flow programs across the Americas, developing a deep understanding of each investment’s thesis, structure, economics, risks, and performance drivers.
Manage the recurring execution of forward flows, warehouses, asset purchase facilities, securitizations, and related financing structures, including funding, borrowing bases, waterfalls, and transaction reporting.
Analyze borrower, servicer, collateral, and transaction data to assess performance against underwriting expectations, identify emerging trends and risks, and develop actionable investment insights.
Continuously redesign how the work gets done. Use AI, automation, Python, SQL, and external service providers to eliminate repetitive manual work, improve controls and data quality, and build scalable workflows.
Develop clear views on portfolio performance and material developments, communicate them effectively to deal teams and other stakeholders, and proactively identify issues requiring action.
Build and improve the monitoring, reporting, analytical, and control infrastructure needed to manage a growing structured credit portfolio efficiently.
Partner closely with investment teams and functions across CPP Investments, taking on increasingly sophisticated responsibilities as your knowledge and judgment develop.

Strong understanding of structured credit products and financing structures, with experience in areas such as forward flows, warehouse facilities, asset-backed lending, ABS, CLOs or SRTs.
Excellent credit, analytical, and financial modeling skills, with the curiosity to translate analysis into investment conclusions.
Demonstrated ability to use AI, Python, SQL, or similar technologies to improve workflows, analyze data, and increase team effectiveness.
High degree of ownership and initiative. You identify problems, develop solutions, and drive work forward without waiting for a detailed playbook.
Intellectual curiosity and ambition to grow from process execution into increasingly sophisticated portfolio analysis, judgment, and portfolio management responsibility.
Strong attention to detail and judgment: automation should reduce manual work without compromising the rigor, controls, and accuracy required to manage institutional capital.
Strong communication skills and the ability to turn complex information into clear conclusions, recommendations, and actions.

Winter Session: Monday January 11 to Friday February 19, 2027

Our six-week full-time program offers students hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments.

Interns parallel the programs they're assigned to. Most work is in person, Monday to Friday. However, some placements are hybrid home-office arrangements. Some roles require weekend shifts and/or early morning or late afternoon/evening work.

The Current
, our flagship audio current affairs program that shapes the national conversation and amplifies the voices that define our time. This is a full-time temporary role for nine months, behind a leave. The job is based in Toronto.
YOUR ROLE
You’ll be leading a team of accomplished journalists who go beyond the news - uncovering the human stories behind the headlines, challenging the status quo and driving the cultural and political discourse in Canada.
The successful candidate will be a creative thinker who puts audience needs at the centre of their decision-making, shaping content that plays equally well as a podcast as it does on terrestrial radio. You bring a deep knowledge of narrative storytelling and immersive sound design. You are at the leading edge of changing audience consumption trends on audio and in digital spaces. You identify stories that can be shared across CBC News owned and operated apps, YouTube and TikTok with a focus on reaching our audiences on their mobile devices.
You will oversee our daily coverage decisions and be the go-to person on journalistic policy and judgement. You have experience leading teams covering all aspects of journalism, from breaking news to deep-dive investigative projects. You have a keen knowledge of legal and ethical risk management. You value the service of a public broadcaster and ensure all of our work adheres to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices, upholding our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance,  impartiality and integrity.
You’ll approach your work with an open mind and a genuine curiosity that encourages experimentation and leads to transformative change. You’ll be comfortable challenging assumptions and seeking out a variety of perspectives to better reflect our audiences.
You’re a strategic thinker who sets direction and delegates effectively. You react decisively to major developments, track stories in real time and reshape shows on the fly to ensure our audiences are getting the content they need to know. You understand that the demands of a daily program can be a flat-out sprint to deadline with a myriad of complex decisions to make along the way, so organizational skills are key.
You have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions and experiences and consider those in programming decisions. You live and promote the values of inclusion and create a respectful work culture.
You support and develop your team through mentoring and meaningful, constructive feedback.
You’re a leader who is excited to show up to work knowing anything can happen on their watch, thrives when news breaks, and is at their best when navigating change.
At CBC News we value collaboration, with your team and with CBC News colleagues and as such you’ll be required to be on-site at the Toronto Broadcast Centre weekdays. Your daily schedule will be determined by production needs. You can expect some early mornings, late evenings or overtime in this role.
YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

The CBC News Summer Scholarship
In memory of Joan Donaldson and Peter Gzowski
CBC News is proud to offer its summer scholarship to aspiring journalists from across the country, a four-month, in-person program that provides valuable hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments. The scholarship replaces and builds on the successes of two former CBC programs for emerging journalists – the Joan Donaldson Scholarship and the Peter Gzowski Internship – bringing them together in one program.
The program is designed to give high-potential emerging journalists experience in both CBC News’ national programming units in Toronto, as well as regional newsrooms across the country, setting them up for potential employment at CBC in the long term.
The 2027 program will run from May through August 2027. May and June will be spent in Toronto at the CBC Broadcast Centre; July and August will be spent in a CBC regional station.
CBC provides a robust training program and ongoing mentorship to ensure scholars are properly supported during the program.
Who is eligible?
Graduating post-secondary students (college or university) in their final year of study. (Applicants will be considered if they have graduated or will graduate between fall 2026 and spring 2027. Students must have finished all classes and assignments by the start of the program on May 3, 2027).
Candidates must be legally eligible to work in Canada.
Candidates must be able to work on a full-time, in-person basis during the program, the first two months in Toronto, and the subsequent two months in a regional station.
Candidates must be able to work at CBC after the scholarship ends, should there be an opportunity to do so.
Formal journalism education is not required, however candidates must demonstrate they have journalism skills and experience.
Candidates must possess a full valid Canadian driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.
What qualities are we looking for?
A strong potential for producing journalism marked by curiosity, critical thinking, command of facts, understanding of context and clarity of expression.
The ability to generate, pitch and pursue strong, original, creative story ideas.
A curiosity about the world and a strong connection to and engagement in local communities.
A willingness to learn and tackle new tasks across all CBC platforms (digital, audio, video, social
A commitment to upholding journalistic and ethical standards and to producing work that is fair, balanced, accurate and thoughtful.
A proven work ethic, strong communication skills and a positive, team-first attitude.
Genuine interest in the ideals and practice of public interest journalism at the CBC, including an
understanding of the importance of broadening the range of perspectives, experiences and points of view reflected in mainstream media.
A strong desire to
live and promote the values of an inclusive and respectful work culture.
Ability to work in-person at CBC in Toronto for two months, and in-person in a regional CBC station for two months.
Ability and Willingness to work flexible hours as required.
What work will scholars do?
Scholars will be placed at a CBC News national program/unit, and then in a CBC regional station. The exact work will depend on those particular placements, but generally, scholars will participate in all aspects of newsgathering for digital, audio, video and social. Tasks could include:
Pitching and chasing original story ideas
Conducting research and interviews
Gathering and editing audio and video
Fact-checking, writing and packaging stories and scripts
Booking guests for live interviews
Presenting material on-air/online
What are the potential placements?
In May and June, scholars will receive training and then be placed with a national program or unit in Toronto. In July and August, scholars will be placed in a regional station. You can read more about the placement areas
here
.
Compensation details
These are paid, full-time positions; compensation is approximately $23/hour.
Scholars are eligible for benefits and accrue five vacation days by the end of the placement
CBC will pay work-related travel costs, but scholars are responsible for their own accommodation and living expenses in both locations.
What are the application requirements?
To be eligible to be considered, candidates must ensure they provide a single PDF that consists of the following items:
A one-page cover letter that explains what you will bring to the program
A resume, maximum two pages
One page listing three examples of your journalism work: Please provide links to your work, not the actual files. If you’ve worked in more than one medium make sure your examples reflect that range (ie. text, audio, video, interactive, etc). One of them should be an example of timely and topical coverage (breaking news, same-day turnaround, etc.). For each link, please write one sentence about why you chose to submit this piece.
Candidates will also be required to answer a series of questions on the application form to verify eligibility in the program and other competencies. Please be prepared to provide the name and contact information of one person who would be able to confidently speak to your journalism skills and recommend you for the program. At this stage, you will also be asked to identify your preferences for potential regional placement areas if you are selected for the program. Ensure you review
the options
as you make your selections.

CBC ABILICREW PLACEMENTS FOR EXCELLENCE PROGRAM
Job title: CAPE - CBC Sports Researcher
This role described below is part of CBC’s CAPE program which is specifically for people with disabilities*. CAPE is a six-month paid placement program that aims to kick-start the careers of people with disabilities, eliminate barriers to employment, showcase individual talents and generate more discussion, learning and content related to disability, accessibility and inclusion.
The program will run from January 11 until June 25, 2027.
What do you need to be eligible?
You must self-identify as a person with a disability*.
You must have no prior long-term work experience with the CBC.
You must be able to work legally in Canada.
You must be available for the assigned workweek during the program, to be discussed during the interview process (up to 38.75 hours-some roles have more flexibility).
*The Accessible Canada Act definition of disability:
“means any impairment, including a physical, mental, intellectual, cognitive, learning, communication or sensory impairment—or a functional limitation—whether permanent, temporary or episodic in nature, or evident or not, that, in interaction with a barrier, hinders a person’s full and equal participation in society."
Please note by applying for this role you give consent to be recognized as a “CAPE participant” and as identifying as a person with a disability. No further information will be shared without your permission.
This position offers accommodation opportunities such as telework/remote and flexible schedules. However the role is based in Toronto.
Part of the CAPE program includes attending weekly online group meetings with other CAPE participants. These meetings will be scheduled with your manager’s approval.
Your role and how you will make an impact:
As a Researcher within CBC Sports you will gather and assist in the production and distribution of content related to CBC Sports broadcast, Olympic Features and Digital content. The ideal candidate will have a background/education in broadcast media or journalism.

Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills.

Integrated Roadmap Planning: Maintain global and centralized visibility of the short-, medium-, and long-term real estate roadmap (annual and 5-year plans).
Demand/Capacity Balancing: Continuously assess internal and external team workloads against capacity envelopes to proactively anticipate bottlenecks and plan future requirements effectively.

Dashboards and Visibility: Develop and maintain Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and visual tracking tools to provide stakeholders with real-time visibility into costs, timelines, and expected benefits.
Data Integrity: Ensure the collection, centralization, and modeling of operational and financial portfolio data to support informed, value-driven decision-making.
Escalation process: Identify and resolve escalated tactical issues impeding project delivery, preparing files for the Governance Committee when required. Identify risk or issues that require escalation to the SteerCo for resolution.
Standardized Risk Management and Partner Tracking
Risk Management Process: Based on a risk-wise approach, drive informed risk management strategies, tracking action plans to reduce overall portfolio exposure.
Partner Performance Monitoring: Monitor the tactical and operational performance of PDS service provider, ensuring adherence to CBC/Radio-Canada’s quality control and compliance standards.

As a Senior Agile Project Manager / Release Train Engineer (APM/RTE) within the T&I Value Management and Delivery Office, you serve as a program-level orchestrator and pivotal bridge between agile product delivery and traditional enterprise governance.  Assigned to a high-impact product family, you will operate within a SAFe-inspired agile bubble; while navigating fixed financial, legal, and operational parameters of a public broadcasting environment.
This is an intensive matrix leadership position. You will work across multiple teams, departments, and corporate functions where you do not possess direct line-management or hierarchical organizational authority. Success requires exceptional lateral leadership, emotional intelligence, and the ability to influence peers, product leaders, corporate partners, and external technology vendors toward shared program outcomes.
Foundational Leadership Competencies
Beyond technical agile process knowledge, you possess foundational capabilities that enable effective execution in a complex matrix enterprise:
Influencing Without Authority & Lateral Leadership:
proven ability to align cross-functional peers, Product Owners, Solution Architects, and non-agile business partners behind program objectives without formal line-management authority. Mastery in negotiation, active listening, and building voluntary consensus across matrixed boundaries.
Emotional Intelligence (EQ) & Political Acumen:
high self-awareness, diplomacy, and emotional control when navigating political dynamics, competing stakeholder priorities, or resistance to change.  Ability to de-escalate friction calmly and turn interpersonal misalignment into constructive problem-solving.
Trust-Building & Program Evangelism:
ability to act as an energetic cheerleader and trusted advisor who builds psychological safety and enthusiasm within delivery teams, while simultaneously instilling confidence, credibility, and rigor among executive sponsors and traditional corporate functions.
Resilience & Comfort with Ambiguity:
high tolerance for ambiguity, fluid priorities, and non-standard operating environments. Ability to remain composed under pressure, balancing the discipline of traditional corporate controls with the responsiveness of agile delivery.
Pragmatic Tailoring & Systems Thinking:
pragmatic, flexible and solution-oriented mindset that balances adherence to core frameworks with fit-for-purpose execution.  Able to tailor day-to-day practices and propose refinements while adhering to core structures to drive business value.
Presentation Skills & Audience Adaptability:
highly comfortable and effective presenting in English and in French to varying audiences, including key business partners, at different levels, tailoring messaging and presentation to the audience and objectives.

Scaled Agile Cadence & Program-Level Orchestration:

Dependency, Risk & Impediment Resolution:
Identify, map, and resolve cross-team dependencies and systemic program impediments alongside Scrum Masters, while maintaining an active program risk register with strategic escalation paths.
Strategic Alignment & Governance Compliance:
Ensure product family backlogs and quarterly objectives remain strictly aligned with Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) strategic goals and corporate governance standards.
Tooling Infrastructure & Delivery Visibility:
Oversee and maintain program-level Jira and Confluence workspace structures to ensure full delivery transparency across backlogs, epics, and features.
Financial Stewardship & Budget Oversight:

Operational Model Execution:
Partner with the Transformation Lead to operationalize, run, and sustain the scaled agile delivery cadence across all product family teams.
Change Mobilization & Bilingual Enablement:
Support cross-departmental change mobilization while enabling seamless bilingual (English/French) communication across distributed product hubs in Montreal and Toronto.
Vendor & Partner Governance:
Co-manage strategic software supplier delivery alongside Product leadership, aligning vendor specifications, contractual milestones, and delivery cadences with internal backlogs & roadmaps.
Performance Metrics & Value Realization:
Develop and maintain dashboards to track flow metrics, delivery velocity, and business value realization to drive continuous program improvement.
Agile Culture & Bureaucracy Reduction:
Embody a servant-leadership posture ('Facilitator vs. Controller'), fostering transparency, team autonomy, and the principle that 'People own the process' while actively streamlining administrative overhead.
Multi-Tier Reporting Cadences:
Drive structured reporting across four executive cadences: Weekly operational updates, Bi-weekly leadership syncs, Monthly performance reviews, and Quarterly reporting to Governance Committees and the Board of Directors.

experience facilitating PI Planning / Quarterly Alignment, multi-team demos, and Program Syncs within SAFe or hybrid scaled agile delivery environments.

description:

employer-matched
defined benefit pension plan
, and a comprehensive and competitive benefits plan. We prioritize learning and development, wellbeing, diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging, and community giving.
Join FSRA and help us shape the future of regulation for generations to come!
Job Description:
Multiple vacancies both permanent and fixed term
PURPOSE OF POSITION(S)
Accountable for providing specialized forensic investigation expertise and team leadership to complex investigations to determine whether there have been contraventions under the nine (9) provincial Acts that FSRA enforces within all regulated financial services sectors. To act as Provincial Offences Officer and
/
or Special Constable under delegated authority in preparing and assisting in enforcement proceedings and prosecutions.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Leads the review and analysis of evidence collected relating to issues of non-compliance brought forward by the Market Conduct Compliance Team to the Case Management Committee. Interviews Compliance staff to gather further information to assess the need for investigation and determine the relative priorities of each investigation.
Leads multiple complex investigations, forensic examinations, and reviews of sensitive, contentious situations, potential risks or allegations related to contraventions and fraud including misapplication, misappropriation, conflict of interest or dishonesty in the conduct of Sector business.
Evaluates and determines investigative objectives, strategies, methods and resourcing, and information gathering (i.e., interviewing parties, identifying, and interviewing relevant witnesses), gathering and securing documentary and other evidence in accordance with the Ontario Evidence Act, Canada Evidence Act and Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
With a search warrant, or other investigative evidence gathering tools and techniques, collects and securely preserves all documents and records on the premises or elsewhere that are relevant to the investigation.
Applies investigative expertise, protocols, tools, technologies, methodologies, and questioning techniques to achieve maximum efficiency and effectiveness in interviewing subjects and witnesses, in the gathering of evidence and formulation of conclusions and recommendations pursuant to an investigation. Evaluates the credibility, relevance and probative value of evidence, and determines the factual circumstances of situations.
Ensures privacy and confidentiality is maintained throughout all phases of investigations.
Weighs and  analyzes evidence in a fair, impartial, and appropriately discrete and thorough manner to adequately support investigation results and meet admissibility requirements of any subsequent proceedings. relating to potential contraventions or offences pursuant to FSRA Acts, Provincial Offences Act or Criminal Code. Prepares formal investigative reports, briefing notes, memoranda and analytical summaries to support findings for the Management and for litigation purposes and enforcement actions supported by evidence (e.g., sanctions including administrative monetary penalties, compliance order, licence suspension or revocation, quasi-criminal or criminal charges, etc.). Leads and/or coordinates the preparation of other correspondence to respond to issues.
Conducts analysis and develops in-depth reports/statistics detailing multi-faceted information to demonstrate trends and patterns across sectors.
Coordinates and assists law enforcement partners on the particulars, evidence or conclusions regarding any investigation or potential investigation that has criminal ramifications.
Works with aligned FSRA or external counsel to track and maintain the flow of investigations from intake to the final disposition phase, as required.
Leads the development/drafting of relevant court documentation (e.g., Crown Briefs, etc.) and appears as a witness in proceedings.
Alerts management to control issues requiring expeditious action and keeps management and executives informed of the status and outcomes of investigative activity. Participates in meetings with management and executive leadership to provide updates on investigations, contentious investigation issues or impending investigations.
Provides expertise and leadership to a team of investigators (including external consultants). Mentors and coaches the team and facilitates a positive work environment and encourages staff to contribute to continuous improvement in the delivery of investigation activities. Assigns and monitors work, provides technical guidance, and reviews work files to evaluate evidence and resolve problems within the framework of FSRA standards and expectations.
Leads the development and implementation of proactive strategies to assist management in detecting and deterring misconduct, including the provision of expertise and advice in fraud management, the development of tools, techniques, and processes to manage exposure.
Develops training materials and delivers educational sessions for colleagues and other functional areas in areas such as fraud, interviewing, conflict of interest and risk awareness.
Contributes expertise to the development of investigative tools and quality practice standards, guidelines and procedures and continuous improvement activities and communicates information to the team on the implementation of new/amended policy/legislation, and program delivery processes.
Participates in FSRA and other Regulatory or Law Enforcement committees or organizations to provide input to address prevention, detection and disruption activities, practices, and information sharing.
QUALIFICATIONS
Education and Experience
University degree in related field including accounting, economics, business, commerce, criminology, or psychology.
Proven experience leading and conducting complex forensic investigations in government or the financial sector.
Experience interviewing subjects is required.
Security clearance required.
Travel throughout the province.
Knowledge and Skills
Strong knowledge of the sectors FSRA regulates and the 9 pieces of legislation it enforces (e.g., Insurance Act,
Mortgage Brokerages, Lenders and Administrators Act, 2006, Credit Union and Caisse Populaires Act, Pension Benefits Act, Loan and Trust Corporations Act
, etc.).
Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of and experience in court procedures  the Criminal Code, Charter of Rights and Freedoms, Canada Evidence Act, Ontario Evidence Act, Ontario Provincial Offences Act, PIPEDA, FIPPA and MFIPPA and related case law.
In-depth knowledge of investigation principles, theories, practices, standards and tools, and interviewing techniques to collect, preserve and present evidence, and to interview witnesses in order to obtain information.
Financial analysis techniques to determine circumstances of fraudulent activity, to conduct sensitive questioning of witnesses and subjects and to apply an operational understanding of controls in conducting vulnerability assessments pertaining to fraud exposures.
Risk assessment and risk management principles to make recommendations on complex issues.
Information technology sufficient to understand its effect on controls and inherent weaknesses in providing opportunities for fraud and dishonesty.
Knowledge of court procedures, practices, and processes to prepare and submit information on possible prosecutions, assist counsel in legal actions, and to act as an agent of FSRA in court proceedings.
Leadership skills to provide oversight of investigations and to coach and mentor the team to achieve results and motivate performance.
Ability to gather, analyze, and synthesize information and data from multiple sources and summarize investigative findings clearly and concisely in writing.
Excellent judgment, discretion, integrity, and ability to maintain neutrality in challenging situations.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and an appreciation for detail and thoroughness.
Tactical communication skills to maintain composure and adjust behaviour to suit the individual and situation (including posture, tone, assertiveness, spatial distance, eye contact, facial expressions) and to diffuse situations when required, adjusting communication style to accommodate an audience or situation.
Active listening skills to gain valuable information during interviews, to establish rapport with a variety of people in the course of conducting investigations; to be assertive yet professional when interacting with witnesses and corporate representatives.
Strong interpersonal, communication skills, and superior writing and documentation skills to conduct meetings, prepare investigation, witness or supplemental reports, recommendations, and other materials, develop and deliver training and facilitate educational sessions for topics such as fraud, risk and conflict of interest.
Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams) and other applications

IMCO’s actively managed Global Credit strategy (~$10.1B AUM) delivers higher risk-adjusted returns through a unified approach to credit investing, integrating public and private credit within a single, globally diversified portfolio. The strategy adopts a holistic approach to portfolio construction, allocating across public credit segments, including investment grade, high yield, leveraged loans, and structured credit, alongside private credit segments to capture relative value opportunities, enhance diversification, and optimize liquidity and return outcomes across market cycles.
Our collaborative culture and value-add approach to strategic partnerships makes us a preferred partner to some of the largest investors in the world. We have a targeted strategy to grow our highly diversified Global Credit portfolio and are looking for a highly motivated Associate Portfolio Manager to join our Global Credit team with a focus on public credit!
The Associate Portfolio Manager, Public Credit will play a key role in managing IMCO’s externally managed Public Credit portfolio, with responsibilities spanning manager selection and due diligence, portfolio strategy and construction, and ongoing monitoring and oversight. The role combines rigorous investment analysis with active portfolio management, while also contributing to ongoing initiatives to enhance the Global Credit platform and target operating model, including the implementation of investment systems and processes and the development of advanced analytics and AI capabilities to improve portfolio insights and support investment decision-making.
As a Member of Our Global Credit Team, You Will Contribute Across Three Core Areas: Manager Selection & Oversight, Portfolio Management and Strategy, and Platform Enhancement:
Provide analytical and portfolio management support to the Managing Director in overseeing externally managed public credit portfolios on a day-to-day basis, including ad hoc analysis and strategic initiatives.
Source, screen, and conduct due diligence on external public credit managers across strategies (e.g., investment grade, high yield, loans and structured credit), utilizing data platforms and AI-enabled tools to analyze performance, identify risks, and support manager screening and ongoing evaluation.
Lead and support the preparation of investment recommendations, including drafting investment memos and presentations for internal Investment Committee approval.
Assist in structuring and negotiating investment mandates, guidelines, and negotiating fee arrangements with external managers in collaboration with risk, legal and other internal teams.
Conduct ongoing monitoring of external managers, including performance attribution, risk exposures, style drift, and adherence to investment guidelines; leverage AI to enhance efficiency in analysis, identify performance and risk trends, and support the development of portfolio-level reporting and insights for senior management.
Lead or contribute to initiatives within Global Credit to enhance portfolio management infrastructure through the application of AI and the integration of new investment systems and analytics capabilities; partner with internal teams (Risk, Performance, Operations, Technology) to improve investment data quality to enable more effective analysis, reporting, and decision-making.
Support portfolio construction and strategic asset allocation across public credit, including contributing to capital allocation decisions across segments and managers, and shaping overall portfolio strategy.
Maintain a strong understanding of global public credit markets, including macroeconomic trends, interest rates, credit spreads, and technical factors, to inform manager selection and portfolio positioning.
Engage regularly with external managers through diligence meetings, portfolio reviews, and on-site visits to assess portfolio strategy, market outlook, and execution capabilities.
Support client and stakeholder reporting, including preparation of quarterly updates, market commentary, and materials for senior management and board-level discussions.
What do you need to succeed?

Advanced SQL skills, including complex queries, tables, views, stored procedures, query optimization, and performance tuning.
Proficiency in Python and PySpark for scalable data processing and automation.
Developed data warehouses with change data capture (CDC) and implemented dimensional data warehouses.

Strong communication, problem-solving, prioritization, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and business stakeholders in a hybrid environment.

description:
At IMCO, our talent is among the best! IMCO offers a uniquely stimulating and rewarding environment where you can help build and drive organizational transformation, all while seeking to challenge yourself, learn, and grow your career.

If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.
‎
We are looking for a highly motivated Principal to join our Client Relationship Management team!
IMCO’s Client Portfolio Management (CPM) Committee is a cross-functional forum with membership comprised of senior client-facing, investment and risk leaders. It is co-chaired by the Chief Investment Strategist and Chief Client Officer and enables discussion and alignment on significant investment strategy decisions that impact client portfolios.
The Principal, Client Portfolio Strategy and Governance will partner with IMCO’s client, investment, and risk teams to develop and advance strategic recommendations affecting portfolios and, where appropriate, participate in client discussions.
The role will help connect CPM’s internal investment work with client priorities by bringing client perspectives into committee discussions and supporting clear communication of portfolio implications, recommendations and trade-offs.
Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Portfolio Construction, this role will contribute to the investment decision making process by bringing investment expertise and judgment to shape portfolio themes, challenging submissions, translating investment team perspectives into decision-ready narratives, and ensuring that CPM discussions and decisions are anchored in client objectives, portfolio construction considerations, risks, trade-offs, and outcomes. The role also owns the forward-looking investment agenda and content for the CPM committee and is accountable for coordinating and advancing the development of integrated recommendations on strategic, investment and total portfolio matters within the committee’s mandate.
As a Member of Our Team You Will be Responsible For:
Client Portfolio Strategy and Recommendation Development
Partner with investment teams to identify the analysis and information required to support recommendations, interpret findings, and synthesize investment, risk, performance, portfolio construction, and client perspectives into clear implications for client portfolios.
Bring a client portfolio perspective to CPM discussions regarding strategic asset allocation (SAA) reviews, discretionary SAA matters, new investment strategies, material strategy changes, benchmarks, and other total portfolio matters within CPM’s mandate.
Partner with client-facing teams to understand evolving client objectives, constraints and governance considerations. Where appropriate, support or participate in client discussions on SAA, portfolio strategy and other material CPM matters, helping explain the investment rationale, portfolio implications, risks and trade-offs.
Ensure recommendations address client objectives, portfolio constraints, expected outcomes, implementation considerations, material risks, and trade offs.
Investment Content & Insights
Set standards for the quality of analysis and data used in CPM materials and ensure conclusions and recommendations are evidence-based, actionable, and aligned to client and portfolio objectives.
Shape complex portfolio topics into concise decision ready narratives that clearly articulate the issue, analysis, options, recommendations, key trade-offs, risks, client implications and implementation considerations, applying investment knowledge to strengthen the quality, coherence, and decision usefulness of content.
Partner with reporting, risk, and investment teams to improve the consistency, visual quality, and usability of CPM materials.
CPM Committee Leadership and Governance
Strengthen governance and elevate the quality of investment decision making, ensuring CPM discussions and outputs are rigorous, well-framed and anchored to client objectives and desired portfolio outcomes.
Lead and facilitate productive discussion among CPM members and subject matter experts, ensuring that key questions, differing perspectives, and trade offs are addressed.
Own the forward-looking CPM agenda, proactively identifying, curating, prioritizing, and sequencing items that require CPM discussion, alignment, or decision.
Maintain clear ownership of CPM outcomes, including decisions, rationale, implications, accountable owners and follow-through.
Continuously improve decision frameworks, templates, and ways of working to sharpen investment content, reduce cycle time, and improve the effectiveness of discussions.

Job Posting Description:
Database Administrator
This position is onsite #LI-Onsite
Are you an experienced Database Administrator looking to join a collaborative and supportive team that strives for operational excellence? Reporting to the Senior Manager, Infrastructure, you will be responsible for the administration, maintenance, security, performance, and support of LCBO’s enterprise database platforms across production and non-production environments.
In this role, you will support a broad and business-critical database landscape, including Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Db2, and other relational and non-relational technologies. You will help ensure database environments are stable, secure, recoverable, patched, and optimized to support critical business systems and transformation initiatives.
If you are a hands-on database professional who enjoys solving complex technical problems, supporting high-availability environments, and contributing to modernization and operational excellence, this is the role for you.
About the Role
Administer and support production and non-production database environments across multiple technologies, including Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Db2, and other relational and non-relational platforms.
Perform routine database maintenance, patching, upgrades, feature packs, and lifecycle activities to keep database platforms current, secure, and supportable.
Monitor database availability, capacity, performance, and overall health; proactively identify risks and implement corrective actions.
Tune database performance, including query optimization, indexing strategies, storage usage, and configuration improvements.
Manage database backup, restore, replication, recovery, and high-availability processes to meet business continuity, disaster recovery, RPO, and RTO requirements.
Support incident, problem, change, and release management processes in accordance with LCBO operational standards.
Collaborate with application, infrastructure, security, cloud, vendor, and project teams to provide reliable database support for business-critical systems.
Provide technical input and recommendations for new database implementations, migrations, upgrades, modernization initiatives, and cloud-based database services.
Implement and maintain database standards, operational procedures, technical documentation, runbooks, and logical and physical database diagrams.
Support database security, access management, privileged access controls, audit requirements, vulnerability remediation, and compliance with LCBO security practices.
Assist with license management and ensure database platform usage aligns with licensing and support requirements.
Develop or maintain automation scripts and repeatable processes to reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and increase operational efficiency.
Participate in rotational 24x7 on-call support for critical database platforms and production incidents.
About You
Required Skill
s
Bachelors' degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or an equivalent combination of education and business experience.

Knowledge of relational database concepts, database architecture, backup and recovery, high availability, replication, and disaster recovery practices.
Experience supporting databases across multiple operating systems, including Linux, UNIX, AIX, and Windows.
Experience with database patching, upgrades, monitoring, lifecycle planning, capacity management, and operational support.
Experience with database security, access management, privileged accounts, encryption, audit requirements, and compliance practices.

Experience deploying, configuring, or supporting databases in public, private, or hybrid cloud environments.
Exposure to cloud database services such as Azure SQL, Amazon Web Services RDS, Google Cloud SQL, or similar managed database platforms.
Experience with automation or scripting tools such as PowerShell, Python, Bash, Ansible, Terraform, or Jenkins.
Experience supporting database modernization, migration, consolidation, or platform transformation projects.
Experience with enterprise monitoring, observability, backup, recovery, and disaster recovery tools.

title: Coordonnateur des services cliniques /Clinical Services Coordinator
description:
À Santé Ontario nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Envie de donner un nouveau souffle à votre carrière?  Saisissez cette opportunité!
Relève de :
Gestionnaire, Centre de ressources provincial – Organes
Classification :
Coordonnateur des services cliniques (FT)
Lieu de travail :
Basé au 483, rue Bay
Horaire :
Combinaison de quarts de 12 heures en semaine et la fin de semaine
Le Réseau Trillium pour le don de vie (RTDV), qui fait partie de Santé Ontario, est responsable de la coordination du don et de la transplantation d'organes et de tissus en Ontario. Notre mandat comprend la sensibilisation du public à l'importance du don d'organes et de tissus, la formation des professionnels de la santé et l'assurance d'un système de don et de transplantation sûr et efficace en Ontario. En collaborant étroitement avec nos intervenants et en favorisant le développement organisationnel et individuel, nous accordons une grande importance à l'honnêteté, à la confiance, au respect et à la compassion.
Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d'un coordonnateur des services cliniques (CSC) permanent à temps plein hautement motivé et expérimenté. Le CSC fournira des services professionnels conformes à la mission et aux valeurs du RTDV. La personne retenue est passionnée par le don d'organes et de tissus et s'engage à atteindre trois objectifs fondamentaux :
1) permettre à chaque personne ou à son représentant légal de prendre une décision éclairée et en toute confiance concernant la possibilité du don; 2) veiller à ce que le processus de don soit une expérience significative et positive pour les proches du donneur ainsi que pour le personnel hospitalier et les autres intervenants; et
3) contribuer au maximum à l'obtention de résultats optimaux pour les patients recevant une greffe d'organe ou de tissu.
Ce poste offre une occasion unique de combiner les pratiques exemplaires et l'expertise clinique. À titre de ressource clé dans le domaine du don d'organes et de tissus, ce rôle offre une grande autonomie ainsi que l'occasion de collaborer et de créer des liens avec divers intervenants cliniques et non cliniques.
Nous offrons un programme complet d'orientation et de formation, ainsi qu'un soutien continu de l'équipe afin d'assurer votre réussite dans ce rôle, de même que des possibilités de perfectionnement pour votre carrière à long terme.
Voici ce que vous ferez :
Gérer les cas liés au processus de don, de l'orientation jusqu'au prélèvement d'organes
Travailler en collaboration avec les hôpitaux donneurs, les équipes de soins de santé, les programmes de transplantation, les banques de tissus, les transporteurs terrestres et aériens, les laboratoires et les autres membres du personnel du RTDV
Coordonner l'attribution des organes et les analyses nécessaires
Prendre des décisions critiques et veiller au respect des règlements de Santé Canada
Faciliter la logistique du prélèvement d'organes et organiser le transport de plusieurs équipes de prélèvement (chirurgiens, transport terrestre et aérien)
Répondre aux appels des hôpitaux référents, effectuer une évaluation préliminaire des antécédents du patient et déterminer toutes les options de don pertinentes
Collaborer avec l'équipe de soins de santé responsable afin d'élaborer des stratégies permettant d'intégrer les services du RTDV au plan de soins de fin de vie du patient et de sa famille
Fournir à l'équipe de soins de santé des recommandations initiales concernant la gestion du processus ou l'état physiologique du patient, selon le cas, jusqu'à l'intervention d'un Spécialiste, Don d'organes et de tissus
Consigner des notes de dossier complètes et exactes et saisir les renseignements clés dans le dossier électronique et la base de données personnalisée du RTDV
Agir à titre d'expert dans tous les aspects du don d'organes et de tissus
Promouvoir et soutenir les pratiques exemplaires en matière de don d'organes et de tissus
Travailler selon des quarts rotatifs de 12 heures dans un centre d'appels occupé fonctionnant 24 heures sur 24, 7 jours sur 7
Exécuter toute autre tâche requise
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Diplôme en sciences infirmières ou baccalauréat en sciences infirmières
Inscription à titre d'IA auprès de l'Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers de l'Ontario obligatoire
Minimum d'un (1) an d'expérience en soins infirmiers en milieu de soins critiques, de préférence
Expérience en don d'organes ou en soins infirmiers en transplantation, de préférence

Trillium Gift of Life Network (TGLN), part of Ontario Health, is responsible for the coordination of organ and tissue donation and transplantation in Ontario. Our mandate includes increasing public awareness of the importance of organ and tissue donation, education of health care professionals, and ensuring a safe and effective donation and transplant system in Ontario. Working collaboratively with our stakeholders and fostering organizational and individual growth, we value honesty, trust, respect and compassion.
We are currently seeking a highly motivated, experienced
permanent full time
Clinical Services Coordinator (CSC). The CSC will provide professional services in a manner consistent with the mission and values of TGLN. The incumbent is passionate about organ and tissue donation, and dedicated to achieving three core objectives, including:
1) enabling every person or legal surrogate to make an informed and confident decision about the option of donation 2) ensuring the process of donation is a meaningful, positive experience for the donor’s loved ones as well as for hospital staff and other stakeholders, and
3) contributing maximally to the attainment of optimal outcomes for patients receiving an organ or tissue transplant
This role offers the unique opportunity to blend best practice with clinical expertise. As a key resource in organ and tissue donation, this role provides a great deal of autonomy and the opportunity to liaise and network with a variety of clinical and non-clinical stakeholders.

Case management of the donation process from referral to organ recovery

Documents comprehensive and accurate case notes and enters key information into TGLN’s electronic chart and custom database

Promotes and supports organ and tissue donation best practices
Works 12-hour rotating shifts in a busy 24/7 call centre environment

The Position
Ontario Health is seeking an accomplished, astute, and highly strategic executive to serve as its next Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer. Reporting to the President and CEO and serving as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will provide enterprise leadership for Ontario Health communications, corporate and public affairs, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is a highly influential role at the intersection of government, health system transformation, and enterprise leadership. As a trusted advisor to the President and CEO, Board Chair, and senior leaders, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will help shape Ontario Health’s strategic positioning, reputation, and relationships with government and the health system.
A central priority will be maintaining strong relationships with Ministers’ offices, Ministry leadership, and other senior government decision makers. The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will bring executive judgment, anticipate emerging issues and sensitivities, and ensure Ontario Health remains closely aligned with government priorities and expectations.
The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will also position communications as a driver and enabler of the Ontario Health strategic agenda. Through proactive planning and a clear cadence of communications, they will help ensure Ontario Health has a compelling story to share about its priorities, progress, and impact, both within the organization and with external stakeholders. The Communications and Corporate Affairs portfolio includes internal and external communications, media and issues management, digital communications, brand and reputation, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is not simply a communications leadership role. It is an enterprise role for an executive who can navigate complexity, influence at the highest levels, and help advance Ontario Health’s mandate across government and the health system.

The ideal candidate is an accomplished senior executive with significant leadership experience in communications, corporate affairs, or public affairs within government, the broader public sector, health care, or another complex and highly visible environment.
They bring deep experience working with elected officials and their teams, senior public servants, Boards, CEOs, and executive teams. They are recognized for sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to anticipate issues, navigate complex government environments, and build trust with senior decision makers.
An exceptional communicator and relationship builder, they can translate complex issues into compelling messages, build trust across diverse stakeholders, and operate effectively within a Crown agency environment. They combine strategic thinking with sound judgment and pragmatism and bring breadth and versatility to contribute beyond the traditional boundaries of a communications portfolio.

Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Rattaché(e) au Président-Directeur général et membre de l'équipe de direction, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes assurera la direction stratégique des activités de Santé Ontario en matière de communication, d'affaires internes et d'affaires publiques, ainsi que de l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et de leurs familles.
Il s'agit d'un poste très influent, à la croisée des domaines de l'action publique, de la transformation du système de santé et de la direction stratégique des activités. En tant que conseiller de confiance du Président-directeur général, du président du conseil d’administration et des hauts dirigeants, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes contribuera à définir le positionnement stratégique de Santé Ontario, sa réputation et ses relations avec le gouvernement et le système de santé.
L'une des principales priorités consistera à entretenir des relations solides avec les cabinets des ministres, les responsables des ministères et les autres hauts responsables gouvernementaux. Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes fera preuve d'un jugement de haut niveau, anticipera les enjeux émergents et les sujets sensibles, et veillera à ce que Santé Ontario reste en parfaite adéquation avec les priorités et les attentes du gouvernement.
Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes aura également pour mission de faire de la communication un moteur et un catalyseur du programme stratégique de Santé Ontario. Le portefeuille du Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes comprend les communications internes et externes, les relations avec les médias et la gestion des enjeux, les communications numériques, la marque et la réputation, ainsi que l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et des familles.

Il est reconnu pour son bon jugement, sa discrétion et sa capacité à anticiper les problèmes, à évoluer dans des environnements administratifs complexes et à instaurer un climat de confiance avec les hauts responsables.
