This region spans major urban academic centres and regional hospitals to small rural providers, as well as a diverse network of community-based services. The CRO is a visible and trusted system leader, accountable for translating provincial priorities into action, advancing regional integration, and ensuring consistent, high-quality, and measurable results across a challenging and dynamic environment.
Internally, the CRO will work closely with Ontario Health’s senior leadership team to align people, resources, and strategy, building team cohesion, strengthening operational capacity, and fostering a culture of collaboration and high performance. Externally, the CRO will represent Ontario Health with health service providers, Ministry officials, community leaders, and political stakeholders, cultivating trust-based relationships and navigating complex issues with clarity and integrity.
The CRO will provide credible, solution-focused leadership to help providers navigate workforce shortages, financial pressures, and infrastructure challenges while maintaining alignment with provincial standards. They will strengthen integration and planning across sectors, using data, relationships, and funding levers to improve access, continuity, and efficiency of care. Accountable for delivering on provincial performance targets that directly affect patient care and system sustainability, the CRO will monitor progress, act on emerging issues, and ensure measurable results. In a politically complex environment, they will build strong, respectful relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, addressing sensitive matters with diplomacy and transparency. At the same time, they will lead long-term system transformation, ensuring that immediate operational successes lay the foundation for a forward-looking vision of regional health system improvement.
This is an exceptional opportunity to shape system performance and integration in a region that reflects the full diversity of Ontario’s health landscape. The incoming CRO will guide the regions through ongoing operational pressures, while keeping a clear focus on long-term transformation and equity.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished health system leader with senior-level experience in health care service delivery, operational and financial administration, performance management, and/or data analytics. Adept at navigating complex, multi-stakeholder environments, they bring strong political acumen and a proven ability to work effectively with government, service providers, boards, and community stakeholders. They possess deep knowledge of Ontario’s health sector, including funding models, policy directions, and transformation priorities, and are skilled at turning strategic vision into measurable results. A collaborative and values-driven leader, they build trust, foster alignment, and inspire teams toward shared goals. Resilient and grounded, they demonstrate sound judgment, thrive in complexity, and remain focused on improving care and equity for the people and communities of Ontario.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.
Ontario Health encourages applications from candidates who are First Nations, Métis, Inuit, and urban Indigenous; Francophone; members of Black and racialized groups; 2SLGBTQIA+ communities; trans and nonbinary individuals; and people living with disabilities.
Ontario Health is an accessible employer, and offers accommodation in all aspects of employment, including the recruitment process.
Directeur général régional de Toronto et de l'Est
Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Guidée par ses valeurs que sont
l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et la bienveillance
, Santé Ontario collabore avec des partenaires issus des hôpitaux, des services communautaires, de la santé mentale, des soins à domicile et d'autres secteurs afin d'améliorer les résultats et les expériences en matière de santé pour chaque Ontarien.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Relevant du président-directeur général, le directeur général régional (DGR) des régions de Toronto et de l'Est dirige l'un des portefeuilles les plus complexes et diversifiés de Santé Ontario. Cette région englobe aussi bien de grands centres universitaires urbains et des hôpitaux régionaux que de petits fournisseurs en milieu rural, ainsi qu'un réseau diversifié de services communautaires. Le DGR est un responsable reconnu et de confiance du système, chargé de traduire les priorités provinciales en actions, de faire progresser l'intégration régionale et de garantir des résultats cohérents, de haute qualité et mesurables dans un environnement difficile et dynamique.
En interne, le DGR travaillera en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de haute direction de Santé Ontario afin d'harmoniser les personnes, les ressources et la stratégie, de renforcer la cohésion de l'équipe et la capacité opérationnelle et de favoriser une culture de collaboration et de haute performance. En externe, le DGR représente Santé Ontario auprès des fournisseurs de services de santé, des représentants du ministère, des dirigeants communautaires et des intervenants politiques, en cultivant des relations fondées sur la confiance et en abordant des questions complexes avec clarté et intégrité.
Le DGR assure une direction crédible et axée sur les solutions afin d'aider les fournisseurs à faire face aux pénuries de main-d'œuvre, aux pressions financières et aux défis liés aux infrastructures, tout en maintenant la conformité aux normes provinciales. Il renforcera l'intégration et la planification entre les secteurs, en utilisant les données, les relations et les leviers de financement afin d'améliorer l'accès, la continuité et l'efficacité des soins. Responsable de la réalisation des objectifs de performance provinciaux qui influent directement sur les soins aux patients et la viabilité du système, le DGR suit les progrès accomplis, prend des mesures pour régler les problèmes émergents et veille à l'obtention de résultats mesurables. Dans un environnement politiquement complexe, il établit des relations solides et respectueuses avec un large éventail d'intervenants, tout en abordant les questions sensibles avec diplomatie et transparence. Parallèlement, il coordonne la transformation à long terme du système, en veillant à ce que les succès opérationnels immédiats jettent les bases d'une vision prospective de l'amélioration du système de santé régional.
Il s'agit d'une occasion exceptionnelle de façonner la performance et l'intégration du système dans une région qui reflète toute la diversité du paysage de la santé en Ontario. Le nouveau DGR guidera les régions face aux pressions opérationnelles continues, tout en maintenant clairement le cap sur la transformation à long terme et l'équité.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un responsable accompli du système de santé possédant une expérience de haut niveau dans la fourniture de services de soins de santé, l'administration opérationnelle et financière, la gestion du rendement et/ou l'analyse des données. Apte à évoluer dans des environnements complexes impliquant de multiples intervenants, il fait preuve d'un sens politique aigu et d'une capacité avérée à travailler efficacement avec les pouvoirs publics, les fournisseurs de services, les conseils d'administration et les intervenants communautaires. Il possède une connaissance approfondie du secteur de la santé de l'Ontario, notamment des modèles de financement, des orientations politiques et des priorités de transformation. Il est également capable de transformer la vision stratégique en résultats mesurables. En tant que responsable collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs, il instaure la confiance, favorise la coordination et motive les équipes à atteindre des objectifs communs. Résilient et pragmatique, il fait preuve d'un bon jugement, s'épanouit dans les situations complexes et reste concentré sur l'amélioration des soins et de l'équité pour la population et les communautés de l'Ontario.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
Santé Ontario encourage les candidatures de personnes issues des Premières Nations, des Métis, des Inuits et des Autochtones en milieu urbain; de francophones; de membres des communautés noires et racisées; de membres des communautés 2ELGBTQIA+; de personnes trans et non binaires; et de personnes en situation de handicap.

description:

At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care.
What Ontario Health offers:
At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:
Comprehensive health coverage from day one

A collaborative, values-driven workplace
where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion
, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity.
Regional Medical Director, Central & West Regions
Shape the Future of Health Care in Ontario
Ontario Health is building a more connected, equitable, and patient-centred health system. Achieving this vision requires exceptional clinical leaders who can bridge strategy and frontline care, inspire collaboration, and drive meaningful improvements for patients, providers, and communities.
As the Regional Medical Director, you’ll play an important role connecting health care networks to deliver quality care across a large geographic area.  Ontario Health Central and West are two of Ontario Health’s six geographic regions, collectively serving approximately 4.4 million people across diverse and growing urban and rural communities. Together, these regions span a vast geographic area, from Mississauga to Huntsville and Orangeville to Markham in Central, and from Waterloo to Windsor and Tobermory to Niagara Falls in West.
The Opportunity
As Regional Medical Director, you will provide clinical leadership across the Central & West Regions, ensuring clinical perspectives are embedded in decision-making, health system planning, and transformation initiatives. The Regional Medical Director is intended as a practicing physician who will work a minimum of 0.6FTE- 0.8FTE per week. This leader provides oversight of all Regional Clinical Leads (physicians) (~30+ physician leaders working 0.2FTE across 2 regions).
You will influence regional and provincial priorities, lead complex cross-sector initiatives, strengthen relationships across the health system, and champion innovative approaches that improve outcomes for patients and communities.
Success in this role will be defined by your ability to connect strategy with clinical practice, build alignment across diverse stakeholders, and deliver meaningful system-level improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Clinical Leadership
Provide clinical leadership aligned with Ontario Health's strategic goals and regional priorities.
Embed clinical expertise into health system planning, service design, resource optimization, and policy implementation.
Establish regional clinical priorities and measurable outcomes that support integrated care delivery.
Champion equitable, accessible, and culturally safe models of care that address the diverse needs of communities across the region.
Lead and mentor Regional Clinical Leads while fostering collaboration, accountability, and clinical excellence.
Health System Transformation
Partner with executive leaders to advance integrated clinical, operational, and strategic initiatives.
Provide expert clinical advice on emerging health system challenges, service pressures, workforce issues, and opportunities for innovation.
Lead complex cross-sector initiatives that improve access, quality, care coordination, and health system performance.
Collaborate with Ontario Health Teams, Health Service Providers, and provincial partners to advance sustainable models of integrated care.
Translate strategic priorities into actionable initiatives that deliver measurable system-wide impact.
Quality, Performance & Clinical Excellence
Advance evidence-informed practices, clinical standards, and quality improvement initiatives across the continuum of care.
Utilize clinical, operational, and performance data to identify opportunities, mitigate risks, and drive continuous improvement.
Promote shared accountability for patient outcomes, equitable access, and responsible stewardship of health system resources.
Partnership & Stakeholder Leadership
Build trusted relationships with physicians and physician leaders, Chiefs of Staff, health system leaders, Ontario Health Teams, and Health Service Providers.
Chair and lead regional clinical forums to strengthen alignment, collaboration, and accountability.
Represent regional clinical perspectives within provincial leadership discussions and advisory committees.
Foster meaningful engagement with clinicians, patients, families, Indigenous partners, and communities to ensure diverse perspectives inform health system priorities.
Advance a unified One Ontario Health approach through collaboration with provincial clinical and operational leaders.
The Leader We Are Seeking
You are a highly respected physician executive who combines clinical credibility with strategic vision, political acuity, and a demonstrated ability to influence across complex health systems.
You understand that meaningful transformation requires more than strategy. It requires trusted relationships, effective collaboration, disciplined execution, and the ability to bring diverse stakeholders together around common goals.
You are equally comfortable advising executives, engaging physicians and frontline clinicians, navigating complex system challenges, and translating ambitious priorities into practical action.
Most importantly, you are a collaborative leader who recognizes that lasting change is achieved through partnership, influence, and shared accountability.
Qualifications and Experience
Physician with a minimum of 10 years of clinical practice experience, in good standing and eligible to practise medicine without restriction in Ontario, with the intention of maintaining clinical practice while serving in this role.
Significant senior executive and/or clinical leadership experience within regional, provincial, or broader health system environments.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale transformation, clinical integration, and organizational change initiatives.
Proven ability to lead complex cross-sector partnerships that improve access, quality, care coordination, and health system performance.
Experience influencing outcomes within executive governance structures and highly matrixed environments where collaboration and consensus-building are critical.
Strong understanding of Ontario's health care system, population health priorities, health policy environment, and emerging sector challenges.
Experience across multiple care sectors, including hospitals, primary care, community care, long-term care and/or public health, is considered an asset.
Master's degree in Health Administration, Public Administration, Health Planning, Business Administration, or a related field is considered an asset.
Why Join Ontario Health?
Few clinical leadership opportunities offer the ability to influence health care at this scale.
As Pan-Regional Medical Director, you will help shape regional and provincial priorities, strengthen partnerships across the health system, and advance innovative solutions that improve health outcomes for millions of Ontarians.
If you are a visionary physician leader who thrives at the intersection of clinical excellence, health system planning and implementation and transformational change, we invite you to bring your leadership and expertise to Ontario Health and help shape the future of health care in Ontario.

title: Manager, Planning and Implementation
description:
Responsable de la planification et de la mise en œuvre
À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Ce que Santé Ontario offre:
Chez Santé Ontario, votre croissance et votre bien-être ne sont pas seulement soutenus, ils sont célébrés à chaque étape. Ici, vous avez l'opportunité d'avoir un impact significatif tout en construisant une carrière épanouissante et durable. En fonction du poste que vous occupez, vous pourriez avoir droit
Une couverture santé complète dès le premier jour,
avec des prestations médicales, dentaires et optiques entièrement prises en charge pour vous et votre famille
Des comptes de dépenses flexibles pour les soins de santé ou le bien-être,
ainsi qu'un programme inclusif pour soutenir votre bien-être.
Un régime de retraite préférentiel à prestations déterminées,
assurant une sécurité financière à long terme
Un droit à des congés compétitifs
qui donnent le temps de se ressourcer
Trois jours personnels et deux jours flottants par an
, offrant ainsi une flexibilité favorisant l'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle, en plus des jours de congés
Des opportunités de formation continue et de développement de carrière
conçues pour vous aider à progresser, à évoluer et à vous épanouir dans votre profession.
Un environnement de travail collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs,
où l'intégrité, la bienveillance, l'humilité, l'inspiration et la ténacité façonnent tout ce que nous faisons.
Des possibilités de participer à des communautés inclusives –
favorisant le sentiment d’appartenance, l’équité et le partage de perspectives diverses au sein de notre équipe
Voulez-vous faire la différence dans votre carrière?  Examinez l'opportunité qui s'offre à vous.
Le Responsable de la planification et de la mise en œuvre joue un rôle clé de direction dans la promotion d'une planification intégrée et axée sur la communauté du système de santé dans toute la région Est de Santé Ontario. En étroite collaboration avec le Directeur de la planification et de la mise en œuvre, le titulaire de ce poste contribue à définir, mettre en œuvre et évaluer les stratégies régionales visant à améliorer l'accès, l'équité, les résultats et l'expérience des communautés que nous servons.
Il s'agit d'une opportunité pour un dirigeant doté d'un esprit de collaboration et d'une approche systémique de piloter des initiatives de planification, de nouer des partenariats solides et de soutenir la mise en œuvre de programmes prioritaires en adéquation avec les objectifs provinciaux et régionaux.
Ce rôle régional vise à répondre aux besoins et priorités spécifiques de la région Est de Santé Ontario.
Voici ce que vous aurez à faire :
Diriger et soutenir la planification, la conception, la mise en œuvre et l'évaluation, à l'échelle régionale, des initiatives visant à promouvoir l'équité en matière de santé, à soutenir les populations prioritaires, à favoriser l'intégration, à renforcer l'engagement et à répondre aux autres priorités de la région Est.
Mettre en place des structures, des processus et des mesures de performance au niveau régional afin de faciliter la mise en œuvre, le suivi, l'établissement de rapports et l'amélioration continue.
Établir et entretenir des relations solides avec les partenaires internes et externes afin d'identifier les obstacles, les lacunes et les possibilités d'amélioration du système.
Mettre à profit la connaissance du système et les partenariats pour soutenir des programmes novateurs et intégrés qui aident les communautés à accéder aux soins et aux services appropriés au moment où elles en ont besoin.
Promouvoir la prise de décisions fondée sur des données probantes, les principes d’équité en santé et l’harmonisation avec les stratégies provinciales et régionales.
Représenter la région au sein des instances locales, régionales et provinciales compétentes afin de contribuer à la planification, à la coordination, à la mise en place de bonnes pratiques et à la définition des priorités en matière de financement.
Assurer le leadership, l'encadrement et la gestion quotidienne du personnel et des domaines de programme assignés, en veillant à leur conformité avec les meilleures pratiques, normes, directives, politiques et procédures acceptées.
Suivre, évaluer et rendre compte des activités régionales, en utilisant les données et les analyses pour appuyer la planification, l'amélioration des performances et la réalisation des objectifs stratégiques.
Se tenir informé des enjeux actuels du système de santé et des initiatives de changement liées aux priorités de la planification annuelle des activités et aux principaux domaines de résultats.
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Une licence en gestion de la santé, en administration publique ou dans un domaine connexe, assortie d'une expérience pertinente, est obligatoire; un master est préférable.
Sept années d'expérience progressive dans le domaine de la santé sont requises; une expérience axée sur l'équité en santé est préférable.
Une solide expérience dans la gestion d'équipe, la supervision des activités opérationnelles quotidiennes et l'alignement du travail sur les objectifs généraux de l'entreprise.
Une solide expérience dans l'intégration de projets d'envergure et complexes dans un environnement en constante évolution, avec une expertise en matière de mise en œuvre opérationnelle et de programmes.
Un sens profond des affaires, avec la capacité de mobiliser les principaux partenaires du système dans la réalisation des activités opérationnelles et des programmes; une expérience clinique est un atout.
Une expérience avérée dans l'établissement et le maintien de relations et de partenariats au sein du secteur de la santé et du gouvernement provincial, en mettant l'accent sur l'intégration des systèmes et la promotion de changements à l'échelle du système.
Des capacités de leadership exceptionnelles, notamment en matière de créativité, d'innovation, d'intégrité, d'initiative et de passion.
La capacité à travailler de manière autonome, à assumer la responsabilité de ses actions et à s'aligner sur la vision et les orientations de la direction.
La capacité à préparer et à présenter des exposés sur des informations techniques et/ou sensibles à des publics divers.
La capacité à gérer plusieurs projets simultanément, appuyée par des compétences avancées en gestion de projet.
La capacité à faire preuve de discernement sur des questions sensibles et controversées et à négocier un consensus autour de stratégies politiques complexes.
D’excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite, avec la capacité de fournir et d'obtenir des informations complexes, techniques ou sensibles de manière claire, concise, logique et dans un format adapté au public.
La maîtrise de la langue française est un atout.
Connaissances et compétences
Un sens des affaires et réflexion systémique, ainsi que la capacité à mettre en œuvre les principes de gestion financière, de gestion des ressources humaines, de dynamique organisationnelle et de gouvernance, de planification stratégique, de gestion des risques et d'amélioration de la qualité dans le secteur de la santé.
Une capacité à mobiliser les intervenants, à gérer les relations et à faire preuve de finesse politique, avec l'aptitude à développer des réseaux, à nouer des alliances, à collaborer au-delà des frontières et à entretenir des relations internes et externes qui soutiennent la performance du département et les initiatives communes.
Des compétences en communication, relations interpersonnelles et travail d'équipe, notamment l'écoute active, une communication claire et concise, le tact, la compassion, la sensibilité et le respect des besoins et des capacités des autres.
Des compétences en gestion des risques et en mesure de la performance, notamment la capacité à mesurer et à évaluer les résultats, à ajuster la direction en conséquence et à soutenir le dialogue et l'analyse grâce aux informations sur la performance organisationnelle.
Des compétences en matière de planification stratégique et de gestion du changement, associées à la capacité de communiquer les objectifs de l'entreprise, d'harmoniser les tâches et les objectifs du service, de définir des cibles et des indicateurs clairs, et d'accompagner les collaborateurs dans les efforts de changement et les initiatives visant à améliorer les performances du service.
Des connaissances en matière de conception de systèmes, de planification des soins de santé et d'élaboration de programmes, notamment la capacité à rechercher des idées, des bonnes pratiques et des tendances; à comprendre le système et l'environnement des soins de santé; et à planifier, mettre en œuvre et évaluer des politiques et/ou des programmes de santé.
Une capacité à développer de nouvelles perspectives, à mettre en œuvre des solutions innovantes, à favoriser la pensée créative et l'innovation, ainsi qu'à concevoir et mettre en œuvre des programmes ou des processus nouveaux ou de pointe.
Une connaissance du secteur de la santé en Ontario, des tendances relatives à la main-d'œuvre dans ce secteur, des enjeux, priorités et besoins locaux en matière de santé, ainsi que des grandes tendances en matière de politique de santé et de développement du système de santé.
Une connaissance et une compréhension du secteur associatif et des programmes qui y sont liés, notamment, mais sans s'y limiter, la santé mentale, les dépendances et la santé liée à la consommation de substances, ainsi que l'intégration au sein du système de santé.
Une connaissance des besoins des populations autochtones urbaines et communautaires ainsi que des communautés francophones.
Une connaissance approfondie des modèles et approches de planification.

Région Est, Ontario

Permanent à temps plein

7

24 octobre 2026

The Manager, Planning and Implementation plays a key leadership role in advancing integrated, community-based health system planning across Ontario Health’s East Region. Working closely with the Director, Planning and Implementation, this role helps shape, implement and evaluate regional strategies that improve access, equity, outcomes and experiences for the communities we serve.
This is an opportunity for a collaborative, systems-focused leader to guide planning initiatives, build strong partnerships and support implementation of priority programs aligned with provincial and regional goals.
This regional role is focused on addressing the distinct needs and priorities of Ontario Health’s East Region.
Here is what you will be doing:
Lead and support regional planning, design, implementation and evaluation of initiatives that advance health equity, priority populations, integrations, engagement and other East Region priorities.
Develop regional structures, processes and performance measures to support implementation, monitoring, reporting and continuous improvement.
Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external partners to identify system barriers, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
Leverage system knowledge and partnerships to support innovative, integrated programs that help communities access the right care and services when they need them.
Promote evidence-informed decision-making, health equity principles and alignment with provincial and regional strategies.
Represent the region at appropriate local, regional and provincial tables to inform planning, coordination, best practices and funding priorities.
Provide leadership, guidance and day-to-day management to staff and assigned program areas, ensuring alignment with accepted best practices, standards, directives, policies and procedures.
Monitor, evaluate and report on regional activities, using data and analysis to support planning, performance improvement and achievement of strategic objectives.
Maintain awareness of current health system issues and change initiatives related to annual business planning priorities and key result areas.
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in health administration, public administration or a related field with relevant experience is required; Master’s degree is preferred.
7 years of progressive healthcare experience is required; experience with a health equity focus is preferred.

title: Senior Legal Counsel
description:
Business Unit
Regular, Full time
Closing Date: November 2, 2026
The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The
Corporate Finance Department
is a regulatory department responsible for oversight of issuers (other than investment funds) in the public and exempt markets. The department reviews public distributions of securities, exempt market activities and continuous disclosure of reporting issuers, and leads issuer-related policy initiatives. The department is also responsible for supervising insider reporting, regulating designated rating organizations, oversight of benchmarks and benchmark administrators and overseeing the listed issuer function for OSC recognized exchanges.
As a
Senior Legal Counsel
, you will work on a multi-disciplinary team and will be given opportunities to:
Review prospectus offerings, exempt market activities, and continuous disclosure filings by public issuers;
Consider applications for discretionary relief from securities legislation;
Consult and engage with issuers, their advisors and other market participants;
Lead the development of significant policy initiatives that impact issuers at both the Ontario and national levels; and
Provide advice and recommendations regarding complex and novel products and issues.
Responsibilities:
Conduct analysis and provide strategic legal advice and subject matter expertise on securities law, capital markets regulation, prospectus offerings, exemptive relief applications, exempt market regulation and a range of emerging regulatory issues.
Independently assess complex prospectus filings and novel products, resolve novel legal and policy issues, and make recommendations on whether regulatory approvals meet the applicable legislative test.
Lead exemptive relief applications, negotiate outcomes with Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) counterparts and market participants, and develop recommendations on complex policy matters.
Lead complex and high-impact policy, regulatory, and legislative initiatives, including drafting securities law instruments and collaborating with CSA, government, and industry stakeholders.
Represent the OSC on CSA and industry committees, contributing to regulatory policy development and identifying solutions to evolving market and regulatory challenges.
Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders, providing guidance on securities law interpretation, transaction structures, and regulatory requirements.
Build consensus and negotiate effectively with regulators, issuers, advisors, and industry participants to address complex legal, policy, and market issues.
Monitor market developments and emerging trends, assessing regulatory implications and recommending innovative, practical solutions that support investor protection and efficient capital markets.
Qualifications:
We are looking for candidates with inquiring minds and a passion for the capital markets who value a collegial environment. Candidates must be members in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario.
Preference will be given to candidates who meet all of the following criteria:
A minimum of 8 years of relevant legal, transactional and regulatory experience;
An in-depth understanding of the Canadian securities regulatory environment;
Experience with the securities regulatory regime as it applies to reporting issuers and issuers raising capital in the exempt market;
Strong analytical, project management and communication skills and the ability to set and adjust priorities;
Excellent legal drafting skills, including experience drafting legislation, rules or other regulatory instruments;
A demonstrated ability to establish collaborative working relationships and engage with internal and external stakeholders; and
Demonstrated judgment and proficiency to balance regulatory objectives with practical business considerations.

At the OSC, we're leveraging technology, data, and modern product practices to transform how regulation is delivered and experienced. The Product Office – Regulatory Platforms is responsible for shaping, delivering, and evolving the core technology products that enable the OSC's regulatory functions. We take a product-centric approach, bringing together business expertise, technology, user experience, and data to deliver solutions that create measurable value.
Our team partners closely with regulatory business units, product managers, architects, developers, and operational teams to modernize critical platforms, improve user experiences, and enable organizational transformation. perform business analysis for projects that involve a higher degree of complexity

University education in Information Sciences, Business Administration or equivalent combination of education and experience and experience working with or knowledge of Business Analysis methodology (IIBA or PMI) and application of tools and techniques.
3 to 5 years of professional experience as a Business Analyst within financial services industry
Ability to evaluate business environment(s), interpret requirements, conceptualize and develop recommendations to enable stakeholder-acceptable business processes.
Well-developed problem-solving and analytical skills to research and identify issues, challenges, root causes and opportunities, and to propose effective solutions for improvement.
Excellent oral and written communication skills to provide advice and guidance and present information clearly and concisely to all levels within the organization, including executives.
Strong client focus including excellent interpersonal and client relationship management skills to build strong relationships with client groups to facilitate, consult and negotiate with internal stakeholders and peers.

title: Business and Market Data Analyst
description:
Business Unit
Regular, Full time
Closing Date: October 23, 2026
The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The
Investment Management Division
oversees the regulation of investment funds and structured products that offer securities to the public in Ontario. Our function in the OSC’s mandate of providing investors protection is a vital one. We have a leadership role in developing new rules and policies within the OSC and within the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) to adapt to the changing environment in the investment fund and structured products industry. Our scope of activity includes reviewing and considering investor protection issues related to the offerings of investment products (including mutual funds, exchange traded funds, structured products, scholarship plans and labour-sponsored funds); assessing product disclosure, including prospectus and continuous disclosure filings; and considering applications for discretionary relief from Ontario securities legislation and rules.
The
Business and Market Data Analyst
position will involve playing a key role in profiling the activities of the Investment Management Division by reporting on the success and impact of Division initiatives and core work processes. The Divisions core processes include rule and policy consultation, prospectus and exemptive relief application reviews and issue-oriented reviews of important regulatory development. The Business and Market Data Analyst’s primary function will be to support the Division’s core processes by conducting research, collecting and interpreting market data and activities and supporting special policy projects the Division undertakes (i.e. Risk Methodologies, and Regulatory burden-reduction initiatives).
Reporting to the Manager, Analytics, the
Business and Market Data Analyst
will be instrumental in developing, maintaining and analyzing key financial data to measure, and report on, internally and for publication (i.e. quarterly and annual reports).
Key Duties and Responsibilities:
Market Research for Division Core Processes
Provide research, including conducting background research on topics relating to investment activities in the funds industry, novel investment products, capital market development, and investor protection concerns, as requested.
With division staff identify, plan and conduct qualitative and quantitative market research to inform on mutual funds industry trends which impact on core Division processes and decisions, including prospectus, application and continuous disclosure reviews.
Conduct analysis of investment products’ attributes and risks using internally developed analytical datasets and frameworks.
Monitor, assess and interpret trends in the investment funds and structured products markets, both in Canada and globally, and prepare and design requirements on these trends.
Proactively identify additional market data and information to collect, maintain and analyze which is conducive to the efficient and effective operation of Investment Management Division.
Identify problems whereby efficiencies can be achieved, research and evaluate various alternatives and proceed with the most efficient solution.
Assess data quality, completeness, and limitations, and document analytical assumptions and methodologies. Present research findings to the Division management team, senior staff, policy project leads and/or committees (i.e. CSA) and address questions and/or defend analysis.
Data Collection, Preparation and Analysis
Work with other divisions to identify, evaluate, access, organize, clean, validate, and maintain internal and external data sources required to support Division research, analysis, and reporting.
Maintain analytical datasets and models to support market monitoring, operational oversight, and risk‑based analysis.
With division staff interpret information related to Division operations, analyze market data, and present and report issues, findings and trends that impact on the work of the Division.
Reporting, Dashboards, and Performance Measurement
Develop, maintain dashboards and report, using Division-wide operational performance measures, to better reflect how the Division is meeting its mandate (i.e. for use in quarterly reports).
Analyze trends, anomalies, and emerging risks in market and operational data and surface issues that may require supervisory, policy, or operational action.
Enterprise Systems and Data Access
Leverage enterprise systems and platforms to extract and use data required for Division analysis and reporting.
Coordinate with enterprise system and digital teams as required to ensure appropriate data access and alignment with organizational standards.
Skills & Qualifications:
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to collect, organize, and translate data into clear insights.
Knowledge of financial markets and investment products, including mutual funds and ETFs, with the ability to analyze market trends and interpret data.
Excellent presentation, problem-solving and strategic thinking skills.
Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated tact and sensitivity when negotiating with diverse parties.
Ability to interact professionally with management and professionals at various levels.
Demonstrated ability to respond to ad hoc unstructured problems with planning, flexibility, communication and execution.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research and prepare dashboards.
Ability to work with minimal direction and prioritize and meet strict deadlines.
Knowledge or experience in the securities industry.
Understanding of investment funds regulation and funds’ operations.

University degree in Business, Finance or a related discipline.
Experience working with data analysis and visualization skills with, data science tools such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, Python and SQL for data preparation, automation and analytical initiatives.
A minimum of 3-5 years of intermediate-level experience in the financial and/or regulatory sector, performing a similar function. Equivalent combinations of education, experience, and demonstrated competencies will be considered.

Basic knowledge of the Ontario Securities Act, regulations, policy statements, rules and internal operating procedures.
High proficiency in the MS Office suite of products.

title: Senior Forensic Accountant
description:
Business Unit
Fixed Term (Fixed Term), Full time
Closing Date: October 23, 2026
The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
Senior Forensic Accountant
Enforcement Division
18-month Contract
The
Enforcement Division
of the Ontario Securities Commission delivers fair, vigorous, and timely enforcement responses to capital markets misconduct. The Enforcement Division investigates and litigates breaches of securities laws in Ontario.  Team members work closely with other securities regulators, self-regulatory organizations and law-enforcement agencies to enhance initiatives to fight misconduct.  A strong visible enforcement presence assists in protecting investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, fosters fair, efficient and competitive capital markets, fosters capital formation, and contributes to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk.
The Enforcement Division is recruiting a
Senior Forensic Accountant
(18-month Contract) to support the investigation of criminal activity with a focus on fraudulent and recidivist behaviour that harms retail investors. The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing the Division's efforts to bring more Enforcement cases before the courts, where offenders may face significant penalties, including jail terms.
What’s in it for you?
Be an integral part of a leading-edge team leveraging an innovative mix of traditional investigative techniques, data analytics, and open-source intelligence analysis to investigate and assist in the prosecution of complex cases of Securities Act and Criminal Code offences.
Work in a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.
Make a difference and have a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets.
What will you do?
Participate in complex financial investigations from intake through conclusion, including assessing referrals, identifying investigative objectives, and developing investigative strategies that evolve as the case progresses.
Lead or participate in multi-disciplinary investigation teams, establish priorities, coordinate investigative activities, and drive the timely progression of investigative files.
Direct the forensic accounting aspects of investigations in collaboration with investigators, litigators, and external law enforcement partners.
Collect, review, and analyze complex financial and non-financial evidence, including banking records, accounting records, corporate documents, digital evidence, and witness testimony, in accordance with investigative and evidentiary best practices.

Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: HR Operational Services

The Role:
The Compensation and Benefits Specialist provides expert analysis, advice, and operational support for PHO's compensation and benefits programs. The role is responsible for compensation administration, salary structure management, job evaluation, pay equity, benefits program oversight, market research, cost analysis, reporting, and continuous improvement. Leveraging organizational data, market intelligence, and industry best practices, the Specialist develops recommendations, business cases, and strategic advice to support compensation programs and organizational decision-making. The role serves as a key resource to leaders, managers, employees, and HR partners, and helps ensure compensation and benefits programs are competitive, sustainable, and aligned with legislative requirements, collective agreements, policies, and established practices.
Key Responsibilities -
Lead the annual compensation cycle, including merit increases, validation or approved of wage adjustments, and related implementation activities.
Administer salary structures and compensation programs in accordance with legislation, collective agreements, policies and approved practices.
Establishes and leverages relationships with external compensation partners, industry peers, and professional networks to obtain market insights, identify emerging trends, and support evidence-based compensation program design and decision-making.
Lead job evaluation for new and revised positions using the applicable methodology; document recommendations and support internal consistency and a defensible pay structure.
Maintain and support PHO’s pay equity program and related compliance requirements.
Provide data-driven advice on compensation matters and support the analysis and resolution of complex issues, including matters that may contribute to grievances.
Administer and support benefit program activities, including annual enrolment, plan changes, monthly remittances, escalated eligibility or coverage issues and employee appeals within the role’s scope.
Monitor benefit plan performance, cost, utilization, service quality and emerging market practices; identify risks and opportunities for improvement.
Monitor vendor performance against established service expectations and metrics and work with vendors and internal partners to resolve issues.
Support vendor reviews, procurement activities and implementation of approved benefit program changes.
Respond to or coordinate pension-related inquiries with the appropriate plan administrator and direct employees to the correct source for pension transactions, estimates or retirement advice.
Assess, interpret and provide guidance on compensation and benefits provisions in legislation, collective agreements, policies, procedures and plan documents.
Partner with HR Business Partners, HR leadership, managers and employees to provide clear, consistent and practical advice within the position’s area of responsibility.
Assess the impact of new legislation, collective agreements and approved program changes; develop and coordinate implementation plans to meet organizational obligations.
Recommend and implement improvements to compensation and benefits policies, programs, processes, templates and guidance tools to improve service and reduce organizational risk.
Maintain current knowledge of relevant legislation, regulations and industry practices.
Develop and prepare compensation and benefits reports, corporate statistics, costing and detailed analysis and scenario planning to support decision-making.
Use the HRIS and other tools to monitor data, validate approved position and employee information, investigate anomalies and support accurate reporting.
Partner with the HR Systems Advisor on system testing, implementation, maintenance, reporting and data integrity relating to compensation and benefits.
Liaise with Payroll on compensation and benefits matters to support accurate and timely pay and deductions.
Identify opportunities to improve or automate work through data, technology and streamlined processes.
Coordinate or lead special assigned HR projects and initiatives within the role’s scope, ensuring deliverables and timelines are met.
Develop clear communications, briefing notes, reports, tools and guidance materials for compensation and benefits programs and changes.
Deliver information sessions and explain complex requirements in language appropriate for employees, managers, senior leaders and HR colleagues.
Maintain effective working relationships with internal partners, benefit carriers, consultants, pension plan administrators, vendors and industry contacts.
Escalate material risks, exceptions and complex issues to the Manager, People Experience or other decision-makers, with analysis and recommended options.
Knowledge and Skills-
Working knowledge of legislation and regulatory requirements relevant to compensation and benefits.
Strong analytical and financial acumen, with the ability to interpret data, identify issues and provide practical recommendations.
Advanced proficiency with HRIS, reporting tools, spreadsheets, databases and word processing applications; ability to improve and automate processes using technology.
Excellent written and verbal communication, consultation, negotiation and customer service skills, including tact and diplomacy when handling complex or sensitive matters.
Ability to work independently, set priorities and manage multiple responsibilities and fixed deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
High attention to detail and sound judgment when working with confidential and sensitive information
Knowledge of artificial intelligence tools and emerging technologies, including the ability to use AI responsibly to support analysis, reporting, process improvement and service delivery.
Education and Experience-
Undergraduate degree in business, human resources or a related field, plus an accredited human resources program and at least seven years of related experience in a unionized environment, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) or in progress.
CHRP designation preferred
Advanced knowledge of compensation and benefits program design and administration, job evaluation, salary structures, market analysis, pay equity and collective agreement application.
Attributes and Competencies-
Provides authoritative advice and recommendations on compensation, benefits, job evaluation and related HR programs, often involving sensitive, complex or contentious issues.
Develops and delivers reports, presentations, briefing notes, communications materials, procedures and guidance documents used to support employee understanding and management decision-making.
Uses tact, diplomacy and influencing skills when communicating decisions, explaining program requirements, addressing concerns or resolving disputes where there may be disagreement or competing interests.
Builds and maintains productive working relationships with internal stakeholders, Payroll, HR Systems, benefits carriers, pension administrators, consultants and other external partners to facilitate effective service delivery.
Provides responsive, high-quality service by assessing client needs, researching issues and delivering accurate information, recommendations and solutions.
Ensures compensation and benefits programs are administered consistently, fairly and in accordance with legislation, policies, plan provisions and collective agreements.
Analyzes issues of varying complexity using legislation, collective agreements, policies, precedents, plan documents, market information and HRIS data.
Determines when an issue can be resolved within established authority and when options or recommendations must be escalated for decision.
Identifies and prioritizes time-sensitive compensation and benefits activities, anticipates data or process issues and initiates corrective action.
Provides subject matter expertise and practical guidance to HR colleagues, managers and senior leaders.

Location: PHO Corporate Office & Toronto Laboratory, 661 University Avenue, Toronto, ON

The Role:
To perform highly specialized and complex laboratory testing, within the Public Health Laboratory, to support research, method development and surveillance under the direction of a principal investigator (e.g. molecular specialist, medical microbiologist, or clinical microbiologist). To perform and evaluate protocols and conduct, under the direction of a principal investigator, research projects, sophisticated analyses and methods evaluations.
Key Responsibilties
Performs highly specialized and complex laboratory testing to respond to potential public health threats from emerging pathogens, protect public health and safety, and to support disease diagnosis, prevention and treatment and other organism of public health importance.
Performs tests and provides input to principal investigators on highly specialized and complex laboratory testing and equipment.
Under the direction of a principal investigator (e.g. molecular specialist) recommends changes to formalized procedures and new protocols for diagnostic laboratory testing of emerging pathogens. Assesses proposed laboratory procedures and reports on findings to a PI for consideration in the improvement of laboratory practices and protocols.
Under the direction of a principal investigator participates in research and development as part of the process in establishing new protocols where none exists. Assesses proposed and existing laboratory procedures and reports on findings to a molecular specialist for further action. Prepares SOPs for research and drafts SOPs for methods being adapted in the clinical laboratory. Conducts, under direction, research projects pertaining to the establishment and implementation of new protocols and procedures, sophisticated analyses and methods evaluations for the improvement of laboratory procedures, protocols and surveillance.
Provides technical support to medical laboratory technologists in performing new procedures that apply to new techniques and protocols which supports the implementation of more effective techniques and new test technology.
Under direction conducts collaborative research projects which may involve provincial/national/ international organizations and universities, to evaluate and establish improved methodologies to enhance PHL testing service. Provides technical support on projects for medical laboratory technologists and laboratory assistants in the diagnostic laboratory, sharing their knowledge and expertise of new methodologies and practices.
Maintains quality control for own research projects.
Maintains the efficient operation of their assigned research laboratory area including maintenance of equipment and ordering of supplies.
Perform evaluations and validation studies of assays and assist with the implementation of new tests or methods in the laboratory in consultation with the PI.

Lead and be accountable for Cost Control activities and deliverables across assigned capital projects, performing the work directly on some projects and overseeing Specialists and consultants supporting delivery on others.
Direct and review the work of Cost Control Specialists/ consultants, providing guidance, resolving issues and coordinating with stakeholders to obtain and validate the information required for Cost Control deliverables.
Guide project delivery teams in the identification and appropriate cost treatment of risks, issues, claims and changes through the change management process, considering the applicable project delivery model and contractual framework.
Facilitate the change control process throughout the project lifecycle, including the identification, assessment, tracking and reporting of approved and potential changes and their impact on project forecasts and contingency.
Develop and maintain project Estimates at Completion (EAC) monthly across assigned projects, coordinating and challenging project team inputs and assessing the cost impact of changes, issues, claims and other known or potential cost impacts in accordance with the applicable project delivery model and contractual framework, to ensure they are appropriately reflected in the forecast.
Ensure the quality and consistency of Cost Control deliverables across assigned projects and work with project teams to identify opportunities to improve the accuracy, completeness and reliability of EAC forecasts and other Cost Control outputs.
Deliver Cost Control training and guidance on IO’s Cost Management framework, processes and requirements, including the relationship between Cost Control, change control and contingency management.
Develop and implement Cost Control and Change Management Plans and contribute to the development and continuous improvement of Cost Management procedures, guidelines, standards and tools.
Implement and oversee the application of IO’s Cost Management framework, processes and requirements across assigned projects, including work delivered by consultants, ensuring consistent application while adapting to project stage, delivery model and project-specific requirements.
Develop and analyze Cost Control metrics and reporting related to project cost performance, EAC, changes, contingency utilization and other key Cost Control indicators to identify trends and support project and portfolio decision-making.
Support the project contingency management process, including assessing and tracking contingency utilization, supporting contingency drawdowns and associated budget transfers, and ensuring approved movements are appropriately reflected in Cost Control reporting.
Work collaboratively with rest of Cost Management disciplines to provide integrated oversight across the project lifecycle, ensuring appropriate alignment and continuity between project budgets, estimates, Cost Control information and forecasts as projects progress through each stage.
Collaborate with Finance, Budgeting and other stakeholders to align project Cost Control information and reporting with financial, budgeting and organizational requirements.

title: Capacity Program Advisor, Office of the Executive Director (Hybrid, Permanent)
description:
Overview
At Law Society of Ontario we believe in the importance of a collaborative and supportive work environment that provides high quality and professional service to the public, lawyers and paralegals, and other stakeholders.
We are always on the lookout for exceptional individuals who are ready to make a meaningful impact, innovate and grow with us.  Our offering:
We value each member of our team and invest in your professional learning and development.
We provide access to the resources needed to support professional growth, mental health and well-being is a priority.
Our competitive compensation package includes a defined contribution pension plan, health and dental benefits plan and a robust Employee and Family Assistance Plan (EFAP).
Our progressive employment policies, high levels of employee engagement and the impressive architecture and beautiful grounds of the historic Osgoode Hall, there are many reasons to work at the Law Society.
We hope you will consider joining the Law Society!
Job Purpose
The Capacity Program Advisor, is responsible for the oversight and implementation of processes, policies, outreach, communication, support and education programs in keeping with the Law Society’s public interest mandate, legislation, by-laws and policies, specifically with respect to licensee health issues, and assessment of incapacity (as defined by the
Law Society Act
). The Capacity Program Advisor serves as an information and strategic resource on licensee health to Professional Regulation. Promotes an assistive, collaborative approach to dealing with licensee health related issues to produce appropriate outcomes in a diverse number of cases.
Qualifications
Minimum of an advanced degree in Health Sciences or a related field of study or an LLB or JD with membership in good standing with the Law Society.
Minimum, 7 years’ experience or equivalent in mental health services or a health regulatory environment. At least two of these years should be in a project management and/or leadership capacity, directing the development and implementation of process improvements in a regulatory/adjudicative environment, and leading change management initiatives.
In depth understanding of the Law Society’s mandate, services, legislation and policies
In depth understanding, and continued research and analysis in legally complex matters
Has current knowledge of related health resources and programs in the community
Demonstrated knowledge base regarding health issues affecting professionals, particularly substance use disorders, mental health disorders and dementias.
Microsoft Office Suite / 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
Broad understanding of technology, particularly applications of technical solutions to work process and procedure in a regulatory / legal environment.
Thorough knowledge of project management principles and best practices, including group dynamics, alliance building, role modeling behavior and building consensus among disparate perspective and competing priorities.
Superior communication skills, both written and verbal; demonstrated high-level drafting skills (e.g., briefing notes, reports, undertakings).
Expressive and persuasive in both spoken and written language
Reason through highly complex spoken and written information
In depth understanding of the Law Society’s mandate, services, legislation and policies
Key Accountabilities
Client / Customer Service Planning
Provides advice, guidance and assistance in planning to Professional Regulation regarding licensee health issues, including licensee incapacity. Develops, recommends and implements training, policy, and effective approaches to the division's activities relating to the incapacity of licensees. In conjunction with division staff establishes and maintains a framework including the creation of effective and ongoing evaluation of investigative and monitoring processes. On an ongoing basis, proactively identifies problems and opportunities and takes action to continuously improve the related work processes.
Maintains up-to-date the “Capacity Resource Manual”, including related procedures, tools and templates. Develops and maintains a roster of health professionals who provide expert opinions to the Law Society with respect to licensee health issues and regularly assesses opinions received with respect to quality, including timeliness. Develops and maintains up-to-date training and orientation materials/programs.
Client / Customer Service Delivery
Monitors the progress of capacity related processes, participating in initial and ongoing risk assessment, the resolution of deficiencies or problems in processes, and coaching and developing the skills and abilities of division staff.  Conducts capacity-related training for Professional Regulation and others across the organization.  Establishes performance measures and targets to address issues of consistency, quality, and efficiency of related processes. Identifies and seeks out external expert resources, when necessary, to ensure that the necessary case specific competencies are met. Identifies where further investigation of issues is required, considering standards of quality, the political and environmental context of the case.
Conducts outreach, including ongoing recruitment and training of medical assessors, liaises with stakeholders, including Ontario Lawyers Assistance Program (OLAP), Ontario Bar Association (OBA)/Canadian Bar Association (CBA), Homewood, and provides related presentations. Conducts relevant research, including research design, data collection, analysis, and reporting. Maintains current list of educational resources.  Regularly assesses and reviews strategies and processes to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of the Law Society’s oversight of licensee health related matters.
Performance Goals, Targets and Standards
Collaborates with the Manager & Senior Counsel, and other Professional Regulation managers and Counsel to develop and monitor standards and best practices in managing health issues of licensees focusing on risk management and the setting of priorities and targets with a view to improving regulator effectiveness in dealing with licensee incapacity. Engages in continuous improvement with respect to standards and services provided to stakeholders.
Policy Development
In conjunction with the Manager & Senior Counsel and Professional Regulation managers identifies emerging health issues affecting professionals, particularly substance use disorders, mental health disorders and dementias. Establishes and implements consistent, fair and sound evidentiary policies and procedures. Advises the Manager & Senior Counsel and members of the division with respect to licensee health issues, including incapacity. Participates in strategic planning and development of policy relating to the division’s licensee health matters and contributes information and expertise to policy development initiatives in regulatory functions as appropriate. Makes recommendations on the development of policies and other initiatives to address these issues. Monitors new and in-progress case files for trends and patterns, and assesses the implications of same with respect to Professional Regulation and related regulatory processes. Participates in strategic planning and policy development as it relates to licensee health issues.
Relationship and Alliance Building
Serves as an information and strategic resource on licensee health to Professional Regulation as well as other staff within the Law Society. Promotes an assistive, collaborative approach in dealings with licensee health related issues in order to produce appropriate remedial outcomes in a large and diverse number of cases.
Conducts outreach, including ongoing recruitment and training of medical assessors and liaison with stakeholders, including members of OLAP, OBA/CBA, and Homewood.

The Payroll Coordinator supports the administration of the payroll function.  This includes the processing of the employee, member parental leave assistance program, and bencher payrolls, along with related source deductions and remittances, preparation of pension and benefits remittances, processing of payroll related journal entries, General Ledger account reconciliations, support the T4, T4A, EHT and WSIB reporting processes managed by the Payroll Specialist, and maintenance of payroll and related files and information. The position is responsible for the updating of the bencher attendance tracking database used to support reporting to the Audit & Finance Committee. The role assists in the preparation of required reporting for benchers and the Audit & Finance Committee, and ad hoc reporting requests for Senior Management and other Committees.
Qualifications
Education and Training
The minimum level of education required to fulfill the core requirements of this position include a college diploma or university degree in business or accounting. Payroll Compliance Practitioner (PCP) required; Payroll Leadership Professional (PLP) or actively working towards PLP strongly preferred.
Experience
The Payroll Coordinator requires a minimum of 4 years previous related experience in a computerized payroll and benefits administration environment, with solid understanding of general accounting functions.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities
Solid understanding of payroll processes and relevant legislation, benefits administration, source deduction and government remittance procedures
General understanding of general accounting functions, including GAAP / CICA guidelines, accounts payable and financial reporting
Solid understanding of Law Society by-laws and policies as they apply to bencher remuneration, expense reimbursement, payroll and related internal controls
Professional communication skills with the ability to speak and write in a clear, articulate manner when communicating with benchers, adjudicators, and staff
Reason through moderately complex spoken and written information in order to communicate by-law, policy, process and standards of reasonableness information in an audience appropriate format
Technical Skills and Knowledge
Thorough knowledge of automated payroll systems and absence management applications,
Thorough knowledge of personal computers and software applications related to a computerized accounting environment, particularly the use of spreadsheet analyses in support of the finance function and report writing applications
Knowledge of reporting tools such as Crystal reports
Key Accountabilities
Client / Customer Service Delivery
Contributes to the development and implementation of integrated payroll processes in support of Law Society client departments and divisions, benchers, and related organizations.
Works closely with client departments and others to communicate appropriate payroll processes, reviews and verifies payroll information, and contributes to the exchange of information.
Provides detailed information and reports as required, responds to client inquiries, and follows up to ensure resolution of complaints.
Remains abreast of Law Society by-laws and policies as well as Canada Revenue Agency statutes, legislation and regulations pertaining to employee payroll, bencher remuneration and expense reimbursement, and communicates the application of same to employees and benchers, (e.g. expense claims allowed, adjusted and disallowed).
Prepares written communication to benchers and adjudicators related to sensitive expense and remuneration matters.
Client / Customer Service Planning
Acts as a subject-matter expert within the Payroll team as well as other departments across the organization on payroll systems, bencher expense reimbursement, and associated guidelines and processes.
Identifies opportunities for improvements within the payroll function, and develops approaches to address these opportunities.
Monitors and assists in improving and implementing new payroll processes and systems through analysis, research and recommendations.
Financial Responsibility
Processes and validates parental leave, employee and bencher payroll and benefits information, in accordance with Canada Revenue Agency statutes, relevant legislation and regulations, and Law Society policies and procedures.
Assists the Payroll Specialist in the processing of Law Society payrolls, including the extraction of needed information from the time and attendance application, analyzing and questioning information, following up to gain clarification.
Processes a full range of transactions and exchanges information with service providers, financial institutions, Law Society client departments, employees, members and benchers to ensure the timely and accurate flow of payrolls (employees, members and benchers).
Administers retirements, terminations and individual record changes, prepares journal entries, and assists with the reconciliation and issuance of T4 slips.
Reviews bencher expense claims for authorization and reasonableness, allocates to appropriate expense category and processes for payment.
Ensures that details of expense claims are accurate and complete, following up with benchers to confirm information, and reconciles approved claims and remuneration payments.
Processes approved bencher activity sheets for remuneration purposes, calculating appropriate statutory deductions and processing in payroll system.
Generates canned and develops custom reports using applicable reporting tools in support of informational needs of management and the Audit & Finance Committee, as required, from information residing in the payroll system, time and attendance application or the bencher tracking database.
For Law Society employee payroll, prepares journals for posting to sub-ledger and general ledgers and uploads the information into the Law Society’s financial system.
Team Membership
Actively participates with other members of the department, contributing to department‑wide projects.
Collaborates with the Payroll Specialist to complete the daily operation of the department, and takes direction from Specialist with respect to Payroll policies, processes and best practices.
Works cooperatively with client department staff to clarify information and provide assistance regarding payroll procedures, and provide accurate and timely service to benchers, employees, clients and customers.
