Maintenir une visibilité claire sur les licences logicielles, les abonnements, les renouvellements et leur utilisation.
Coordonner les processus d’approvisionnement, de déploiement, de remplacement et de disposition avec le fournisseur de services gérés, les Finances et les autres fournisseurs.
Veiller à ce que les registres des actifs et des licences soient exacts, complets et régulièrement examinés.
Soutenir la budgétisation et les prévisions relatives aux actifs technologiques, aux licences, aux renouvellements et aux dépenses opérationnelles.
Cerner les possibilités de rationaliser les licences, de réduire le gaspillage et d’accroître la valeur des investissements technologiques.
Veiller à ce que les processus liés aux arrivées, aux changements de poste et aux départs soient reflétés avec exactitude dans les registres des actifs, des licences et des accès.

Processus opérationnels, contrôles et rapports

title: Senior Procurement Associate / Associé principal en approvisionnement
description:
Corporate Profile
CDEV advances economic prosperity for Canada by delivering financial and commercial expertise to the Government of Canada. A self-sustaining Crown corporation since 1982, and reporting to Parliament through the Minister of Finance CDEV is the federal government’s trusted advisor and active asset manager of more than $75 billion in strategic assets. Operating at arm’s length and at the speed of business, CDEV is regularly called upon to advise on and execute critical financial transactions, support priority policy objectives, and maximize the value of corporate assets in Canada’s best interest. In periods of economic pressure, CDEV brings the agility and rapid responsiveness required for government to act quickly and effectively.
Headquartered in Toronto, with an office in Ottawa and governed by an independent board of directors, CDEV has four pillars of expertise:
Asset Management
Financial and Commercial Advice
Monetization and Divestments
Indigenous Economic Participation
Drawing on deep private and public sector experience, CDEV is responsible for the active management of over $75 billion of assets and programs through its eight subsidiaries, forming the CDEV Group of Companies. Its high-profile roles in recent years include the purchase and ongoing management of the Trans Mountain pipeline, the establishment of the $15-billion Canada Growth Fund, the establishment and management of the $10-billion Large Employer Tariff Loan (LETL) facility and the $10-billion federal Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program, and the $2.14-billion financing agreement with Telesat to support Canada’s largest ever space program.
Position Overview
Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer, the Senior Procurement Associate will provide procurement advice, coordination and hands-on support across CDEV’s procurement activities. The role will help ensure that purchasing and contracting activities are conducted in a transparent, fair, well-documented and policy-compliant manner, with particular attention to procurement policies and expectations applicable to federal Crown corporations. The Senior Procurement Associate will support business units through the full procurement lifecycle, including planning, solicitation strategy, request for proposal processes, evaluation support, contract award documentation, supplier engagement and continuous improvement of procurement practices.
Responsibilities
Lead and support procurement activities across the organization, including procurement planning, sourcing strategies, solicitation documents, evaluations, approvals, awards and file documentation.
Advise internal clients on procurement requirements, policy obligations, risk considerations and appropriate procurement approaches for goods and services.
Support the development and administration of RFPs, RFQs and other competitive procurement processes, including drafting procurement documents, coordinating vendor questions and addenda, and supporting evaluation committees.
Review procurement files to help ensure transparency, fairness, value for money, appropriate approvals and compliance with policies applicable to federal Crown corporations.
Prepare procurement-related briefing materials, recommendations, evaluation summaries, award documentation and records of decision for management review.
Support contract award, vendor notification, supplier debriefings and transition to contract administration, working with business units and legal or finance colleagues as required.
Identify opportunities to improve procurement tools, templates, processes and guidance to strengthen consistency, efficiency and governance across CDEV.
The selected candidate will be based in Toronto or Ottawa, currently with a hybrid work option.
Needed Skills
Strong knowledge of procurement policies, practices and governance expectations applicable to federal Crown corporations, including public-sector transparency, fairness, value-for-money and documentation requirements.
Experience with procurement in the financial services or related sectors, including professional services procurement would be considered an asset.
Experience advising internal clients on procurement strategy, sourcing options, solicitation design, evaluation approaches, risk management and contract award processes.
Practical experience supporting RFPs, RFQs, standing offers, vendor communications, evaluation committees, procurement files, contract administration and supplier debriefings.
Ability to interpret procurement requirements and translate them into clear, practical guidance for business units and senior leaders.
Sound judgment, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple procurement files in a fast-paced, commercially oriented environment.
Required Skills and Qualifications
Post-secondary education in business administration, supply chain management, public administration, finance, law or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Several years of progressive procurement, sourcing, contracting or supply chain experience, preferably in a federal Crown corporation, public-sector, broader public-sector or regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience supporting competitive procurement processes, including RFP planning, drafting, evaluation support, approvals, award recommendations and procurement file documentation.
Knowledge of federal procurement policy frameworks, trade agreement considerations, conflict of interest principles, contract management practices and supplier relationship management.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear procurement documents, briefing materials, recommendations and records of decision.
High degree of professionalism, discretion and integrity, with a commitment to ethical procurement and sound stewardship of public resources.
Bilingualism in English and French is considered an asset.
CDEV’s employee value proposition is centered on building, developing and retaining a high-performing and commercially minded team. As a result of these efforts, CDEV earned the
Great Place To Work®
in 2025.
We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, and we will work with you if you require accessibility accommodation at any point during the recruitment process, pending that you let us know of your needs in advance. Note that only qualified candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
Profil de l’entreprise
La Corporation développement des investissements du Canada (CDEV) favorise la prospérité économique du Canada en fournissant une expertise financière et commerciale au gouvernement du Canada. Société d’État autofinancée en activité depuis 1982, la CDEV relève du Parlement par l’intermédiaire du ministre des Finances. Elle est la conseillère de confiance du gouvernement fédéral et gère activement plus de 75 milliards de dollars d’actifs stratégiques. Fonctionnant en toute indépendance et au rythme des affaires, la CDEV est régulièrement appelée à donner des conseils et à mener à bien des transactions financières cruciales, à soutenir des objectifs stratégiques de politique publique et à maximiser la valeur des actifs corporatifs dans l’intérêt supérieur du Canada. En période de tensions économiques, la CDEV apporte la souplesse et la réactivité nécessaires pour permettre aux pouvoirs publics d’agir rapidement et efficacement.
Située à Toronto, disposant d’un bureau à Ottawa et dirigée par un conseil d’administration indépendant, la CDEV s’appuie sur quatre piliers de l’expertise :
Gestion d’actifs
Conseils financiers et commerciaux
Monétisation et dessaisissement
Participation économique des Autochtones
Forte d’une solide expérience dans les secteurs privé et public, la CDEV assure la gestion active de plus de 75 milliards de dollars d’actifs et de programmes par l’intermédiaire de ses huit filiales, formant le groupe de sociétés de la CDEV. Parmi ses rôles les plus importants de ces dernières années, on peut citer l’acquisition et la gestion continue de l’oléoduc Trans Mountain, la création du Fonds de croissance du Canada de 15 milliards de dollars, l’établissement et la gestion du Crédit pour les grandes entreprises touchées par les droits de douane (CGETDD) d’une valeur de 10 milliards de dollars, le Programme fédéral de garantie de prêts pour les Autochtones d’une valeur de 10 milliards de dollars et l’accord de financement de 2,14 milliards de dollars conclu avec Telesat pour soutenir le plus important programme spatial jamais réalisé par le Canada.
Aperçu du poste
Relevant du chef de l’administration, la personne titulaire du poste d’associée principale ou d’
associé principal en
approvisionnement fournira des conseils, de la coordination et un soutien pratique relativement aux activités d’approvisionnement de la CDEV. Elle contribuera à faire en sorte que les activités d’achat et de passation de marchés soient menées de manière transparente, équitable, bien documentée et conforme aux politiques, en portant une attention particulière aux politiques et aux attentes en matière d’approvisionnement applicables aux sociétés d’État fédérales. Elle appuiera les unités opérationnelles tout au long du cycle d’approvisionnement, notamment la planification, la stratégie de sollicitation, les processus de demande de propositions, le soutien aux évaluations, la documentation liée à l’attribution des contrats, les relations avec les fournisseurs et l’amélioration continue des pratiques d’approvisionnement.
Responsabilités
Diriger et soutenir les activités d’approvisionnement à l’échelle de l’organisation, notamment la planification, les stratégies de sourçage, les documents de sollicitation, les évaluations, les approbations, les attributions et la documentation des dossiers.
Conseiller les clients internes sur les exigences en matière d’approvisionnement, les obligations liées aux politiques, les considérations relatives aux risques et les approches appropriées pour l’acquisition de biens et de services.
Soutenir l’élaboration et l’administration des demandes de propositions, des demandes de prix et d’autres processus d’approvisionnement concurrentiels, y compris la rédaction des documents, la coordination des questions des fournisseurs et des addendas, ainsi que l’appui aux comités d’évaluation.
Examiner les dossiers d’approvisionnement afin de contribuer à assurer la transparence, l’équité, l’optimisation des ressources, les approbations appropriées et la conformité aux politiques applicables aux sociétés d’État fédérales.
Préparer des notes d’information, des recommandations, des résumés d’évaluation, des documents d’attribution et des comptes rendus de décision liés à l’approvisionnement aux fins d’examen par la direction.
Soutenir l’attribution des contrats, les avis aux fournisseurs, les comptes rendus aux fournisseurs et la transition vers l’administration des contrats, en collaboration avec les unités opérationnelles et les collègues des services juridiques ou financiers, au besoin.
Cerner les occasions d’améliorer les outils, les modèles, les processus et les lignes directrices en matière
d’approvisionnement afin de renforcer la cohérence, l’efficacité et la gouvernance à l’échelle de la CDEV.
La personne retenue sera basée à Toronto ou à Ottawa, avec actuellement une option de travail hybride.
Compétences recherchées
Solide connaissance des politiques, pratiques et attentes de gouvernance en matière d’approvisionnement applicables aux sociétés d’État fédérales, notamment en ce qui concerne la transparence, l’équité, l’optimisation des ressources et la documentation.
Expérience dans la prestation de conseils aux clients internes sur les stratégies d’approvisionnement, les options de sourçage, la conception des sollicitations, les approches d’évaluation, la gestion des risques et les processus d’attribution de contrats.
Expérience pratique du soutien aux demandes de propositions, aux demandes de prix, aux offres à commandes, aux communications avec les fournisseurs, aux comités d’évaluation, aux dossiers d’approvisionnement, à l’administration des contrats et aux comptes rendus aux fournisseurs.
Capacité d’interpréter les exigences en matière d’approvisionnement et de les traduire en conseils clairs et pratiques pour les unités opérationnelles et les dirigeants.
Bon jugement, souci du détail et capacité de gérer plusieurs dossiers d’approvisionnement dans un environnement dynamique axé sur les affaires.
Compétences et attributs requis
Diplôme d’études postsecondaires en administration des affaires, gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, administration publique, finances, droit ou dans une discipline connexe, ou combinaison équivalente d’études et d’expérience.
Plusieurs années d’expérience progressive en approvisionnement, sourçage, passation de marchés ou gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, préférablement dans une société d’État fédérale, le secteur public, le secteur parapublic ou un environnement réglementé.
Expérience démontrée du soutien aux processus d’approvisionnement concurrentiels, y compris la planification des demandes de propositions, la rédaction, le soutien aux évaluations, les approbations, les recommandations d’attribution et la documentation des dossiers d’approvisionnement.
Connaissance des cadres de politiques fédérales en matière d’approvisionnement, des considérations liées aux accords commerciaux, des principes relatifs aux conflits d’intérêts, des pratiques de gestion des contrats et de la gestion des relations avec les fournisseurs.
Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et verbale, y compris la capacité de préparer des documents d’approvisionnement, des notes d’information, des recommandations et des comptes rendus de décision clairs.

title: Director, Legal Services
description:
CreateTO
is shaping Toronto’s future through impactful real estate solutions. A City of Toronto agency, CreateTO works collaboratively with internal stakeholders, external partners and community members to create more livable, sustainable and inclusive communities. CreateTO is here to increase the social, cultural and economic value of our city’s $27-billion real estate portfolio, ensuring positive impacts for residents and a bright future for Toronto.
We are looking for a lawyer who understands the business and strategic objectives behind a transaction, can identify and manage risk while minimizing project delays, and can provide clear, practical advice to senior leaders and project teams. If you’re passionate about contributing to the best use of one of North America’s largest and most valuable real estate portfolios, we’d love to have you on the team.
THE OPPORTUNITY
The Director, Legal Services supports the Associate General Counsels and Chief Legal Counsel in resolving legal issues, ensuring legal compliance and mitigating risks. The role includes:
Supporting the legal aspects of the assigned portfolio of projects and corporate functions.
Providing advice on legal implications related to CreateTO’s projects.
Maintaining an awareness of legal and regulatory matters relevant to achieve CreateTO’s broad business and policy objectives.
Advising project leads on all legal matters affecting CreateTO’s projects and business arrangements to support operational decision-making.
PRINCIPAL FUNCTIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Maintaining a deep understanding of CreateTO’s business and industry and providing leadership in operational business decisions from a legal perspective.
Leading the drafting and negotiating of complex real estate and leasing transactions, including acquisitions, dispositions, leases, licences, easements, rights-of-way, development agreements, reciprocal rights and operating agreements, and other property-related arrangements.
Providing strategic legal advice on lease structuring, property/asset management, development rights, environmental matters, litigation and other landlord and tenant issues.
Advising on transaction structures involving public and private-sector partners, joint ventures, development partners and other stakeholders.
Providing legal advice throughout the development lifecycle, from early feasibility and structuring through approvals, financing, construction, project delivery and long-term operations.
Providing legal advice on construction and capital projects, including construction agreements (e.g. CCDC and OAA), consultant agreements, low carbon and sustainability initiatives, procurement, project delivery, insurance, contractor/consultant performance, change orders, claims, disputes, litigation and other construction related matters.
Conducting due diligence on real estate and commercial leasing transactions, including title searches and corporate searches.
Navigating legal and regulatory challenges to achieve CreateTO’s broad business and policy objectives.
Providing direction and supervision to external counsel, including with respect to litigation, arbitrations, mediations and expropriations.
CANDIDATE ATTRIBUTES
An experienced lawyer with 7+ years of broad real estate, commercial leasing, development and construction experience that meets the above requirements, and the ability to lead cross-divisional teams to resolve legal issues.
Ideally will have had exposure to public and private sector real estate interests and land use planning, as well as gained corporate governance experience and board experience.
Aptitude for detail, with a high level of accuracy and superior legal drafting skills.
Exceptional organizational skills are necessary to coordinate a variety of responsibilities, in an often-changing environment, to achieve stated goals and objectives.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to exercise good judgment, tact and discretion.
Ability to work with highly confidential information with both maturity and professionalism.
A high degree of competence in verbal and written communication.
Ability to solve problems and take the initiative.
TOTAL COMPENSATION
The salary range for this position is $128,270 to $192,910 annually, with the expected range for this role to start between $150,000 to $160,000 commensurate with qualifications and experience.
In addition to base salary, CreateTO offers a comprehensive total compensation package including participation in the OMERS defined benefit pension plan, competitive vacation entitlement, extended health and dental benefits, life and disability insurance, and access to employee wellness support including an Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
With a highly engaged team, CreateTO scores well above benchmarked organizations in terms of its employees’ passion, commitment, diversity and pride. As part of the organization’s Strategic Plan 2023-2027, “Inspire internal success” was named as one of five priority objectives.
CreateTO wants its team to reflect the city we represent, and we strive to provide an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, and perspective, all of which are proven to build better companies. Our goal is to create an environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best work and be themselves.

title: Manager, Operations & Maintenance
employer: Exhibition Place (Board of Governors) / Canadian National Exhibition Association
description:

Established in 1879 and located on the shores of Lake Ontario, Toronto, the award-winning Exhibition Place is Canada’s largest entertainment venue, hosting over 2,000 events and attracting over 5.5 million visitors a year. The 192-acre site is an integral component of Toronto and Ontario’s economy, particularly with respect to conventions, sports, festivals, recreation, culture, and tourism. Exhibition Place boasts the award-winning, LEED Gold Certified Enercare Centre, Canada’s largest exhibition and convention centre, and the Automotive Building LEED Silver conference venue. Since 2004, Exhibition Place has undertaken an environmental stewardship initiative, entitled GREENSmart, which includes the promotion of sustainable development, environmental initiatives and leading-edge green technologies and practices across the site.

What can I expect to do in this role?

Manage the provision of maintenance and repair services including carpentry, electrical, energy management, building automations, lighting controls, mechanical, fleet operations, heating/ventilation/air-conditioning, locksmith services, mechanical, painting, plumbing, vehicle maintenance and welding.
Establish a positive, healthy and safe work environment in accordance with all appropriate legislation and regulations.
Uphold and enforce organizational policies and procedures.
Ensure compliance with the building, electrical and fire safety codes
Develop and manage the planning and implementation of environmental and energy conservation initiatives.
Review and approve purchase requisition for operations services.
Oversee preparation and approve cost estimates on behalf of operations services.
Analyze and effectively resolve operational issues and advise the Director of Operations and Facilities Services.
Manage and maintain the District Energy Plant as well as the power supply to the site & tenants.
Manage the Exhibition Place Internal Utilities Metering System for both internal and tenant customers.
Manage maintenance planning and the Computerized Maintenance Management Software (CMMS).
Design and implement PM programs to reduce breakdowns.
Ensure timely completion of preventative and proactive maintenance programs.
Consult and advise of cost-effective solutions to client functional requirements.
Provide technical advice & feedback to capital projects as required.
Participate in project teams as a strategic resource in a leadership capacity.
Initiate the development and implementation of policies, procedures and standards in the area of electrical/mechanical and maintenance operations.
Provide guidance in the preparation of tender documents, quotations and contracts related to facility services.
Perform other duties as assigned.
How do I qualify?
Post-secondary education in mechanical or electrical engineering discipline plus a minimum of 10 years maintenance experience in a fast-paced facility complex.
Extensive experience at management level in the area of electrical/mechanical/automation/ metering, building systems services preferably in a maintenance and consumer show environment.
Experience in managing staff in unionized environment.
Strong functional ability in the use of a standard office suite of computer programs and knowledge of facility management software packages.
Excellent skills in the area of verbal and written communications, interpersonal, conflict resolution and problem solving at all organizational levels including political level and third party clients.
Required to respond to emergencies outside of regular working hours, as necessary to support operational requirements.
Extensive knowledge of and ability to interpret collective agreements,
Occupational Health & Safety Act
, Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System, applicable codes, standards, guidelines and government legislation as they apply to operations services.
Proven customer services skills.

title: Licensing Analyst
description:
WHY WORK AT HCRA:
We foster a professional home building industry that Ontarians can trust.
The Home Construction Regulatory Authority (HCRA) is a not-for-profit corporation that is designated by the provincial government of Ontario to administer and enforce the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017 and associated regulations. HCRA holds licensed builders to professional standards, protects the public interest, and enhances consumer confidence in the homebuilding industry in Ontario. In addition, HCRA strives to educate consumers to ensure that they can make informed decisions and understand the benefits of a regulated homebuilding sector. As one of Ontario’s newest regulators, HCRA is dedicated to providing the highest level of service to everyone they serve.
HCRA provides a flexible, hybrid and collaborative work environment, with an array of benefits as well as considerable time off allowances. Additionally, as a mid-sized organization, team members have direct exposure to senior management on a regular basis, and they get the opportunity to work on a range of assignments with significant responsibilities. By joining the HCRA, you'll be a part of the establishment of a growing regulator that is passionate, engaged, forward-thinking, and innovative.
WHAT THE POSITION IS:
We are seeking a permanent, full-time Licensing Analyst as a backfill. Reporting to the Supervisor, Licensing, you'll review and assess new licence and licence renewal applications, including supporting and historical information, and make recommendations in line with HCRA's licensing criteria and operational policies under the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017. You'll carry your own file of applications, recommending approval, conditions on the licence, or refusal, and using sound judgement about when a file needs to be escalatedfor further review. Day to day, you'll follow up with applicants to close information gaps, respond to escalated licensing inquiries, and keep records accurate and complete in Dynamics 365 CRM and the Ontario Builder Directory. You'll also support the team's administrative work as needed, including fees, payments and incoming applications. Beyond your own files, you may be asked to contribute to the development of licensing processes, guidelines, tools and forms, and consumer and public education materials, helping the team improve how licensing works and roll out program changes.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:
Success in this role requires hands-on experience assessing applications or files against legislation or policy, so you can work independently on most files within your first few months. You'll bring a sharp eye for detail and a commitment to accuracy, whether you're reviewing an application, entering data or reconciling fees. You should be able to interpret and apply legislation and policy to individual files, reach a sound, well-documented recommendation, and recognize when a file needs to be escalated. You'll manage a high-volume caseload and competing deadlines without losing accuracy, and work well both independently and with colleagues in Licensing, Finance, Professional Conduct and other teams. Just as important are strong client service and communication skills (written and verbal), including the ability to explain recommendations clearly to the Supervisor, Assistant Deputy Registrar, and senior staff, and to communicate licensing requirements to applicants in plain terms.
We are looking for two to four years of experience reviewing applications, files or submissions against legislation, regulations or policy, ideally in a regulatory, licensing or compliance environment. These skills may come from work experience, education, training, or a combination.
Experience at a Delegated Administrative Authority, regulator or licensing body would be an asset, as would knowledge of the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017 and the Ontario Building Code.
We would also value experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 or a similar CRM, experience reviewing financial, background or conduct information, and proficiency in French or another language that helps us communicate with Ontario's builders and homebuyers
Annual Salary Range:
The salary range for this position is between $68,000.00 CAD and $85,000.00 CAD (Depending on qualifications, skills, and experience).
APPLICATION INFORMATION:
If interested, please apply by
October 20, 2026
.
We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.  If you have questions, you can also contact HR at
hr@hcraontario.ca
. For more information about HCRA or to view other career opportunities, please visit
www.hcraontario.ca
.
Accommodation, if required, will be provided throughout the hiring process in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code.
HCRA is committed to providing an atmosphere free from barriers that promotes equity, inclusion and belonging. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against employees or qualified applicants on the basis of race, religion, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, marital or family status, age, gender identity or expression, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Your application will always be reviewed by a person. AI is not used to screen, source, or select applicants at any stage of our recruitment process, but may be used in a limited supporting way.

Our Capital Project Group within GO/UP is looking for multiple Construction Management Field Specialists to join the team! Reporting to the Senior Manager, Construction Management Field, you will oversee the safe delivery of construction projects within your designated project portfolio such as, signals, stations and track. In compliance with Metrolinx policies, procedures, systems, resources, and deliverables you will ensure the safety and protection of employees and contractors and maintain associated corporate values, and act as embedded members within the corridor Delivery Teams bringing construction and project management related expertise and guidance in a collaborative working group.
What will I be doing?
Undertake site coverage and provide site presence over the project works from the context of safety, quality, environment, engineering/design compliance, functionality, and commissioning, and providing feedback and input to Delivery Teams.
Undertake handovers/inspections between Project Delivery Teams and asset operators/maintainers, as applicable.
Monitor day-to-day construction activities, ensuring that they are in accordance with planned works, which includes review of lookahead and dashboard activities, reviewing and understanding workplans and corridor access, and ensuring construction site activities comply with the planned works, protection means, and applicable permits.
Support coordination and deconfliction of concurrent and overlapping works between contractors, Delivery Teams, Operations, asset stakeholders and other affected parties.
Track site progress and productivity, reporting against project schedules by monitoring on-site activities and summarizing through daily site reports. This includes tracking under-performances and resource utilization (incl. access utilization).
Provide construction and project management level expertise into Metrolinx business units, which includes input into project and program schedules, policies and procedures, standards and standard development, engineering assurance, health and safety, workplan and design reviews, operating practices, and general best practices, lessons learned and industry standards.
Undertake and participate in regular safety engagements with contractors and project teams, including field observations and discussions, promoting proactive identification and resolution of safety concerns and reinforcing Metrolinx safety expectations.
Manage the identification and resolution of issues related to construction health and safety incidents, escalates high-profile, near miss, and complex matters to the Manager or Senior Manager, and recommends changes to methods, equipment, and materials to improve safety.
Develops relationships with external consultants, contractors, and stakeholders to secure cooperation in effectively coordinating overlapping work activities to ensure on-site performance and construction procedures meet legislation and regulatory requirements, contractual agreements, and Metrolinx safety requirements.
What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?
Completion of a degree or diploma in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Trades, Occupational Health and Safety or a related discipline is an asset.
Demonstrates progressive experience in planning, design, construction, construction supervision, construction safety, and administration of infrastructure or similar large-scale projects. Rail (track and/or signals) experience is considered an asset.
A valid Ontario Class G driver’s license is required to travel to various site locations. Must meet and maintain the corporate standard for a good driving record.
Demonstrates progressive experience in project management, understanding contracts and change variations. Experience with different procurement models (P3, AFP, Alliance, DBB) is considered an asset.
Experience working in an Owner and/or Constructor organization with knowledge of the required roles and responsibilities is considered an asset.
Must be able to obtain qualifications in Canadian Rail Operating Rules (CROR).
Knowledge of the application of legislation and regulatory requirements governing health and safety in the construction industry for the implementation and maintenance of construction safety management plans and policies, procedures and best practices to ensure the safety and protection of employees, construction contractors and associated corporate values.
Ability to read and understand work methodology plans, engineering drawings, risk assessments, and other construction management documents, applying knowledge to review and critique where required against site conditions.

This role is site-based. Frequent, regular and consistent site presence at project site locations is required. .
Required to work evenings, nights and weekends on a rotational basis, subject to call-in during emergencies and to assist with accident investigations.
Works outdoors in all weather conditions and at all hours of the day or night.

The
Engineering & Safety Division
is hiring an
Engineering Lead, Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
whom provides strategic leadership for the development, governance, integration, and application of Geographic Information Systems across the Engineering and Safety Division (ESD). The Engineering Lead, GIS is responsible for ensuring that geospatial information and analysis are effectively integrated into business processes and decision-making across the organization.
Working at the intersection of engineering, asset management, capital planning, operations, and technology, this role establishes the strategic direction and governance framework for GIS while leading the development of advanced geospatial capabilities that support a common, system-level understanding of the railway network.
The role will enable the organization to integrate asset location with condition, age, performance, lifecycle, operational, and project information to support evidence-based decisions and optimize infrastructure investment.
Why This Role Matters
The Engineering Lead, GIS will play a critical role in enabling Metrolinx to make increasingly integrated, evidence-based decisions about its infrastructure and assets.
As the Asset Management Program continues to mature, the organization requires the ability to understand not only asset inventories, but also how asset condition, risk, performance, operational constraints, capital projects, and planned interventions interact spatially across the network.
This position provides the leadership required to establish GIS as a foundational component of that capability. Through effective governance, data integration, spatial analytics, and cross-functional leadership, the Engineering Lead, GIS will enable the organization to:
Improve the prioritization of infrastructure investments.
Coordinate capital interventions across multiple programs.
Identify spatial dependencies, conflicts, and opportunities.
Strengthen risk-based asset management and State of Good Repair planning.
Improve visibility of asset condition and lifecycle requirements.
Integrate engineering, asset, operational, and project information.
Support system-level planning across the railway network.
Provide senior leaders with clear, spatially informed decision-support information.
Establish consistent enterprise geospatial standards and practices.
Advance the organization's digital asset management capabilities.
What Will I Be Doing?
Strategic GIS Leadership
Establish and lead the strategic direction for GIS within the Engineering and Safety Division, ensuring alignment with enterprise Asset Management, State of Good Repair (SOGR), capital investment, and infrastructure planning objectives.
Develop and maintain a division-wide GIS strategy, roadmap, and business plan that identifies priorities, capabilities, technology requirements, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
Provide strategic advice and subject matter expertise to senior leadership on the use of geospatial information, analytics, and technology to support infrastructure and asset management decisions.

practices of customer service associated with Single Point of Contact (SPOC) service desk, demonstrating resourcefulness and excellent customer service and problem solving skills.  Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office

Recommends improvements to service desk, computer builds, deployment procedures or identifies areas of improvement while working in the field. Reference and guidance are provided by accepted IT methodologies, documentation, corporate policies and procedures.

description:

Our Finance Office is seeking a highly motivated and analytical Senior Financial Analyst to establish and support inventory governance, controls, and financial oversight. The successful candidate will provide financially informed analysis and decision support to assigned business divisions, ensuring compliance with accounting standards, audit requirements, legal obligations, and corporate reporting requirements. This role requires a strong understanding of the financial and operational impacts of business processes and activities, with a focus on enhancing inventory management practices, strengthening internal controls, and driving operational excellence through timely, accurate, and insightful financial analysis.
What will I be doing?
Inventory Governance, Controls and Compliance -
Establish, maintain, and monitor inventory governance frameworks, internal controls, and risk management processes to ensure compliance with corporate policies, accounting standards, audit requirements, and vendor contracts. Assess existing processes, develop control documentation, recommend improvements, and support governance reporting to senior leadership.
Inventory Accounting and Financial Stewardship -
Provide accounting oversight and technical guidance for inventory related transactions, ensuring the appropriate classification and treatment of inventory, capital assets, impairments, write-offs, and operating expenditures. Review and validate inventory related invoices, reconciliations, and reporting to support accurate financial records and compliance with accounting requirements.
Inventory Reconciliation and Reporting -
Perform and document monthly inventory reconciliations between financial and operational systems, investigate variances, and ensure timely resolution of discrepancies. Develop, maintain, and analyze inventory scorecards, key performance metrics, and reporting to support business decision-making and operational performance.
Physical Inventory Oversight -
Coordinate and support inventory count activities, including cycle counts and annual physical counts. Review count results, assess financial impacts, validate variance explanations, and ensure inventory records accurately reflect physical inventory on hand.
Audit and Stakeholder Support -
Provide analytical support, financial reporting, and subject matter expertise to business partners. Prepare supporting documentation, respond to inventory accounting inquiries, and contribute to presentations, audits, and governance committees.
Financial Planning, Analysis and Business Partnering -
Lead the annual Budget, quarterly Forecast, and long-range planning processes for assigned portfolios, partnering with operational stakeholders to identify risks, opportunities, resource requirements, and cost optimization initiatives.
Financial Reporting and Month-End Close -
Lead month-end, quarter-end, and year-end financial close activities for assigned portfolios, ensuring the completeness, accuracy, and timely reporting of financial results. Analyze actual results against budget and forecast, investigate variances, identify key drivers, and provide meaningful commentary to management and business partners.
What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?
Completion of a degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Commerce, or a combination of education, training and experience deemed equivalent.
Recognized professional accounting designation (i.e., CPA – CMA, CA, CGA) combined with progressive professional experience in business planning and financial management in a large public or private organization is an asset.
Demonstrated years’ progressive experience as a financial analyst.
Experience with Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) principles.
Knowledge of business practices, financial analysis, and reporting; understands the financial and accounting impact of business processes to evaluate current and future business activities (e.g., audit, legal, and reporting requirements).
Experience in the application of the principles and practices of operating and capital budget formulation, analysis, evaluation and controls, financial planning/management processes, generally accepted budgeting principles and techniques, and financial systems.
Extensive experience using MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) software tools.
Knowledge of enterprise-wide financial, human resources and budgeting system, preferably Hyperion.
Familiarity with MS Power BI or other dashboarding/reporting tools an asset.
Highly developed interpersonal, and excellent oral/written/presentation communication skills.

Role Summary
Our award-winning Legal Services team is seeking a labour, employment, and human rights lawyer to join our busy and collegial legal team, headquartered in downtown Toronto. Ideal candidates will have a strong interest in problem solving, contributing to setting key strategic direction, and partaking in the leadership and strategic development of a busy labour and employment legal team.
Reporting to a Director, Legal Services, the successful candidate will provide proactive, timely and strategic advice to senior business leaders and their teams, including labour and employment issues arising from operating a busy bus and train transit network; complex infrastructure construction projects; issues that may impact upon Metrolinx customers and the general public; and a wide range of human resources-related files arising from long-range planning as well as day-to-day operations.
Metrolinx has both unionized and non-union employees, and the workforce is both office-based and front-line. Our bus and rail operations operate within a highly regulated environment. Works independently with a wide variety of business units and stakeholders

Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, oral/written/presentation, and drafting skills, and able to provide legal opinions and interpretations, and direct and manage external legal counsel effectively
Ability to function well under pressure and demonstrate teamwork in a legal department and across client departments
Ability to translate complicated legal concepts into readily understandable advice

title: Director, Sector & Regional Development
description:
Position Summary:
The Director, Sector and Regional Development is responsible for executing on OVIN’s external engagement strategy to drive sector growth, strategic partnerships, and commercialization opportunities across Ontario’s automotive and mobility ecosystem. This role is focused on building and activating relationships with industry, global partners, government, and the broader innovation ecosystem to reinforce OVIN as a key connector and catalyst.
About the Ontario Centre of Innovation:
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is a not-for-profit organization committed to accelerating economic growth in Ontario through the commercialization of advanced technologies and research. OCI acts as a bridge among academia, industry, and government, investing in collaborative R&D, fostering innovation ecosystems, and helping promising ventures bring new technologies to market. In 2024, OCI invested $117 million across the province, including $61 million in industry contributions. These efforts helped drive the creation and retention of over 5,500 jobs and catalyzed more than $700 million in private-sector follow-on investments. OCI’s role is central to Ontario’s vision of innovation-led prosperity: by reducing the risk of commercialization, facilitating partnerships, and strategically deploying capital into high-impact technologies, OCI contributes to the province’s competitiveness, talent retention, and long-term economic resilience.
Key Responsibilities:
As the Director, you will be expected assume the following responsibilities:
Strategic Partnerships & External Engagement
Support the development and deliver on the execution of OVIN’s external engagement strategy across Ontario and priority global markets.
Build, maintain, and expand relationships with industry leaders, SMEs, post-secondary institutions, government, and ecosystem partners.
Identify and secure high-value partnerships that drive commercialization, sector growth, and new opportunities.
Represent OVIN at industry forums, events, and engagements.
Sector Strategy & Market Intelligence
Maintain a deep understanding of sector trends across automotive, mobility, advanced manufacturing, and defence and dual-use technologies.
Identify emerging opportunities and align engagement strategies to advance OVIN’s strategic priorities.
Provide market insights and strategic advice to inform organizational direction and portfolio growth.
Regional & Ecosystem Development
Strengthen relationships across Ontario’s regional innovation ecosystems.
Lead initiatives that promote regional development, supply chain growth, and cross-sector collaboration.
Facilitate connections between Ontario companies and global markets, customers, and partners.
Work closely with internal teams to align external opportunities with program priorities and pipeline development.
Support and contribute to corporate initiatives, advisory committees, and cross-functional activities.
Other duties as assigned
Skills and Competencies:
10+ years of progressive experience in business development, strategic partnerships, or ecosystem development within automotive, mobility, advanced manufacturing, or related sectors
Demonstrated success in originating, structuring, and closing complex, multi-party partnerships and collaborations.
Strong, established network across industry, government, academia, and/or global markets.
Deep understanding of the Ontario innovation ecosystem, including funding programs, commercialization pathways, and key stakeholders.
Proven ability to identify and translate market and technology trends into actionable strategic opportunities.
Experience engaging with global partners and navigating international markets and partnerships
Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to assess business cases, partnership models, and investment opportunities.
Experience working with or alongside large industry players (OEMs, Tier 1s), SMEs, and scaling companies.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-evolving environments.
Strong communication and executive presence, with experience representing organizations in high-profile forums.
Experience contributing to or shaping strategy, policy, or sector-level initiatives.
Highly developed analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear insights.
Ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels, connecting ecosystem opportunities to programmatic outcomes.
High degree of professionalism, integrity, and sound judgment.

OCI staff at all levels
Industry (from the CEO to the shop floor)
Academic researchers, students, university research administrative staff
University/college/hospital/government administration
Government (at all levels, federal, provincial, and municipal)

description:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) drives the development of Ontario’s economy by helping create new jobs, products, services, technologies, and businesses. We also support and invest in early-stage projects, where the probability of commercial success and potential total return on innovation are substantial. Another expanding focus for OCI is the development of the next generation of innovators through our entrepreneurship fellowships and programs for students and youth across Ontario. title: Program Specialist
description:
Program Specialist - Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI)
Job Summary
The Program Specialist plays a key role in supporting the effective delivery, administration, and performance of the EV ChargeON program portfolio. Working closely with the Director, EV ChargeON and cross-functional teams, the Program
Specialist helps ensure programs are delivered efficiently, transparently, and in alignment with OCI’s operational requirements and government-funded program expectations.
This role is responsible for supporting financial oversight, reporting, and operational coordination across multiple EV
ChargeON projects. The Program Specialist maintains strong internal processes, accurate tracking systems, and clear documentation to support high-quality program governance and seamless execution.
The Program Specialist will work cross-functionally with internal program teams, external funding recipients, charging network operators, consultants, and data stakeholders to ensure reporting compliance, data integrity, and timely delivery of program reporting requirements. This role will also support the development of reporting processes, templates, dashboards, and performance metrics to inform program evaluation, public reporting, and future policy and infrastructure planning.
Who We Are
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is the province’s leading innovation engine, bringing together industry, academia, government, and investors to accelerate commercialization and scale Ontario-made technologies.
From AI and quantum to life sciences, cleantech, and advanced manufacturing, OCI powers the programs and partnerships helping Ontario companies grow, compete globally, and build the future, right here.
Key Responsibilities
. Lead the end-to-end coordination and delivery of all required reporting for the EV ChargeON program, including managing timelines, developing templates, and collaborating with funding recipients to ensure compliant, timely submissions.
. Coordinate with funding recipients and stakeholders to collect operational data, track reporting compliance, and support the implementation of standardized data governance practices.
. Review, validate, clean, and analyze charging usage data and supporting documentation submitted by recipients to ensure data quality, completeness, and consistency.
. Support the development of dashboards and tracking tools to analyze infrastructure performance trends, utilization metrics, and overall program impacts.
. Act as the key point of contact for reporting inquiries, liaising directly with charging network operators, consultants, and project proponents regarding data submissions.
. Drive process improvement by creating standard operating procedures, identifying automation opportunities to streamline workflows, and evolving program metrics to align with EV ChargeON objectives.
. Develop and maintain reporting guidance documents, FAQs, templates, and standard operating procedures.
. Maintain program-wide project trackers to consolidate data being tracked across all projects and prepare data and summary inputs for reporting requirements.
. Maintain a living repository of success stories, key metrics and project outcomes for all projects for use in reporting and communications.
. Complete additional tasks as assigned.
Skills and Competencies:
. University degree in Business, Public Administration, Data Analytics, Engineering, Environmental Studies, or a related field.
. Experience with EV charging infrastructure, clean transportation, energy, utilities, or government funding programs is considered a strong asset.
. Minimum 3+ years of experience in program coordination, reporting, data analysis, infrastructure programs, or related fields.
. Experience managing complex reporting processes involving multiple stakeholders and deadlines.
. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience interpreting large datasets and preparing reporting summaries.
. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong working knowledge of PowerPoint, Word, and reporting or visualization tools.
. Excellent organizational, project management, and communication skills.
. Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, evolving environment with competing priorities.
. Strong stakeholder management and customer service orientation.
. Experience developing operational processes, templates, and reporting frameworks is an asset.
Internal Contacts/External Contacts
. OCI staff across all levels
. SMEs, start-ups and other program applicants
. Industry Partners
. Academic and research institutions
. Utilities
. Government stakeholders
This role is being recruited to fill a current vacancy.
OCI
is committed to creating a diverse and equitable environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. OCI welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Labour and Employee Relations Manager
description:
Position Title:
Labour and Employee Relations Manager
Employment Type:
Full-Time Staff | Non-Union
Annual Salary Range:
$90,000 - $100,000
Division:
People & Culture
Reports To:
Director, Labour and Employee Relations
Location:
2180 Yonge Street, Toronto, ON
TVO Media Education Group (
TVO
) is devoted to inspiring learning that changes lives and enriches communities. We are an internationally recognized digital learning organization that strives to engage, inform, and educate Ontarians of all ages.
Who we are
We are an agency of the Ontario Ministry of Education and a registered charity that contributes to learning, civic engagement, and public service media across Ontario. We provide free, trusted, and accessible educational content that can support Ontarians of all ages, regardless of background, location, or circumstance. To fulfill our mandate, TVO delivers curriculum-connected resources through TVO Learn and TVOkids, offers Ontario’s largest online high school through TVO ILC, and produces journalism, documentaries, current affairs programming, and podcasts with TVO Today that help Ontarians understand the issues shaping their communities.
What we’re looking for
TVO is seeking a seasoned generalist to fill a role as a Labour and Employee Relations Manager to provide practical, solutions-focused labour and employee relations support in a highly unionized environment. This role advises leaders on collective agreement interpretation, grievances, investigations, performance management, and conflict resolution while supporting a constructive, collaborative labour relations culture.
How you will make an impact
Provide day-to-day labour and employee relations advice to managers and People & Culture colleagues, including guidance on collective agreement interpretation, employment legislation, policies, past practice and risk-informed options.
Support the administration of TVO’s policies and collective agreements by helping leaders address issues related to discipline, performance management, attendance, accommodation, restructuring, workforce planning, terms and conditions of employment and other workplace matters.
Work collaboratively with union representatives, managers and internal stakeholders to resolve employee relations issues and grievances in a fair, constructive and timely manner, including participation in grievance meetings, labour-management discussions and follow-up actions.
Conduct fact-finding, workplace reviews and investigations related to employee concerns, policy breaches, discipline, respectful workplace matters and other labour and employee relations files; prepare clear documentation, findings and recommended next steps.
Research, analyze and prepare background materials for collective bargaining, grievance responses, arbitration preparation, settlement discussions and labour relations planning, including comparator research, trend analysis and documentation review and share recommendations with the Director, Labour and Employee Relations.
Support the implementation of negotiated settlements, collective agreement changes and labour relations commitments by coordinating with People & Culture, Total Rewards, HRIS, Payroll, Finance and operational leaders as required, ensuring downstream impacts are understood and implemented accurately.
Help develop and deliver manager resources, communications and informal training and coach leaders to strengthen their confidence in managing within a unionized and non-unionized environment and applying People & Culture policies consistently.
Monitor relevant labour and employment legislation and emerging labour relations practices to support compliance and continuous improvement on matters related to employment standards, labour relations, occupational health and safety, human rights and accessibility, short term disability, accommodations and attendance management.
Maintain accurate file documentation, notes, reports and records that support informed decision-making, timely follow-up and defensible labour and employee relations outcomes.
Apply conflict resolution, facilitation and mediation skills to support effective workplace problem-solving and maintain respectful working relationships with employees, leaders, union partners and colleagues.
What you will bring to TVO
Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Industrial Relations, Labour Relations, Law, Business Administration or a related discipline; equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.
Minimum of 5 years of experience working in a multi union public sector environment, leading investigations, grievances and negotiations.
A strong interest and experience in the use of AI in a human resources environment.
CHRP or CHRL designation is an asset.
Progressive labour and employee relations experience in a unionized environment, with demonstrated ability to interpret and administer collective agreements and advise managers on workplace issues, combined with a broad HR generalist expertise
Strong working knowledge of Ontario labour and employment legislation, including employment standards, labour relations, occupational health and safety, human rights and accessibility requirements.
Experience supporting grievance management, workplace investigations, discipline, performance management, accommodation, restructuring or workforce change files.
Strong research, analytical and writing skills, with the ability to prepare clear summaries, recommendations, briefing materials, investigation documentation and labour relations records.
Sound judgment, discretion and diplomacy when handling confidential, sensitive and/or complex workplace matters under time pressure.
Excellent interpersonal communication, facilitation and conflict resolution skills, with an inclusive and collaborative style that builds trust with leaders, employees, union representatives and colleagues.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, follow through on details and work effectively in a fast-paced environment where issues may be urgent, sensitive or ambiguous.
Self-starter with proven ability to pivot between strategic and hands-on work.
Motivated to pursue new and alternative strategies along with a focus on continuous improvement.
Strong service orientation, mature judgment, attention to detail.
You live our values: we value bold thinking, we embrace change, we thrive with diverse voices, we honour our commitments, we're better together
What we offer
Working at TVO, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work that impacts millions of Ontarians. You’ll belong to a diverse, tight-knit community of talented colleagues who share a passion for education. With learning at the centre of everything we do, we invest in developing our people and promoting a culture of continuous learning. You might even get to meet Polkaroo!
We hope you’ll consider joining us.
Applications will be accepted until 4:00pm on October 30, 2026.
Not sure you have everything we’re asking for, but know you can make a big impact? We encourage you to apply for consideration.
Please Note:
We are hiring for an existing vacancy on our team and expect to move forward with screening and interviewing candidates shortly after the posting closes.
The posted salary range reflects the target hiring range for the position. Final compensation will be determined based on a number of factors including qualifications, relevant experience, and internal equity.
TVO does not use artificial intelligence (AI) or automated decision‑making tools to screen, assess, or select candidates. All applications are reviewed by the hiring team.
Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process (e.g., including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms). If you are seeking accommodations during the application or interview process, please advise us as soon as possible so that appropriate arrangements can be made by sending your request to
accommodations@tvo.org
.

title: Executive Coordinator, Collections Care
description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement. As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking an Executive Coordinator, Collections Care to support the operational, administrative, financial, and project coordination needs of the Collections Care division. Reporting to the Chief, Collections Care, this role serves as a key operational partner, ensuring the department runs smoothly through executive support, budget administration, project coordination, and process improvement. The successful candidate will manage complex administrative activities, support strategic initiatives, coordinate departmental projects, and maintain effective communication across a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. This role is ideal for a highly organized professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys balancing executive support, financial administration, and project coordination responsibilities.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Provide executive-level administrative support to the Chief, Collections Care, including calendar management, meeting coordination, briefing materials, correspondence, and presentations
Coordinate departmental operations, procedures, and administrative processes to support efficiency and productivity across Collections Care
Manage departmental financial administration, including budgeting support, invoice processing, purchase orders, expenditure tracking, reconciliations, and financial reporting
Support the planning, coordination, and execution of Collections Care projects and strategic initiatives, including resource planning, procurement, scheduling, and reporting
Conduct research, environmental scans, stakeholder outreach, and data gathering to support departmental planning and decision-making
Prepare executive summaries, reports, presentations, and briefing materials for leadership and stakeholders
Coordinate departmental events, meetings, travel arrangements, onboarding activities, and professional memberships
Assist with grant, fellowship, and funding-related initiatives that support Collections Care objectives
Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders, handling sensitive and confidential matters with professionalism and discretion
WHAT YOU BRING
University degree, college diploma, or equivalent combination of education and experience in business administration, arts administration, museum studies, cultural management, or a related field
Minimum five (5) years of experience supporting senior leadership in an executive coordination, operations, administrative, or project coordination capacity
Demonstrated experience managing complex calendars, projects, competing priorities, and administrative processes
Experience supporting budgets, financial tracking, expenditure reporting, and procurement processes
Strong proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint
Experience using Power BI, Copilot, Adobe Acrobat, DocuSign, or similar business productivity tools
Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills
Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage confidential information with discretion
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, presentations, and executive correspondence
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders and navigate complex organizational environments
Experience supporting project coordination, process improvement, or strategic initiatives is an asset
French language proficiency is considered an asset
WHAT WE OFFER
Comprehensive benefits coverage:
For permanent and full-time contract positions (conditions apply), enjoy paid benefits for individuals and families, a health spending account, and an Employee Assistance Program.
Worry-free retirement savings:
With our pension plan, you benefit from an employer-matched Defined Benefit contribution plan, which provides predictable lifetime retirement income, survivor benefits, and early retirement options without the stress of investment decisions.
Support for new parents:
Enjoy a parental leave top-up to 95 percent of your salary for 17 weeks, helping you balance work and family life.
Perks:
Free ROM membership for permanent full-time and part-time staff, plus discounts to over 200 attractions through Attractions Ontario.
And more!
SALARY & TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT
START DATE: November 2026
OPEN DATE: October 7, 2026
CLOSE DATE: Open until filled
STATUS: Full-time, permanent
EMPLOYEE GROUP: Non-Union
EXPECTED COMPENSATION: Salary: $74,419 - $87,552
SCHEDULE: 35 hours weekly
PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Six (6) months
LOCATION (onsite): Toronto, ON
WHAT TO EXPECT IN OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS
Application & initial screening:
Apply online. Selected individuals will be invited to complete a pre-recorded video questionnaire to tell us more about your interest in ROM, your team leadership, operations support, and customer service experience, and the impact you could make as part of our Visitor Experience team.
First interview:
A 1-hour in-person interview with the Hiring team. This in-depth interview will focus on your skills and how they align with the team's and ROM's needs.
Second interview:
A 1-hour in-person meeting with the hiring team. You may be asked to present a pre-assigned case study and discuss scenarios relevant to your role. Depending on the position, you might also receive a tour of ROM and a preview of your responsibilities and interactions.
The above-listed process may change or vary based on the nature and scope of the position.
WHY PEOPLE CHOOSE ROM
Cultural engagement:
Daily interactions with Toronto's diverse culture and international visitors offer insights into social and cultural trends. We champion inclusive community programs and connections through diverse experiences.
Continuous learning:
At ROM, expertise and continuous skill development are paramount. Our culture of curiosity and open-mindedness fosters growth beyond traditional career paths.
Passion & fulfillment:
Our work in preserving and curating cultural narratives brings deep satisfaction. We are passionate about the arts, global history, cultural diversity, and leveraging digital technologies to enhance accessibility.
Team & culture:
ROM promotes a positive workplace with collaborative, supportive teams that encourage creativity and innovation. We value new ideas and collective problem-solving.
Academic collaboration:
We are committed to education, partnering with universities and providing student resources, underscoring our dedication to research and accessibility.
If you’re excited about this role, even if your experience differs from the specific requirements, we encourage you to apply. We’re keen to meet candidates who can contribute their talents to our goals, and will consider an equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, education, and experience.
COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, INCLUSION, & ACCESSIBILITY
At ROM, we embrace diversity in our exhibits, communities, and teams. We encourage applications from racialized persons, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQI+ individuals, and those who can further diversify our ideas. We are committed to equitable employment opportunities and a workplace free from discrimination and harassment.
We welcome and accommodate candidates with disabilities throughout the selection process. Please contact us at careers@rom.on.ca for assistance.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
ROM does not require “Canadian experience.” International applicants with equivalent experience are encouraged to apply.
ROM uses technology-assisted tools (including JazzHR TalentFit) to support the review and screening of applications. All hiring decisions are made by human reviewers.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
APPLY NOW
Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Please note that all candidates receiving a verbal job offer will be subject to a background check. This includes a criminal background check and verification of professional references, and, other checks depending on the role.

title: Research Assistant, Japan Gallery (24-month contract)
description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum, ranking among the top 10 cultural institutions in North America. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement. As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost 21st-century museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking a Research Assistant – Japan Gallery for a two-year, full-time contract to support the development of the Prince Takamado Gallery of Japan, planned for 2028.
Reporting to the Chief Curator, Art and Culture and working closely with the Bishop White Committee Curator of Japanese Art and Culture, you will contribute to the research and development of the new gallery while supporting related publications, exhibitions, programs, acquisitions, and loans.
You will research artworks and artifacts within ROM’s collection, contribute to the development of new narratives and approaches to presenting Japanese art and culture, maintain collections documentation, and participate in consultation and collaboration with colleagues and communities. This is an exciting opportunity for an emerging museum professional with expertise in Japanese art and culture to contribute directly to a major gallery development project.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Conduct collections-based research on Japanese artworks and artifacts being considered for inclusion in the new gallery
Research and help identify potential acquisitions and loans that support the gallery’s interpretive and collections objectives
Collaborate in developing narratives, methodologies, and approaches for understanding and presenting Japanese art and culture in a museum setting
Contribute research and content to gallery development, publications, exhibitions, programs, and related initiatives
Maintain accurate collections documentation and data within ROM’s collections management system (TMS)
