title: Senior Conservator (18-month Contract)
description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement. As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking a Senior Conservator of Organic Objects to provide advanced conservation expertise and leadership in the preservation, examination, treatment, and preventive care of objects in ROM’s collections and temporary custody.
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Conservation, you will independently assess complex conservation needs, develop and execute treatments, establish preservation standards, conduct and interpret technical research, and provide expert guidance across the Museum. You will play an integral role in exhibitions, galleries, acquisitions, loans, collections care, emergency response, and major institutional projects while balancing preservation requirements with access, interpretation, and operational needs.
As a senior member of the Conservation team, you will also oversee the effective operation of a conservation laboratory, establish priorities and workflows, and provide guidance and supervision to conservators, interns, volunteers, and project staff as required. This is an opportunity for an accomplished conservation professional to contribute deep technical expertise, sound judgment, and leadership to the stewardship of internationally significant collections.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Examine collection objects, assess their condition and conservation needs, and develop and perform appropriate treatments supported by thorough written and photographic documentation
Establish and apply preventive conservation standards for environmental conditions, handling, storage, mounting, display, packing, transportation, exhibitions, and loans
Conduct technical examination and conservation research into object materials, manufacture, deterioration, treatment methods, and conservation materials, including coordinating and interpreting scientific analysis
Provide conservation expertise for exhibitions, galleries, acquisitions, loans, collections moves, storage improvements, and other major museum initiatives
Collaborate with curators, designers, collections professionals, and project teams to balance preservation requirements with access, interpretation, and operational needs
Survey collections, assess risks, establish conservation priorities, and contribute to preventive conservation, emergency preparedness and emergency response
Lead the effective operation of the conservation laboratory, managing workflows, priorities, equipment, supplies, budgets, and resource requirements
Supervise, mentor, and provide technical guidance to junior conservators, interns, volunteers, and project staff as required
Advance conservation knowledge and practice through research, professional development, publications, presentations, consultations, and public or educational programming
WHAT YOU BRING
Master's Degree in Conservation with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience, specializing in the conservation of organic objects; at least 3 years in a museum setting preferred. Alternatively, a combination of education and experience deemed acceptable.
Advanced expertise in Organic Object conservation specialization, including object materials and fabrication techniques, deterioration processes, examination, preservation, and treatment
Excellent knowledge of conservation treatment theory and practice, preventive conservation, and professional standards and ethics, including the CAC/CAPC Code of Ethics and Guidance for Practice
Demonstrated ability to assess complex conservation problems, exercise sound professional judgment, and independently plan and execute treatments
Experience with scientific examination and analysis, including coordinating analytical work and interpreting findings to inform conservation decisions
Strong conservation documentation skills, including written and photographic documentation and the use of relevant digital, image management, and collections database tools
Proven ability to manage complex projects, priorities, resources, budgets, and deadlines while providing leadership or mentorship to staff, interns, or volunteers
Proficiency in conducting and interpreting scientific analyses such as e.g. p-XRF and digital X-radiography
Excellent organizational, problem-solving, communication, consultation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines
Experience with conservation documentation in a digital content management system. Familiarity with TMS is an asset.
Ability to safely perform precise, physically demanding conservation work, travel with collection objects when required, and respond to urgent conservation needs outside regular working hours

title: Engineer, BPV
description:
About Us:
At Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA), we are deeply committed to safety and passionate about making Ontario a safer place to live, work and play. As one of Ontario’s public safety regulators, established by the provincial government, our team of more than 450 professionals administer safety regulations and enhance public safety across multiple sectors - boilers and pressure vessels and operating engineers; elevating devices, amusement devices and ski lifts; and fuels. Our people are our greatest asset and every role is vital to our vision of working together for safer communities —today and tomorrow.
Position Summary:
Engineer employees are represented by The Society of United Professionals, IFPTE Local 160. As an Engineer, BPV, you will assess the safety of submissions from the clients for the registration or variance to the design of pressure retaining components and systems such as boilers, pressure vessels, piping and fittings in accordance with the provincial act, regulations and adapted codes and standards.
Job Responsibilities:
Evaluate design submissions in relation to the Ontario Regulations and adapted codes and standards (CSA, ASME and ANSI) including:
Review TSSA application forms and confirm manufacturer’s qualifications such as an approved QC program
Analyze component or system’s technical drawings and calculations including performing stress calculations
Follow up with client to address outstanding information requirements or technical issues
Present and review submission with internal committees where necessary (e.g. variances)
Extend approval through issuing of CRN (Canadian Registration Number) when appropriate
Respond to client requests for consultation regarding the regulations, codes and standards
Research changes to codes + standards and share with TSSA colleagues such as other Engineers, Inspectors and Technical Specialists
Provide technical support to field staff as requested
Contribute to the creation and maintenance of internal process documentation such as SOP’s (Standard Operating Procedures) and external documents such as guidelines for industry
Actively participate in promoting public safety as a member of CSA/or ASME committees
Participate in audits of clients to ensure compliance with regulations, codes and standards
Continuously develop knowledge of components and systems design as well as applicable regulatory documentation
Job Qualifications:
Mechanical engineering degree from a Canadian university or other academic program that is recognized by the Professional Engineers of Ontario (PEO) for licensure.
P.Eng. license
3-5 years of engineering experience in a related pressure equipment industry.
Candidates with the following qualifications are preferred:
Sound knowledge of boiler and pressure vessel designs
Knowledge of the Ontario Acts, Regulations, and safety codes (CSA and ASME)
Software application proficiency in Microsoft Office, PV Elite, Turbo IX and SolidWorks
Working knowledge of welding techniques and associated metallurgy and materials

IFPTE Local 160 and TSSA
.

description:
The Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) is a not
‑
for
‑
profit regulator dedicated to enhancing public safety across Ontario. TSSA’s team of over 450 professionals delivers safety oversight across multiple regulated sectors through technical expertise, compliance, and collaboration with industry partners. At TSSA, safety is embedded in our culture and in all aspects of our work. Each role at TSSA has an impact on keeping Ontarians safe through engagement, evidence, enforcement, and education. We help build a safer community.
At TSSA, your impact is helping create a safer Ontario. As a Fuels Engineer, you'll work closely with customers and colleagues to support understanding safety requirements and promote compliance. Through collaboration, technical expertise, and problem-solving, you'll help maintain the integrity of the fuel systems that communities depend on every day. It's more than a career. It's a chance to contribute to safety in a practical and meaningful way.
Your Key Contributions:
Evaluate Compliance of Fuel Systems and Devices:
Review engineering submissions, applications, technical drawings, calculations, and supporting documentation to assess compliance with applicable legislation, regulations, and adopted codes and standards.
Support Safe Product and System Approvals
: Complete technical assessments and issue approvals, variances, registrations, and other regulatory authorizations following technical review and assessment of fuel systems, appliances, and equipment.
Provide Technical Guidance:
Respond to client, industry, and stakeholder inquiries regarding regulatory requirements, engineering standards, codes, and compliance obligations to support safe installation and operation of fuel-related equipment.
Contribute to Incident Investigations:
Collaborate with Inspectors and Investigators to assess safety incidents, determine compliance with regulatory requirements, conduct root cause analysis, and support public safety outcomes.
Advance Compliance and Risk Mitigation:
Identify and address safety concerns, including fuel appliance recalls and non-compliance matters, by communicating risks, supporting corrective actions, and promoting adherence to regulatory requirements.
Support Continuous Improvement and Knowledge Sharing:
Research emerging technologies, regulatory changes, and updates to codes and standards, while contributing to operational procedures, technical guidance documents, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
Represent TSSA and Promote Public Safety:
Participate in technical committees, industry associations, working groups, and projects to support the development of safety standards and strengthen public awareness of regulatory requirements.
Your Qualifications & Key Strengths:
Certifications:
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Chemical, or Electrical Engineering, Applied Science, or an equivalent qualification recognized by Professional Engineers Ontario (PEO), combined with a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation in good standing.
Technical Background:
Bring 3 to 5 years of engineering experience within a regulatory environment, fuel industry, consulting, or related technical field, supported by a sound understanding of fuel systems and equipment design from a mechanical, chemical, and/or electrical engineering perspective. Experience with fuel oil, propane, natural gas, pipeline, Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), and/or Hydrogen systems is considered an asset, including familiarity with the CSA B149 series, CSA B139 series, CSA Z662 and CSA B31.1/B31.3 piping systems and associated industry practices.
Regulatory & Industry Knowledge:
Demonstrate knowledge of applicable Ontario regulations, safety codes, and industry standards, including CSA codes and standards, for fuel systems and pipelines; ASME standards for power piping, process piping, hydrogen piping, and pressure vessels.
Engineering Systems & Quality Management:
Apply experience working with engineering quality management systems, engineering review processes, and electronic records management practices. Experience working within engineering management, regulatory administration, or customer relationship management platforms, such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, is considered an asset.
Engineering & Analytical Skills:
Apply strong technical analysis skills to review engineering drawings, calculations, specifications, manuals, control systems, PLC programming logic, and related documentation to assess compliance and support sound engineering decisions.
Demonstrate the ability to evaluate complex technical issues and identify safety risk.
Communication & Collaboration:
Utilize strong written and verbal communication skills to provide technical guidance, maintain accurate technical records, resolve complex compliance issues, and collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders to support public safety objectives.
Demonstrate the ability to manage multiple priorities and contribute to a professional, public safety-focused environment.

title: Inspector, Fuels
location: Peel Region, ON, Georgetown, Burlington, Oakville, Toronto West, Downtown Toronto/Etobicoke
description:
At Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA), we are deeply committed to safety and passionate about making Ontario a safer place to live, work and play. As one of Ontario’s public safety regulators, established by the provincial government, our team of more than 450 professionals administer safety regulations and enhance public safety across multiple sectors - boilers and pressure vessels and operating engineers; elevating devices, amusement devices and ski lifts; and fuels. Our people are our greatest asset and every role is vital to our vision of working together for safer communities —today and tomorrow.
At TSSA, inspectors make a difference for Ontarians every day. Out in the field, you’ll connect with regulated parties and help them meet safety requirements through your expertise and education initiatives. Your work builds trust, enhances compliance, and strengthens the systems that keep people safe. You will have a direct impact on public safety across the province, supported by a professional, collaborative, purpose-driven team.
Your Key Contributions:
Promote Public Health:
Conduct inspections of fuel facilities, equipment and other regulated sites to confirm compliance with the Technical Standards and Safety Act and its associated regulations.
Respond to Safety Incidents:
Attend and inspect incidents involving fires, explosions, carbon monoxide exposure, and public complaints to determine root causes and recommend actions that reduce the likelihood of recurrence.
Support Compliance Outcomes:
Issue orders and provide guidance to stakeholders based on the interpretation and application of fuels regulations, codes, and standards.
Maintain Accurate Regulatory Records:
Document inspection findings, incident details, and compliance data in TSSA systems to support risk-based decision-making and accurate reporting.
Contribute to Consistent Service Delivery:
Plan and schedule daily inspection activities, prepare reports within established timelines, and support audit inspections in accordance with standardized procedures.
Engage Industry and the Public:
Provide clear, timely information to certificate holders, contractors, and members of the public to build awareness of regulatory requirements and encourage safe practices.
Support a High-Performing Team:
Share technical knowledge, participate in training activities, and collaborate with colleagues to promote a cooperative and safety-focused work environment.
Your Qualifications & Key Strengths:
Certifications in Progress:
Actively pursuing or currently holding relevant fuels certifications, with a minimum qualification of Gas Technician (G2). Additional certifications are considered an asset including Oil Burner Technician (OBT2), Liquid Propane or Petroleum Mechanic (PMH/PM2/PM3).
Maintain or work toward the technical endorsements needed to inspect regulated fuels equipment in accordance with applicable codes and standards.
Technical Background:
Bring at least five years of experience in the gaseous fuels industry, supported by a strong working knowledge of the Technical Standards and Safety Act and associated fuels regulations (210/01, 212/01, 213/01, 215/01, 216/01, 217/01).
Demonstrate proficiency with fuels-related codes and standards, including CSA B149 series, the Liquid Fuels Handling Code, and CSA Z662 for oil and gas pipeline systems.
Apply strong analytical skills when conducting inspections, completing incident investigations, determining root causes, and assessing risks within regulated environments.
Use business systems to document findings, maintain accurate compliance records and support consistent service delivery.
Travel Requirements:
Daily travel required; therefore, a valid Ontario Class G driver's licence and a driving record suitable for fieldwork are essential.

title: Risk Advisor
description:
The Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) is a not‑for‑profit regulator dedicated to enhancing public safety across Ontario. TSSA’s team of over 450 professionals delivers safety oversight across multiple regulated sectors through technical expertise, compliance, and collaboration with industry partners. At TSSA, safety is embedded in our culture and in all aspects of our work. Each role at TSSA has an impact on keeping Ontarians safe through engagement, evidence, enforcement, and education. We help build a safer community.
Join TSSA’s Risk team and play a key role in advancing public safety across Ontario. As a Risk Advisor, you’ll use data, risk assessment methodologies, and analytical expertise to identify emerging safety risks and support evidence-based regulatory decisions. Your insights will help prioritize inspections, inform compliance strategies, and drive proactive actions that make a meaningful impact on public safety.
Your Key Contributions
Assess Safety Risks:
Apply risk assessment methodologies to evaluate public safety risks and support regulatory decision-making.
Analyze Risk Data:
Review incident, inspection, and operational data to identify trends, emerging risks, and key risk drivers.
Support Risk-Based Planning:
Develop and maintain risk indicators, scoring models, and prioritization tools to inform inspections and compliance activities.
Provide Risk Advice:
Review risk assessments, operational plans, and safety initiatives, providing practical recommendations to improve safety outcomes.
Support Investigations:
Facilitate In-Depth Root Cause Analyses (IDRCA) and contribute to incident investigations by identifying contributing factors and lessons learned.
Collaborate Across Teams:
Partner with Operations, Data Analytics, and other stakeholders to strengthen risk-informed decision-making and enhance analytical tools.
Document and Communicate Findings:
Prepare clear, defensible risk assessments, methodologies, and reports that support transparency and quality assurance.
Promote Continuous Improvement:
Participate in cross-functional initiatives and stay current on emerging risk management practices, regulatory trends, and public safety issues.
Your Qualifications & Key Strengths:
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or chemical engineering.
Experience:
Minimum 4 years’ experience in risk engineering including risk assessment methods, safety analysis, engineering analysis, or a related technical safety advisory role, including progressive experience supporting evaluations within a regulatory, public safety, industrial, utilities, transportation, or compliance-based decision making
Experience analyzing data, identifying trends, and developing actionable recommendations to support decision-making.
Experience facilitating discussions, risk assessment workshops, incident investigations, or stakeholder engagement activities is considered an asset
Knowledge & Skills:
Knowledge of risk management principles, methodologies (HAZOP, LOPA, SIL) and standards (e.g., ISO 31000).
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to interpret complex technical, operational, and safety-related information.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and familiarity with data visualization, reporting, or analytics tools is an asset.
Proficiency with Hazard Identification applications (FMEA Pro, PHA Pro) and familiarity with data visualization, reporting, or analytics tools is an asset.
Ability to conduct Quantitative Risk Analysis (Probabilistic Risk Assessments) such as consequence and frequency analysis and risk estimation.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work within established timelines.

title: Grants and Programs Committee Member (Volunteer)
description:
Join TAF's Grants and Programs Committee
Help Advance Climate Action in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area
The Atmospheric Fund (
TAF
) is seeking new members for its Grants and Programs Committee.
This committee plays an important role in advancing climate action across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area by reviewing funding proposals, making recommendations on funding for grants and programs that help reduce carbon emissions and support healthy, resilient communities, and providing staff with insights regarding trends, needs and opportunities for supporting climate action.
About TAF
TAF is a regional climate agency that invests in low-carbon solutions for the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area (GTHA) and helps scale them up for broad implementation. We are experienced leaders and collaborate with stakeholders in the private, public and non-profit sectors who have ideas and opportunities for reducing carbon emissions. We advance the most promising concepts by investing, providing grants, influencing policies and running programs. We’re particularly interested in ideas that offer benefits beyond carbon reduction such as improving people’s health, creating new jobs, boosting urban resiliency, and contributing to a fairer society. TAF is a proud member of the
Low Carbon Cities Canada (LC3) network
.
For the GTHA to be carbon neutral by 2050, much needs to be done, and quickly. TAF is focused on enabling the acceleration and scale-up of low-carbon solutions to reach that goal.
About the Grants and Programs Committee
The
Grants and Programs Committee
is a standing committee appointed by TAF's Board of Directors. The committee supports the Board by:
Reviewing grant and program funding proposals
Making recommendations on funding approvals and conditions
Providing strategic advice on grants and program priorities and opportunities
Supporting oversight of funded activities
Providing input to support effective program implementation
An opportunity to contribute to climate solutions
We're looking for several new members to join the Grants and Programs Committee for terms beginning in 2027.
We're particularly interested in individuals with significant professional experience (typically 5 to 10+ years) in climate solutions and related fields, including expertise in designing, funding, implementing, or scaling impactful initiatives. We welcome applications from people with a range of backgrounds and experiences, including those with expertise in one or more of the following areas:
Electric vehicles, public and active transportation
Electricity sector decarbonization
Buildings, energy efficiency, and retrofits
Market transformation and scaling solutions
Program design, delivery, and evaluation
Grantmaking and strategic funding
Finance, investment, and capital mobilization
Community engagement, community benefits, social equity, and social innovation
No one candidate is expected to bring expertise in every area. Strong committees are built on diverse perspectives and expertise, and we welcome applicants who can contribute both.
Members join a thoughtful and collaborative group of leaders and experts from across the climate sector and related fields. The committee offers a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful climate action while learning from and connecting with peers who bring a wide range of experiences and perspectives.
Time Commitment
The committee meets three times per year, with meetings typically lasting about three hours. Meetings are hybrid, and members are encouraged to attend in person if feasible. Meetings are scheduled on weekdays during business hours.
Committee members should expect to spend time reviewing meeting materials in advance. Package length varies depending on the agenda and funding proposals under consideration, and preparation time may range from a few hours to more significant review for some meetings. TAF staff prepare and distribute meeting materials, manage the grant review process, facilitate meetings, and are available support committee members as needed.
Application Process
We're using TAF's recruitment platform to support an efficient, accessible, and equitable selection process for committee appointments.
"Start your application" at the top right of this page; you'll submit your résumé and answer a short about your interest in serving on the committee and the experience, expertise, and perspectives you would bring. Your responses to these questions will be reviewed without identifying information so that reviewers can focus on your interests, experience, and perspectives. You'll also be asked a few brief administrative questions and will have the option to complete a confidential demographic survey, which is collected separately from applications and not shared with reviewers.
We encourage you to answer the questions in your own words. We're interested in hearing about your experience and perspective, not a perfect application.
Applications will be accepted until September 30, 2026. We will begin a rolling review of applications on September 21, 2026, and encourage interested candidates to apply early.
Shortlisted candidates will be invited to meet with senior TAF staff and the Committee Chair. Recommendations for appointment by to TAF's Board of Directors will be presented at the November 3, 2026 meeting; names are kept confidential until appointed. All applicants will be notified once the recruitment process is complete.

title: Intermediate Analyst, Financial Planning & Analysis
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
Reporting to the Director of Financial Planning & Analysis, the Intermediate Analyst, Financial Planning & Analysis will enable success through partnering with the business and leveraging exceptional analytical skills to utilize data and available systems to support comprehensive financial analysis. Is required to complete multiple business cases, variance analysis and participate in cross functional teams to support decision making. The position has exposure to senior leadership team.
The candidate will communicate clearly and concisely to support the development of TPA’s annual budget, monthly forecasting, and performance measurement of each business unit.  The role also supports various financial governance initiatives, monthly management reporting, and special projects as assigned. Must be comfortable to have an in-person presence, deadline focused and ability to work independently.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Prepare and present key components of the annual financial budget, monthly forecasts, and profitability of business segments
Prepare the financial models (P&L by segment) for forecasting, budgeting, scenario analyses and long-range planning.
Leverage corporate performance planning tool for end-to-end enterprise use.
Analyze financial performance against budgets/forecasts and prepare various reports in collaboration with business partners for root cause analysis.
Review ad-hoc analyses to evaluate business initiatives, strategies and cost optimization.
Review monthly capital expenditure tracking and forecasting with key stakeholders and determine risk and opportunities
Support monthly and quarterly management reporting through data mining and analyzing financial results, synthesizing key trends, and communicating business insights to senior leadership team
Analyze trends and identify risks and opportunities to support short and long-term business objectives
Build rapport and partner with business leaders, developing a highly collaborative and respectful dialogue to support the growth of the organization and delivery of services to our customers
Coordinate with City of Toronto stakeholders to provide timely monthly, quarterly and annual financials and supporting schedules
Other duties as assigned
QUALIFICATIONS

title: Sr Manager, EV Network Development
description:

Reporting to the Director, Parking Development, the Senior Manager, EV Development is responsible for leading the strategic growth, operational performance, expansion, and commercialization of the Toronto Parking Authority's EV charging business. The position provides overall leadership for EV charging network planning, deployment, operations, partnerships, technology platforms, customer experience, revenue growth, and capital programs.
The Senior Manager will develop and execute TPA's EV charging strategy, oversee the growth and performance of the Green P EV charging network, and ensure successful delivery of infrastructure expansion projects, technology integrations, utility initiatives, and strategic partnerships. Working closely with Operations, Technology, Finance, and external stakeholders, the role will support TPA's transformation into a leading mobility services provider while delivering strong customer, operational, environmental, and financial outcomes.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Product Management and Execution
Develop and execute TPA's EV charging strategy and multi-year roadmap, including network expansion, customer products, technology enhancements, and revenue growth initiatives.
Lead planning, prioritization, business case development, and execution of EV charging infrastructure projects across TPA facilities and partner sites.
Execute on key strategic initiatives to deliver superior experiences that bridge the digital and physical worlds, empowering customers to engage with the TPA across multiple channels to drive revenues and enhance customer experiences.
Oversee development and implementation of public charging programs including Level 2 charging, fast charging hubs, fleet charging opportunities, and future mobility solutions.
Lead strategic partnerships with charge point operators, utilities, technology providers, government agencies, and other industry stakeholders.
Manage EV charging network growth initiatives, including site selection, deployment planning, commercialization strategies, and utilization optimization.
Oversee all EV-related procurement activities, including development of Scope of Work documentation, Requests for Proposal (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), Expressions of Interest (EOIs), and contract negotiations.
Lead implementation of customer-facing technologies, payment platforms, software integrations, roaming relationships, and digital products that improve customer experience and operational efficiencies.
Represent TPA in industry working groups, utility consultations, regulatory discussions, pilot programs, and stakeholder committees related to EV charging and transportation electrification
Coordinate approvals and stakeholder engagement activities with City divisions, external agencies, utilities, councillor offices, and Business Improvement Areas as required.
People Leadership
Provide leadership, direction, coaching, and performance management to the Manager, EV Charging Operations and Lead, EV Network Development.
Establish goals, priorities, and performance expectations aligned with departmental and corporate objectives.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, customer service, and continuous improvement.
Lead cross-functional teams and external consultants in the delivery of strategic EV initiatives.
Build and maintain strong working relationships across Operations, Technology, Finance, Marketing, and external stakeholders.
Identify resource requirements and engage external resources or consultants as required to support project delivery.
Reporting and Insights
Develop and monitor EV charging business KPIs, operational metrics, throughput targets, revenue forecasts, service level standards, and customer experience measures.
Analyze charging network performance, transaction trends, customer behavior, pricing effectiveness, asset utilization, and operational efficiency.
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting on business performance, strategic initiatives, capital projects, and operational outcomes.
Use data analytics and business intelligence tools to support investment decisions, network optimization, and strategic planning.
Identify opportunities to improve charger reliability, customer satisfaction, network utilization, and financial performance.
Financial and Commercial Management
Accountable for management of EV business unit operating and capital budgets, forecasts, and financial performance.
Lead annual business planning, operating budget preparation, and capital investment planning for EV charging programs.
Develop revenue growth strategies and identify cost optimization opportunities across the EV portfolio.
Lead funding applications, grant programs, incentive opportunities, and reimbursement claims in collaboration with Finance and external agencies.
Support long-term EV business case development and investment planning activities.

Minimum three (3) years’ experience in EV charging, mobility, retail, digital and/or omnichannel experience.
Broad knowledge in the field of product management, e-commerce and digital programs is an asset.
Sound knowledge of procurement processes and contract management.
Sound understanding of Change Management practices, and ability to partner with and influence individuals and cross-functional teams.
Ability to execute high-level program planning and think strategically; outstanding problem-solving skills grounded in data and consumer insights and understand how to incorporate analytics into project requirements.
Excellent communication, presentation, collaboration and influencing skills across internal and external stakeholder relationships. Ability to be persuasive, motivational, and persistent as needed.
Strong team leader/player who can foster productive friction, create a great place to work and holds themselves to the highest accountability and commitment.
Customer-centric approach to delivering great service to customers and stakeholders.
Ability to evaluate business trends and competitive landscape and modify business strategies accordingly.
Demonstrated effective management of P&Ls, targets, budgets combined with strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to plan and prioritize; has strong financial and proforma modeling skills.
Strong commitment to the organization’s Core Values and cultural change.
Ability to perform effectively in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment.

This position will assist and provide support in implementing the approved Strategic Plan.

description:

We’re here to help. When an injury or illness happens on the job, we move quickly to provide wage-loss benefits, medical coverage and support to help people get back to work. wsib.ca

Shape the Future of Workplace Insurance in Ontario
At WSIB, actuarial work goes far beyond traditional insurance valuation. Our team plays a critical role in ensuring the long-term financial sustainability of Ontario's workplace insurance system while helping support over five million workers and hundreds of thousands of employers across the province.
As an
Actuarial Consultant
, you'll work on complex, meaningful projects that directly influence funding strategies, premium rate setting, benefit liability valuations, forecasting, legislative costing, and financial decision-making at an enterprise level. As a member of the Actuarial leadership team, you'll collaborate with senior leaders including Directors and Chief Actuary, business partners, government stakeholders, auditors, and fellow actuarial professionals to deliver insights that help guide the future of workers' compensation in Ontario.
Why Join WSIB's Actuarial Team?
Our actuarial team offers a unique opportunity to work on highly specialized casualty and social insurance challenges that are rarely found elsewhere. We are deeply committed to supporting professional growth and development. Whether you're continuing your actuarial journey or looking to expand your leadership capabilities, you'll have opportunities to work alongside experienced actuarial professionals, lead complex projects, build expertise in workers' compensation insurance, and contribute to innovative actuarial solutions that have real public impact.
What You'll Be Doing
Actuarial Leadership & Technical Expertise
Lead or contribute to the review and delivery of complex actuarial work while ensuring accuracy, quality, and timely execution of key initiatives.
Provide guidance on actuarial methods, models, assumptions, and analytical approaches.
Review and validate actuarial calculations, model outputs, and project deliverables for accuracy and reasonableness.
Ensure project milestones and timelines are achieved.
Lead or contribute to:
Valuation of benefit liabilities (Schedule 1 and Schedule 2).
Schedule 1 premium rate setting and Schedule 2 administration rate setting.
Funding and financial forecasting initiatives.
Development and enhancement of actuarial methodologies and models.
Prepare reports, recommendations, and actuarial analyses for the Director
s
& Chief Actuary and actuarial senior leadership.
Stay current with evolving actuarial standards, industry practices, and WSIB policies.
Present actuarial findings, estimates, methodologies, and recommendations to internal and external stakeholders.
Participate in stakeholder meetings, presentations, information sessions, and consultations.
Experience Studies, Costing & Special Projects
Lead or participate in analytical studies and strategic actuarial initiatives that support funding, pricing, valuation, and policy decision-making.
Design, review, validate, and report on actuarial experience studies used to establish or validate model assumptions.
Conduct and support studies related to:
Mortality
Claim termination patterns
Occupational disease claims
Health care costs
Future administration expenses
Economic and financial assumptions
Perform actuarial costing of legislative, policy, and operational changes.
Support development of presentations and materials for:
WSIB Senior Leadership
Board of Directors
Government stakeholders
Employers and external actuarial advisors
Contribute to special projects involving:
Enhancements to actuarial models
Earnings by source analysis
New funding and pricing methodologies
Accounting standard implementation
Process modernization initiatives
Project Leadership
Manage projects from planning through execution while coordinating the work of actuarial team members and ensuring high-quality outcomes.
Develop project plans, schedules, and deliverables.
Coordinate project activities and assign work across team members.
Identify resource requirements and support workload planning.
Monitor progress through regular project updates and status reviews.
Review team deliverables to ensure technical accuracy and quality standards are met.
Drive projects to successful completion within established timelines.
Stakeholder Collaboration & Relationship Management
Build strong relationships across the organization and externally to support actuarial initiatives and informed decision-making.
Partner with leaders and teams across Operations, Strategy, Finance, Technology.
Collaborate with employers, worker representatives, auditors, actuarial consultants, and other external stakeholders.
Maintain active involvement in actuarial professional organizations and industry networks.
Liaise with workers' compensation boards, government agencies, health and safety organizations, and industry groups to stay informed on emerging trends and developments impacting workers' compensation and actuarial practice.
What You'll Bring
Required Qualifications
University degree in
Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics
, or a related discipline.
5+ years of actuarial experience
within the insurance industry, workers' compensation, pension, consulting, or a similar environment.
2-5 years of experience leading projects, initiatives, or project teams.
Strong analytical, modeling, forecasting, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities, including presenting complex actuarial concepts to diverse audiences.
Required Professional Designation
You must hold one of the following actuarial fellowship designations:
FCIA
(Fellow of the Canadian Institute of Actuaries)
FSA
(Fellow of the Society of Actuaries)
FCAS
(Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society)
What Makes This Opportunity Different
This is not a typical actuarial role. At WSIB, you'll work on complex social insurance and workers' compensation challenges that combine actuarial science, public purpose, financial sustainability, and real-world impact. The recommendations and analyses you provide help shape funding decisions, premium rates, benefit liabilities, and long-term financial strategy for one of Ontario's largest insurance systems. This is an exciting opportunity to join a dedicated team within Ombudsman Toronto and advance the City of Toronto’s commitment to establishing a right to adequate housing. If you are passionate about fairness, equity, and overcoming systemic discrimination hurdles in the City’s treatment of people who are living in housing precarity, this may be the job for you.
Ombudsman Toronto operates independently of City Council and the City administration. Staff of Ombudsman Toronto report directly or indirectly to the Ombudsman, an independent Officer of City Council.
Position Summary
To provide senior-level decision support and coordination to the Deputy Ombudsman and Senior Leadership Team (SLT) on the management of business and corporate service functions, ensuring the organization has the operational infrastructure to deliver its mandate. This role is responsible for managing finances, human resources, organizational planning, contracts and operations to ensure the organization operates efficiently, with accountability and in accordance with strategic objectives.
The Impact You’ll Make
As the Manager, Business Services, you will provide senior-level decision support and coordination, overseeing all business, administrative and operational functions that enable Ombudsman Toronto to effectively deliver on its mandate.
In this role, you will provide confidential strategic advice on complex issues, support organizational excellence, prepare reports, briefing notes and correspondence for senior executives on a variety of sensitive matters, and develop and implement plans and policies that support Ombudsman Toronto's strategic goals. You will also help ensure that equity and inclusion goals are advanced across policies and programs while leading the implementation of the current strategic plan and identifying solutions for business transformation in response to evolving and changing needs.
You will lead transformation and organizational change initiatives that improve service levels to the public through developing project plans, timelines, budgets, milestones and deliverables. You will lead or coordinate project and operational initiatives involving staff, contractors and other stakeholders, and participate in identifying and measuring operational performance standards while making recommendations for improvement.
You will foster effective teamwork, high standards of work quality and organizational performance, continuous learning and innovation. Responsibilities include overseeing day-to-day staff operations, scheduling, assigning and reviewing work, and providing general coordination of staff without direct authority to complete projects and recommendations on complex, sensitive matters.
You will develop, recommend and administer the annual budget for the office, ensuring expenditures remain within approved budget limitations. A key part of this role is to coordinate finances, facilities, equipment, supplies, technology and other operational resources, and together with other managers develop initiatives that improve efficiency and reduce costs associated with ineffective practices or policies, including with respect to data management.
Working with People & Equity (P&E), you will provide advice on corporate human resource and employment policies, ensure compliance with same, coordinate recruitment initiatives for hiring managers, and provide guidance regarding corporate policies, procedures and legislative regulations to all levels of staff. You will also be responsible for procurement, contract and vendor management, collaborate with Purchasing & Materials Management to ensure compliance with corporate procurement processes. In addition, you will establish and foster communications and linkages with other City entities, participate in various internal working groups and committees, and maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry-specific developments and best practices and procedures for operational effectiveness.
Key Qualifications
Post-secondary education in a discipline pertinent to the job function (e.g., Public Administration) or an approved combination of education and experience.
Extensive experience leading programs, projects or initiatives at the senior level, paired with strong project management skills.
Considerable experience providing strategic advice to senior leaders in areas of policy and/or issues management.
Considerable people management experience, including experience leading, motivating and developing a team of staff, supporting and promoting an inclusive and respectful workplace culture.
Considerable experience conducting research, analyzing complex data, interpreting and summarizing information to support decision-making; as well as experience preparing plans and comprehensive reports, paired with advanced MS Office Suite proficiency (specifically MS Excel, OneNote and PowerPoint).
Understanding of administrative fairness and human rights in service delivery and Ombudsman office operations.
Demonstrated experience in public procurement processes, as well as managing and delivering projects while maintaining budgetary control and ensuring expenditures remain within approved budgets.
Excellent analytical skills, strategic advice and ability to deliver results.
Excellent ability to problem-solve and make timely and well-informed decisions.
Ability to react quickly to changing situations and demands, manage competing priorities, and meet tight timelines.
Ability to consistently exercise and display sound judgment, integrity, and discretion.
Exceptional communication skills with demonstrated experience in working independently and as part of a team.

Reporting to the Supervisor, Epidemiology and Data Analytics Unit, the Senior Health Information Analyst provides expertise and support to programs in Toronto Public Health including advice and support related to the collection, analysis, interpretation and reporting of surveillance data, as well as providing expertise and leadership for quality controls and mechanisms related to public health data.
The Senior Health Information Analyst is a key role within the Epidemiology and Data Analytics Unit, providing leadership on quality initiatives, developing and implementing new surveillance products, evaluating existing products, and identifying opportunities to enhance and streamline the work of the team.
The ideal candidate will possess strong data analysis, dashboard creation and statistical reporting skills, project management expertise, and be able to work effectively in a dynamic environment where the priorities frequently shift to address current priorities.
Major Responsibilities:
Designs, develops, and prepares new health status and operational reports, health information systems, processes, dashboards and databases.

Extracts, manages, analyzes, interprets and reports data using appropriate methods to support timely surveillance and reporting for health status data.

Applies proven analytical approaches to identify errors or limitations in data and implements processes and to improve data validity.
Recommends strategies to resolve or mitigate the impact of identified data quality issues.
Provides on-the-job instruction to staff concerning the input, or preparation for input, of surveillance data.
Provides support and consultation to divisional programs and services
Represents the division on internal and external committees dealing with communicable disease data and health status information.

Orients staff to available databases and the use of population health information in programme development, monitoring and evaluation.

Works collaboratively to confirm data requirements and identifies appropriate methods for collecting and analyzing health data for TPH staff, managers, and other internal and external clients.
Uses project management tools and approaches to monitor the progress of large- and small-scale projects, identifies barriers to meet timelines and project goals, and proposes solutions.
Responds to requests for public health data and information.
Liaises with City departments and external agencies to obtain and/or share health related data.

Your application must describe your qualifications as they relate to:
University degree in Health Sciences, Public Health, Health Informatics, Biostatistics, or a related discipline.
Extensive experience using statistical software to analyze large health data sets, including SAS, R, STATA, PYTHON, or equivalent.
Considerable experience applying population health statistical methods and, in the collection, analysis, communication, and interpretation of public health data.
Considerable experience using Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Access, as well as data visualization tools such as Tableau. Power BI and ArcGIS.

Experience working with communicable diseases preferred.
Strong customer service, communication, and consulting skills.

Strong analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex datasets and develop practical recommendations.

Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and meet deadlines.

The division also directly operates early learning and child care programs through the City’s Toronto Early Learning & Child Care Services (TELCCS).
The Health and Safety Officer  provides leadership, expertise and consultation services to Toronto Children's Services management and staff in matters of occupational health, safety and wellness by developing effective policy, programs, education and communications leading to a positive health and safety culture and injury reduction.
Major Responsibilities:
Contributes to the development and implementation of and is responsible for the maintenance of a comprehensive divisional Health, Safety and Wellness Program in association with corporate, union and divisional stakeholders.
Responsible as the division lead for corporate health and safety initiatives, in the areas of integrated disability management, occupational health and safety policies, procedures and programs, and workplace wellness consistent with all provincial and municipal legislation.
Leads the divisional joint Health and Safety Committee and working group. Provides expert advice, guidance and consultation on all areas within health and safety, such as infection control requirements, workplace incident reporting, and return to work practices.
Governs and develops health, safety and wellness initiatives and targets for over 40 work locations, including on-site specific consultation and audits.

Manages the development and facilitation of the annual divisional health and safety recognition conference.
Prepares, maintains and submits up to date documentation, where required by the Ministry of Labour (MOL), Toronto Public Health (TPH), or other regulatory bodies, to demonstrate that Toronto Children’s Services meets regulatory requirements.
Initiates, builds and maintains relationships with internal and external partners in order to develop, facilitate and promote occupational health and safety, and workplace wellness.
Develops divisional policies and procedures; designs, implements, maintains and evaluates performance related to health, safety and wellness initiatives. Recommends and implements corrective actions/activities to support continues improvement.
Regularly collects and analyzes health and safety workplace incident data, prepares reports and presents to senior management and all workers; develops and implements improvements to ensure targets are met.
Leads and organizes divisional working groups in the development of policies and programs as related to occupational health, safety and wellness.
Assesses and reports on emerging health, safety, infection control and wellness case law and legislative changes, and initiates corresponding Toronto Children’s Services actions including updates to policies and procedures.
Identifies and analyzes health, safety and wellness training needs and, through leadership and consultation, develops, designs and delivers training/workshops, team building and education programs to meet divisional and organizational needs.
Develops, implements and recommends blended learning approaches to support diverse staffing needs and divisional priorities.

Considerable experience providing consultation, guidance and direction to management and staff regarding compliance, accountability, and best practices relevant to occupational health and safety, and workplace wellness in a unionized environment.
Considerable experience in the development and delivery of health, safety and wellness programs and training, including conducting needs assessments.
Experience conducting research and analysis, assessing compliance, developing and implementing recommendations, and writing operational policy and guidelines consistent with relevant health, safety and wellness legislation and best practices.

The Vision Zero Strategy unit in Transportation Services leads the development, operationalization, and evaluation of transportation safety initiatives that support the City of Toronto's Vision Zero Road Safety Plan. The unit is responsible for advancing evidence-based policies, programs, engineering countermeasures, and operational strategies aimed at eliminating traffic-related fatalities and serious injuries. Working collaboratively with internal divisions, external agencies, academic partners, consultants, and community stakeholders, the unit develops and evaluates innovative road safety solutions, conducts research and data-driven analysis, oversees pilot projects and strategic studies, and leads the development of policies, guidelines, standards, and performance measures that improve safety for all road users. The unit plays a key role in translating technical evidence into actionable recommendations, supporting informed decision-making and continuous improvement of Toronto's road safety programs and practices.
The Project Manager will report to the unit Manager, Sheyda Saneinejad. They may be assigned to projects in any part of the unit’s portfolio as described above. In some cases the Project Manager will be leading or co-leading a project, in other cases the Project Manager may serve as a supportive team member on a project led by another person or unit. Given the nature of the Vision Zero portfolio positive collaboration with other units and sections is the key to success of this unit and the City’s Road Safety Plan.
Major Responsibilities:
The primary functions associated with this position include, but are not limited to the following:
Project Management
Leads the development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of projects and programs in a manner that is consistent with best practices and negotiated contracts, as well as City policies, plans, and strategies.
Leads stakeholder engagement with staff of other City divisions, agencies, boards, commissions, community groups, academic institutions, consultants, industry partners and other levels of government on projects, studies, policies and strategic initiatives.
Leads, coordinates and/or provides input on procurement processes, including preparation of purchase documents, evaluation of bids and submissions, recommendations for award, negotiation, and execution of contracts. Leads and supports multidisciplinary transportation safety projects involving policy development, engineering countermeasures, transportation operations, research, data analysis and program evaluation.
Develops and coordinates new Service Level Agreements, Project Charters and other Inter-Divisional Agreements.
Reviews, tracks, evaluates and is accountable for the work performance of external service providers, including oversight of consultant-led technical studies, research projects, pilot initiatives, data collection programs and evaluation activities; ensures project objectives, schedules, deliverables and budgets are achieved.
Ensures that the project expenditures are controlled and maintained within approved budget limitations, processed and documented in compliance with City and Division policy as well as the Construction Act, and are tracked according to spend rates.
Develops business cases, policy recommendations, technical guidance and strategic advice for senior management based on research findings, project outcomes and transportation safety evidence.
Technical
Knowledge
Conducts technical problem investigations, performs site visits and inspections, participates in conducting studies and commenting on technical reports (including drawings and specifications), and provides detailed recommendations and advice that is in alignment with municipal best practices, industry guidelines, and applicable regulations.
Conducts project-specific and ongoing technical research into assigned areas, including road safety policies, emerging transportation technologies, human factors, transportation operations, Vision Zero best practices, and innovative approaches being implemented in peer jurisdictions.
Maintains state-of-practice knowledge in field of work, such as complete streets, safe systems and transportation planning, including comparable peer cities and regulatory proposals and changes by other levels of government that may impact the City of Toronto.
Assesses current practices and improves procedures and protocols in collaboration with City divisions through comprehensive knowledge of City Policies and Guidelines.
Leads or supports the design, implementation and evaluation of pilot projects and innovative transportation safety initiatives using quantitative and qualitative performance measures.
Analyzes transportation, collision and operational data to identify trends, evaluate program effectiveness and support evidence-based decision making.
Leads or participates in the development and review of policies, standards, guidelines, procedures and performance measures related to road safety, transportation operations and multimodal mobility.
Teamwork and Supervision
Works with interdivisional, interdisciplinary and interagency teams and consultation processes to plan toward and support project and program delivery while addressing political, community, business and other stakeholder interests.
Embraces diversity and inclusion, fosters teamwork and a positive workplace culture through cooperation, collaboration, and maintaining constructive and respectful relationships.
Provides work direction to assigned project team members and junior staff including the scheduling, assigning and reviewing of tasks and task-specific training and coaching, as needed.
Ensures compliance with the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act and all other related provincial regulations and corporate and divisional safety standards and procedures.
Communication and Reporting
Prepares and delivers briefings to senior management in the Transportation Services division and individual members of City Council, drafts staff reports and presentations for management review and submission to City Council and its Committees, and drafts correspondence for a variety of audiences.
Prepares and delivers communication and engagement plans for internal and external stakeholders, including websites and (social) media strategy.
Represents the Transportation Services division or City of Toronto when communicating with elected officials and members of the public, at meetings with stakeholders, when participating in working groups and committees, as well as when coordinating and collaborating with peer cities, other levels of government, and technical associations.
Key Qualifications:
Your application must describe your qualifications as they relate to:
Post-secondary education in a discipline pertinent to the job function (e.g. planning, engineering, economics, business, environmental science,  public policy) or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Considerable experience in project management, delivering assignments from inception through to implementation
and evaluation with minimal direction while balancing competing stakeholder interests, political considerations, operational requirements and strategic objectives.
Considerable experience in the field of road safety and one or more of the following areas: road safety policy and program development, traffic operations, transportation planning, transportation engineering, Complete Streets Design,  , Safe System
transportation research, program evaluation, infrastructure planning and implementation
or equivalent initiatives which evaluate options and facilitate decision-making for making changes to public streets.
Experience managing consultant assignments, technical studies, pilot projects, research partnerships or other complex multi-stakeholder initiatives.
Experience interpreting and presenting technical, operational and analytical information to diverse audiences including senior management, technical staff and external stakeholders.
Strong knowledge of Vision Zero principles, Safe System approaches, transportation safety performance measurement, program evaluation methodologies, transportation analytics and emerging mobility technologies.
Working knowledge of policies and regulations governing the street network, including but not limited to: Provincial policies and plans; Highway Traffic Act; Toronto Official Plan; Toronto Traffic By-Law; all applicable design guidelines.
Highly developed interpersonal skills with emphasis on communication (written/oral; speaking/listening), conflict resolution, and political acumen.
Excellent skills in delivering presentations, building and maintaining relationships, and resolving conflicts.
Effective leadership and team-building skills, and the ability to provide work direction to project team members, contractors, and staff in a unionized environment.
Proficiency in MS Office (i.e. Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and online meeting platforms (e.g. WebEx). Clients have the right to appeal decisions made about the amount of assistance or benefits they are eligible to receive.
Reporting to the Manager, Program Support of TESS's Quality Control & Assurance Section, Case Presenters are an essential part of the Division in defending eligibility decisions by preparing oral and written submissions and making presentations to the Social Benefits Tribunal (SBT). Case presenters provide analytical expertise, advice, guidance and recommendations on issues pertaining to eligibility for social assistance, Divisional and Provincial policies and the application of various laws to those issues.
Major Responsibilities:
Provides analysis, expertise, consultation, guidance and formulations of creative solutions on cases that are under appeal to ensure that the eligibility decision adheres to Ontario Works Act, Legislation and City policies. Make recommendations when a decision is challenged and provide advice on how to resolve the matter in compliance with existing policies, procedures, and guidelines. Breakdown complex information to communicate with clients and stakeholders in plain, simple language.
Defends the Division's position on eligibility decisions affecting entitlement for social assistance. Prepares written and oral submissions to represent the City and defend eligibility decisions at the SBT. Liaise with internal and external stakeholders including clients, staff of all levels, and the legal community to achieve desired results.
Supports, challenges, and cross-examines testimony and evidence presented before Tribunals, Boards, and the courts. Identifies, organizes, and participates in pre-hearing teleconferences, early resolution processes, and related proceedings. Provides guidance and preparation to local office staff and third-party witnesses appearing before these bodies, as appropriate. Acts as a witness and represents the City's interests in civil and criminal court proceedings when required.
Identifies appeals, including Human Rights challenges that cannot be resolved. Recommends to Senior Management whether representation is required at the Tribunal and Board and plans strategies to defend cases. Liaise and collaborate with other staff to effect timely completion of any eligibility reassessments, corrections, or case management actions that impact the client's entitlement to assistance.
Reviews files and staff's written submissions and ensures eligibility decisions meet Divisional policies and Provincial directives, are consistent with social assistance legislation, tenets of Natural Justice, provincial and federal privacy laws and rules of evidence requirements. Validate and calculate overpayments to ensure that the correct amount of assistance was issued according to eligibility and legislative requirements.
Identifies trends, themes and cases of general importance and other decisions of the Tribunal and Board that impact on Divisional policies and procedures. Discusses key observations with the Division's solicitor where appropriate. Provides recommendations to unit Senior Management.
Reviews unsuccessful Tribunal decisions and assesses for fairness and errors and, identifies those cases requiring applications for reconsideration. Prepares and files written submissions and responses to the Tribunal and Board and client, lawyer or legal representatives.
Performs quality control functions for the Division. Ensures compliance with appeals processes and procedures and general program file requirements. Researches, drafts and submits information/recommendations to various levels of management and the Division for amendments or changes to support consistent application of policy and improved outcomes.
Compiles, researches, and assesses precedent setting jurisprudence related to Tribunal and Board decisions, Provincial and Federal legislation, Provincial directives, and Divisional policies. Incorporates these principles and findings in oral and written submissions before the Tribunal and Board to enhance the successful defense of cases. Seek creative solutions and ways to bring about early resolution to reduce ambiguity for the client and administrative pressures on the parties.
Develops and provides manuals and training to the Appeals Review Unit and Divisional staff to promote and maintain a skilled and knowledgeable workforce. Provides information and advice to other units within the Division.
Participates on various internal and external committees for the section and represents the unit as required.
Acts/serves as a witness on behalf of the City for civil and criminal court proceedings, as required.
Provides information and responds to inquiries and requests from Division's legal counsel on appeals related issues.
Requests legal advice from Division's legal counsel.
Key Qualifications:
Considerable experience working in a regulatory environment interpreting and applying policy and legislation, researching, and analyzing case files and preparing supporting documentation to defend a position in relation to relevant legislation.
Considerable experience in exercising critical judgement, analysis, and providing alternative solutions and negotiating resolutions.
Experience in advocacy and dispute resolution, including the ability to present persuasive arguments, make recommendations to management, committees, tribunals and similar bodies, and respond effectively, both verbally and in writing.
Experience incorporating equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility principles into service delivery and eligibility assessments to promote equitable outcomes and compliance with legislative and policy requirements.
You must also have:
Proven political acumen and the ability to navigate complex landscapes, effectively managing competing goals and priorities, consulting and problem solving while maintaining positive working relationships.
Demonstrated experience in digital-first environment, including use of web and teleconferencing applications (such as WebEx, Zoom, MS Teams), and email and messaging systems (such as MS Outlook).
Knowledge of the Ontario Works Act and Regulations, provincial social assistance directives, Social Benefits Tribunal Rules of Procedure and Practice Directions, the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (MFIPPA), and their application in the delivery and administration of municipal social assistance programs.
Ability to identify emerging issues, prioritize, and where appropriate, escalate to management, and apply any relevant solutions.
Ability to review and provide subject matter context on judicial decisions, including Social Benefits Tribunal decisions, and policy interpretation pertaining to OW eligibility and potential trends and impacts.
Strong ability to effectively manage varied workload with impeccable organizational skills, while contributing to overall teams’ success in meeting program service delivery requirements.
Exemplifies Toronto Public Service Values including providing exceptional client service and carrying out duties with broader City objectives in mind.
Demonstrated ability to utilize conflict resolution, mediation, and negotiation skills to assist and promote settlement of disagreements in formal and informal settings.

Job Description
Reporting to the Senior Project Manager, Energy Unit, CPDD, the Project Manager Capital Projects & Initiatives will provide project management leadership and support on energy and carbon-reduction initiatives and projects including renovation and retrofit projects for P&R Division. The Project Manager will assist other project leads to complete a high-level electrical servicing and distribution analysis to prepare proper scope and budget during the project initiation phase.
The Project Manager will review the state-of-good-repair (SOGR) capital program and identify fuel switching scope, energy efficiency improvements, solar PV opportunities and other opportunities and ensure the scope and budget in the capital align with City's Energy Transition Plan and other policies such as TransformTO, the Toronto Green Standard, and Net Zero targets.
Major Responsibilities:
Project Management and Support:
Lead and support the planning and implementation of energy driven capital projects (e.g., fuel switching, renewable installations, deep retrofits) from inception to completion, ensuring budget, scope, and schedule compliance. Develops and implements project control systems, cost evaluation methodologies, performance evaluation criteria, in accordance with approved corporate policies and guidelines.
Technical Oversight:
Review and provide comments/ recommendations pertaining to mechanical, electrical, and architectural drawings, specifications and construction documents to ensure feasibility and alignment with transition goals; identify opportunities for efficiency improvements and low-carbon technologies. Negotiates innovative solutions to complex project challenges involving multiple stakeholders to achieve City's objectives.
Asset Management:
Conduct comprehensive energy assessments, assist project leads in preparing electrical upgrade scope, project future energy consumption and assist in planning capital program to achieve net-zero, and develop long-term (5-10 year) capital transition plans.
Energy and Carbon Data Analysis & Reporting:
Conduct analysis of energy and carbon to assess consumption, GHG emissions, project performance and savings from efficiency projects as per International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP) and ensuring compliance with Ontario Regulation 25/23. Prioritize energy efficiency projects and investments based on detailed analysis and cost-benefit analysis.
Stakeholder Engagement:
Liaise with Division staff, other City Divisions, agencies, boards, community groups, funding bodies, consultants, and authorities as required to support transition goals. Identify various grants and champion the application process.
Procurement & Contract Management:
Prepare RFPs, tender documents, and technical specifications; evaluate bids; supervise contractor performance; manage disputes and claims.
Policy & Program Development:
Support policy recommendations, funding strategies, outreach initiatives and the development of standard operating procedures related to the implementation of the Energy Transition Plan; provide technical guidance on the implementation of energy and carbon related initiatives.
Compliance & Safety:
Ensure adherence to legislation, building codes, corporate standards, and health & safety regulations; track infractions and support litigation as needed.
Leadership:
Supervise staff, consultants, and contractors on a project basis; foster collaboration, high performance, and continuous learning. Supervises and coordinates the day to day operation of all assigned project staff including the scheduling, assigning and reviewing of work.
Budgets:
Develops, recommends, administers, monitors and reconciles project budgets, and ensures that the project expenditures are controlled and maintained within approved budget limitations.
Key Qualifications:
Post-secondary education in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Building Science or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Energy Manager (CEM), (P.Eng.) designation in Ontario (mechanical/electrical discipline), CMVP and/or LEED credentials are an asset.
Experience leading and supporting large scale energy, decarbonization and Net-Zero capital projects through the full project lifecycle, including feasibility studies, design & construction, cost estimation, budgeting, procurement, commissioning, closeout and post-implementation performance.
Experience supporting project delivery, procurement, consultant and stakeholder coordination, and risk management, with strong communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.
Experience identifying, evaluating and implementing decarbonization measures such as fuel switching, deep energy retrofits, and other energy conservative measures, including integration with SOGR and long term capital plan.
Experience analyzing energy and GHG data, including benchmarking, baseline, avoided energy and emissions, lifecycle analysis and business case development for energy and carbon-reduction initiatives.
Experience applying measurement and verification (M&V) principles, including IPMVP, performance tracking, and verification of energy, GHG and cost savings. Proficiency with RETScreen, EnergyPlus, IES VE or equivalent tools.
Familiar with relevant energy and building codes, standards, and regulatory requirements, including IS0 50001, ASHRAE standards, Ontario building code, and applicable electrical / TSSA requirements.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a new campus recruitment team within the People & Equity Division. Reporting to the Senior Campus Recruitment Lead, the Consultant, Campus Recruitment will connect students, recent graduates and people early in their careers with meaningful opportunities at the City.
Through campus recruitment and outreach, you'll strengthen student experiences and develop inclusive talent pipelines that support workforce needs and equity goals. Guided by a student-first approach, you'll help shape programs and experiences and build trusted relationships across campuses and communities.
You'll advance equitable and accessible hiring by identifying and reducing barriers, using data and feedback to improve outcomes. Working collaboratively across the organization, you'll bring people together around shared goals, while demonstrating care and integrity throughout your work.
What You'll Do
Early-Career Talent Attraction
You'll support campus recruitment and talent attraction activities for students, recent graduates, and people early in their careers.
Coordinate recruitment and outreach activities for student, intern, co-op and entry-level roles.
Provide guidance on recruitment cycles, timelines, talent streams, inclusive assessment materials and accessible hiring practices.
Use targeted sourcing and research to identify diverse talent and maintain talent pools that support current and future workforce needs.
Embed equity-informed and accessible practices throughout the work to strengthen access to opportunities for members of equity-deserving communities.
Campus and Early-Career Programs
Supporting the City's campus and early-career programs will be a key part of the role. This includes student placements, co-ops, internships, new-graduate initiatives, rotational programs, and the City's Unpaid Student Placement Program.
Collaborate with City divisions and post-secondary institutions to coordinate program timelines and requirements, onboarding and orientation, mentorship connections and evaluations.
