Toronto is home to more than 3 million people whose diversity and experiences make this great city Canada’s leading economic engine and one of the world’s most diverse and livable cities. As the fourth largest city in North America, Toronto is a global leader in technology, finance, film, music, culture, innovation and climate action, and consistently places at the top of international rankings due to investments championed by its government, residents and businesses.  The City of Toronto is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment where all employees and members of the public feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of the public and the communities in which we live and serve.
The Communications Division plays a vital role in connecting the City of Toronto with residents, staff, and key stakeholders by delivering clear, impactful messaging about City programs, services, and priorities. Operating with an agency-like model, the division develops and executes integrated marketing and communications campaigns that drive measurable results. Through a centralized, centres-of-excellence approach, the Communications team fosters a culture of growth, collaboration, and innovation, empowering staff to tell proactive, compelling stories that place the city and its divisions at the heart of public engagement.
The Communications Division also supports issues management, media relations and crisis communications, helping the City anticipate emerging issues and coordinate timely, accurate responses across divisions. All communications efforts are strategically aligned with the City's broader organizational goals, ensuring consistency, relevance, and meaningful impact across all channels.
About the Role
Reporting to the Director, Media Relations and Issues Management, the Manager Communications, Issues Management role plays a critical part in shaping how the City anticipates, responds to, and communicates about sensitive, high-profile, cross-divisional and intergovernmental matters. You’ll provide senior-level strategic advice and operational support to the City Manager, Deputy City Managers, division heads, and senior leadership teams, working closely with the Chief Communications Officer, the Communications Management Team, and the Mayor’s Office.
This is a unique opportunity to build and lead a team focused on proactive issues management, developing strategies and action plans that reflect the City’s values and priorities while helping protect its reputation and foster public trust. You’ll be responsible for setting the direction for this new unit in the Media Relations & Issues Management Centre of Excellence, guiding coordinated responses to complex and politically sensitive issues, and ensuring communications are timely, accurate, and aligned with broader organizational goals.
Your team will be responsible for:
Managing cross-divisional and large-scale reputational risks to enhance and protect the City’s public image
Preparing Communications senior leadership for Council and Committee meetings through detailed briefings on emerging issues and ongoing campaigns
Providing insight and analysis on politically sensitive items to inform issues management and communications strategies and leadership briefings
Ensuring timely and strategic decision-making through accurate tracking, documentation, and reporting on issues, reports, and policy matters
Championing continuous improvement of the forecasting process by leveraging data, trends, and feedback
Developing a proactive strategy that includes social listening, crisis response planning, and collaboration with the Manager, Social Media, to engage with the public and address concerns in real time
Supporting the Division’s Agenda Forecasting System to anticipate and plan for Council and Committee items with corresponding issues management and communications strategies.

Post-secondary education in Communications, Public Relations, Political Science, Public Administration, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Extensive experience leading the full issues management process, including developing and implementing issues management strategies and action plans that align with organizational priorities and values, with coordinated responses to cross-divisional and intergovernmental matters.
Extensive experience providing strategic communications advice and operational support to senior leaders in a complex, high-profile organization, with a strong background in issues management, media relations, and strategic communications.
Extensive experience monitoring, identifying, and assessing sensitive, emerging, and high-profile issues to develop timely and effective communications strategies that protect organizational reputation and support balanced media coverage.
Considerable experience in budget planning and administration, including resource allocation to support strategic priorities.
Experience serving as a media spokesperson and/or building relationships with journalists is considered an asset.
Strong understanding of municipal governance, Council procedures, and decision-making processes, with awareness of the political, social, and economic factors influencing all levels of government.
Proven ability to leverage data, trends, and feedback to improve forecasting processes and strengthen organizational preparedness, including the development of crisis communication plans and integration of social listening tools.
Strong collaboration skills, with the ability to work across divisions and in partnership with teams such as Social Media and Media Relations to ensure consistent and responsive issues management and public engagement.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to translate complex concepts into clear, compelling narratives for diverse audiences.
Demonstrated leadership in managing high-performing teams, championing strategic best practices, and fostering innovation within a collaborative, inclusive, and results-driven work environment.
Knowledge of outreach strategies for diverse and multilingual audiences, applying an inclusive and culturally responsive communications lens.
Knowledge of relevant legislation and policies, including MFIPPA, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, the Ontario Human Rights Code, and AODA.

Excellent analytical skills with the ability to recommend solutions.

title: Asset Management Specialist - Enforcement
description:
Req ID: 28636
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 2
Closing Date: 10/28/2026
Job Summary
The Asset Management Specialist leads the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the Enforcement Division’s asset management program, supporting a diverse portfolio of vehicles, technology, communications equipment, uniforms and specialized operational assets across eight regulatory and enforcement service areas.
The role provides strategic and operational leadership through the development of asset strategies, lifecycle and investment plans, governance frameworks, performance measures and business processes that support operational readiness, sustainability, accountability and effective resource allocation. Working collaboratively across corporate and operational teams, the Specialist provides subject matter expertise, oversees asset management systems and data, and leads initiatives that optimize asset performance and support front-line service delivery.
Duties and Responsibilities
Lead the Division’s asset management program, including the development and implementation of strategies, policies, governance frameworks, standards, controls and performance measures.
Establish and maintain consistent processes governing asset planning, acquisition, deployment, utilization, maintenance, replacement, transfer and disposal to support effective life cycle management and accountability.
Develop lifecycle plans, replacement forecasts, multi-year asset plans, budget forecasts, business cases and funding recommendations to support long-term investment and resource allocation decisions.
Assess asset condition, utilization, criticality, risk, and lifecycle requirements to identify investment priorities, optimization opportunities, funding gaps and future asset needs.
Lead procurement planning and acquisition strategies, including requirements development, specification preparation, evaluations, contract administration, vendor management and warranty oversight.
Implement and oversee asset management systems, inventories and registries to ensure accurate asset data, effective tracking, lifecycle accountability and audit readiness.
Evaluate and optimize asset management technologies and related business processes to enhance asset visibility, system effectiveness and operational efficiency.
Develop dashboards, performance measures and management reports and analyze financial, utilization, inventory and lifecycle data to identify trends, risks and opportunities for optimization and continuous improvement.
Conduct audits, reconciliations, risk assessments and benchmarking activities to strengthen governance, optimize asset performance and support informed decision-making.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations regarding asset investment, governance, procurement, lifecycle planning, operational risk and resource allocation.
Lead stakeholder engagement, consultation and requirements gathering with Fleet Services, Finance, Procurement, IT, Materiel Management and operational partners to support coordinated asset planning and stewardship.
Lead cross-functional initiatives and represent the Division on corporate committees, working groups and enterprise projects to advance asset management objectives and operational effectiveness.
Coordinate operational asset stewardship activities, including vehicles, inventories, assignments, transfers, recoveries, replenishment and compliance monitoring.
Ensure governance, funding, procurement, training, tracking and life cycle controls are established to support the successful introduction of new programs, services, technologies and operational assets.
Performing other duties, responsibilities and special projects as assigned.
Skills and Qualifications
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Business Administration, Public Administration, Asset Management, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations Management, Information Technology, or related discipline.
Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in asset management, program development, inventory management governance, fleet coordination, logistics, operational resource management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing asset management policies, governance frameworks, lifecycle strategies, internal controls, performance measures and continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated experience providing governance, planning or analytical support for a large, high-value and operationally diverse asset portfolio.
Experience conducting strategic planning, risk analysis, lifecycle forecasting, state-of-good repair reviews, inventory management, asset optimization, budget development and business case preparation.
Demonstrated ability to assess financial exposure, operational consequences and organizational risk and translate complex findings into practical strategies, controls and recommendations.
Experience administering or providing functional oversight of corporate or enterprise assets, inventory, fleet or technology-management systems, such as SAP, fleet management information systems, IT asset-tracking tools or equivalent platforms.
Demonstrated knowledge of data governance, asset registries, audit controls, performance measurement, management reporting and asset lifecycle data.
Strong research, policy development, analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to interpret corporate policies, operational requirements, technical information and industry best practices and develop appropriate divisional standards, procedures and processes.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint, with the ability to analyze complex data, develop dashboards, prepare professional reports, presentations and business cases.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex information and present recommendations to management and stakeholders.
Strong interpersonal, consultation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes and establish effective working relationships across multiple business areas.
Demonstrated project management and change management skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives involving competing priorities, multiple stakeholders and complex operational requirements.
Ability to exercise independent judgement, manage sensitive information and work with minimal supervision in a complex, high-accountability environment.
Knowledge of municipal procurement, inventory management, fleet operations, and asset optimization and management best practices is considered an asset.
Knowledge of LEAN principles and continuous improvement methodologies is considered an asset.
Certification in Asset Management, Supply Chain Management, Project Management or a related discipline is considered an asset.

title: PUCC/Permit Technologist
description:
Req ID: 28690
Number of Positions: 2
Vacancy Type: Combination  - 1 Permanent Position & 1 Temporary Position
Duration of Contract for Temporary Position: Up to 2 years
Closing Date: 10/30/2026
Job Summary
Under the direction of Managers, Rapid Transit Program Office (RTPO), RTPO is seeking two experienced, motivated, and detail-oriented professionals to fill the role of PUCC/Permit Technologist.
The PUCC/Permit Technologist role will be responsible for conducting both office-based and field reviews of Public Utilities Coordinating Committee (PUCC) and Road Occupancy Permit (ROP) applications on behalf of the RTPO. This role supports the delivery of the City's major rapid transit initiatives, including the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension (ECWE), Bus Rapid Transit (BRT), and Hazel McCallion Light Rail Transit (HMLRT) projects.
Key responsibilities include ensuring compliance with City policies, procedures, standards, and applicable legislation; reviewing and evaluating new and existing permit applications; coordinating with internal and external stakeholders; and conducting site inspections to verify that work has been completed in accordance with approved permits and City requirements. The successful candidate will assess permit submissions, review supporting documentation, and perform field investigations as required to determine whether applications should be approved, modified, or returned for revision. Through these activities, the PUCC/Permit Technologist will play a critical role in supporting the safe, efficient, and coordinated delivery of municipal infrastructure and rapid transit projects across the city.
Duties and Responsibilities
Reviews and evaluates Public Utilities Coordinating Committee (PUCC) and Road Occupancy Permit (ROP) applications in support of RTPO projects, in coordination and consultation with the City's Permitting and Technical Services sections, as required.
Ensures compliance with City policies, procedures, standards, applicable legislation, and service timelines; maintains accurate electronic permit records and databases.
Coordinates application reviews with internal departments, utility companies, contractors, consultants, and other project stakeholders; attends pre-construction meetings as required.
Coordinates meetings with utility companies and inspection staff to resolve conflicts between proposed or approved utility alignments and field conditions.
Provides technical guidance and support to staff, internal stakeholders, utility companies, contractors, and external applicants regarding utility applications and ROP requirements.
Conducts site visits, as required, to support the review and assessment of proposed PUCC and ROP applications.
Performs site inspections to verify compliance with permit conditions and confirm completion of approved works in accordance with City by-laws, standards, and municipal requirements.
Identifies, assesses, and helps resolve permit-related issues, conflicts, and operational impacts affecting rapid transit infrastructure and projects.
Reviews permit submissions and provides recommendations regarding approval, revision, or rejection based on applicable requirements and site conditions.
Maintains accurate records, correspondence, reports, and supporting documentation related to permit reviews and inspections.
Ensures the timely investigation, response, and resolution of inquiries, complaints, and service requests received from residents, elected officials, and other stakeholders.
Conducts research and assists in the development of programs, initiatives, policies, and strategies that support RTPO objectives and the City of Mississauga's strategic priorities.
Support the successful delivery of the ECWE, BRT, and HMLRT programs through effective permit administration, stakeholder coordination, and field oversight.
Prepares reports, correspondence, and briefing materials related to permit matters, as required.
Performs other related duties as assigned.
Skills and Qualifications
Successful completion of a diploma in Civil Engineering Technology from a recognized Community College / University Degree with a minimum of 2 years of progressive experience in permitting, construction and maintenance of services infrastructure (or an equivalent combination of education and experience).
Membership in the Ontario Association of Certified Engineering Technicians and Technologists as a Certified Engineering Technologist (C.E.T.) or an equivalent designation considered an asset.
Demonstrated ability to co-ordinate complex utility or construction projects.
Knowledge of applicable legislative requirements such as the Occupational Health & Safety Act and Employment Standards Act.
A strong understanding of road maintenance procedures, Ontario Provincial Standards and Specifications (OPSS), utility infrastructure alignments and construction methodologies.
Must be able to read and interpret all types of engineering drawings, specifications and construction standards.
Strong interpersonal, communication and leadership skills are required.
Excellent organizational, computer skills and problem-solving abilities are required.
Must be able to multitask, function well in a team environment, and demonstrate a proven ability to work with a broad range of stakeholders.
Computer literacy in CAD and Microsoft applications including Access.
Experience with GIS programs, INFOR Public Sector Application Software and SAP is an asset.
Ability to travel to various work locations as and when required.

title: Technologist, Building Services
description:
Req ID: 28656
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/22/2026
Job Summary
This role reviews applications for building permits to confirm all building applications accepted and issued comply with the Ontario Building Code Act, Ontario Building Code, “applicable law” and are processed in accordance with the standards and requirements established in the Building By-law.  Accurately assess each proposal to determine applicable fees and charges and determine appropriate construction values.
Duties and Responsibilities
Review & Assessment
•    Review and assess building permit application submissions in accordance with the Ontario Building Code Act, Building By-law , as well as other applicable law, department policies and procedures.
•    Review building permit applications to determine necessary approvals in accordance with applicable legislation and ensure compliance has been achieved prior to permit issuance.
•    Review and assess requests for conditional permits to determine eligibility and provide recommendations for management approval
•    Process building permit applications, including the review of documents, drawings and specifications for limited scope building permit applications to ensure compliance with the Building Code Act, Ontario Building Code, Building By-law, municipal by-laws and other applicable legislation as part of our express review services. Liaise with inspections staff to resolve design and construction issues and provide permit status
•    Coordinates and monitors approval process for projects subject to site plan approval and other applicable planning approvals.
•    Monitor application timelines to ensure compliance with prescribed timelines in the Ontario Building Code Act and take corrective action as necessary
Interpretation
•    Accurately interpret and apply the Ontario Building Code Act, Ontario Building Code, Building by-law and other applicable legislation.
•    Interpret the Building Code Act, Building By-law and other applicable legislation as defined, to determine applicable fees and charges
•    Performs research for and prepares technical reports as required or requested
•    Accurately provide professional advice on building permit applications and associated processes
Data Entry & Record Keeping
•    Compile and maintain accurate records and associated documentation in accordance with established internal controls, protocols and legislation.
•    The accurate documentation is required in order to mitigate financial, reputation risks, and legal challenges.
•    Daily use of MAX, SharePoint, SAP and ePlans.
Customer Service
•    Act as the principal point of contact throughout the building permit approval process for the public, applicants, City staff and external agencies.
•    Provide guidance and direction to applicants and internal stakeholders regarding building permit applications and associated approvals. Assists applicants in the coordination and expedition of building permit applications to ensure overall customer satisfaction.
•    Assists applicants in the facilitation of building permit issuance in compliance with prescribed timelines
•    Proactively build and maintain relationships with clients, able to provide clear, timely and transparent communication of information to facilitate timely building application approvals.
Meetings
•    Attend meetings to discuss and provide advice regarding building permissions, approvals applicable legislation and associated processes. Conduct preliminary meetings and consultations advising applicants of the required approvals, documents, specifications and drawings required to facilitate building permit issuance and provide direction as to the necessary procedures and protocols.
Skills and Qualifications
•    Undergraduate Degree or Community College Diploma in one or more of the following areas: Architecture, Engineering or related discipline
•    Registered Building Official with the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing (MMAH)
•    Qualification in the following categories as defined under  Part 3, Division C of the Ontario Building Code from the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing (MMAH) in the following categories: House, Small Buildings, General Legal Process, HVAC-House, Plumbing-House.  Qualification in additional categories would be considered an asset.
•    Eligibility for and willingness to obtain and maintain the Certified Building Code Official (CBCO) designation from the Ontario Building Officials Association (OBOA)
•    Thorough knowledge of the Building Code Act and Ontario Building Code
•    Working knowledge of Construction Regulations and Occupational Health and Safety Act
•    Working knowledge of the following principles and standards: building design and construction principles; building construction methods, building industry issues, trends and best practices.
•    Minimum of five years of related work experience reviewing and interpreting architectural drawings and policy documents or equivalent combination of education and experience
•    Knowledge of building and development application processes and associated legislation is highly preferred
•    Proficient in reading and interpreting drawings, specifications and other technical documents
•    Excellent verbal and written communication skills and interpersonal skills to effectively deal with the general public, consultants, developers, staff and others stakeholders within the building approvals process.
•    The ability to effectively communicate technical information to a non-technical audience is required
•    Well-developed analytical, research, organizational, negotiation and problem solving skills
•    Strong computer literacy is required with experience using MS Office and Adobe Acrobat; experience with Mississauga Approvals Express (MAX), EDMS, SharePoint, electronic plans submission (ePlans) or other permitting software is considered a strong asset
•    Must be flexible in adapting to rapidly changing workloads and work environments

Job Summary
Working for the City means you are part of something big, something special! You will be part or a team of engaging, enthusiastic and dedicated people that are committed to collaborating with one another to deliver on our commitment to the residents, visitors and businesses of Mississauga.

Exercise Counsellor:
Responsible for demonstrating proper instruction to customers with respect to correct technique and use of exercise equipment.
Responsible for enforcing fitness etiquette rules and guidelines posted.
Assist customer service with facility tours, provide direction, and clear all applicable areas in emergency situations.
Perform daily safety inspections, inventories and cleaning duties.
Responsible for checking wristbands for select fitness classes as needed.
Provide emergency first-aid when required.

Counsellor will show select cardio and strength exercises, takes blood pressure, heart rate and will provide quality customer service and act as a knowledgeable resource to participants.

Strong written and verbal skills.
Experience and familiarity with common fitness training techniques.
Strong program leadership skills.

title: Fitness Supervisor
description:
Req ID: 28703
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/28/2026
Job Summary
The City of Mississauga is seeking a Fitness Supervisor to lead the development and delivery of diverse fitness programs that reflect the needs, interests and experiences of our community. Reporting to the Fitness Manager, you will work with an experienced team of industry professionals to coordinate fitness programs and initiatives across the city. You will also contribute as part of a facility team, supporting the day-to-day operation of the facility, programs and staff while fostering a welcoming, accessible and inclusive environment that promotes positive community experiences and excellent customer service.
Duties and Responsibilities
Initiate, design and deliver quality programs that encourage and support healthy, active living for community residents
Lead a diversified part-time staff team, including exercise counsellors, personal trainers and group exercise instructors, while identifying opportunities for volunteers and student internship placements
Hire, coach, train, schedule and supervise staff, ensuring the delivery of safe, effective and high-quality programs and services
Manage, monitor and recommend annual operating budgets, maintain financial accountability, provide budget forecasts, and strive to achieve established targets.
Monitor, prepare and approve part-time payroll and provide reports as required
Participate as part of the facility and building supervisory teams, including Manager on Duty shifts, to ensure the effective supervision of facilities, programs and staff while maintaining excellent public relations and customer service
Ensure a coordinated approach to service delivery, facility and space utilization, and identify opportunities to maximize participation and cross-program collaboration
Develop and participate in outreach initiatives that introduce fitness concepts and healthy living opportunities to the community and encourage community involvement in recreation services
Provide timely and effective resolution of customer concerns and complaints using sound judgment, decision-making and communication skills
Prepare for, respond to and follow up on accidents, incidents and emergency situations in accordance with corporate policies and procedures
Work collaboratively with the Supervisor of Operations and Facility Manager to ensure a high standard of facility cleanliness, maintenance and readiness
Maintain strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including customer service, parks, human resources, standards and training, community development and partner organizations
Ensure compliance with all applicable City of Mississauga Recreation and Culture standards, corporate policies, procedures and legislative requirements
Maintain all required statistics and prepare reports, evaluations and recommendations as required
Participate in business unit, divisional and departmental initiatives, projects and working groups that support organizational priorities
Perform other related duties as assigned
Skills and Qualifications
Degree or diploma in Recreation, Physical Education, Kinesiology, or validated equivalent, with a minimum of three years full-time related experience
Current certification in personal training and/or group exercise through CSEP, CANFIT PRO, CPTN, OFC, ACSM or validated equivalent
Demonstrated knowledge of and experience with program design and delivery, program maintenance software (example: ActiveNet, Perfect Minds, etc.), customer service, budget management, partnership program delivery and volunteer group dynamics
Must have excellent written and oral communication skills
Ability to work in a changing team environment and also possess an interest in professional development
Must hold a valid and current Intermediate First Aid or Standard First Aid certification with CPR C & AED from a recognized WSIB-provider or must hold a valid and current Basic First Aid or Emergency First Aid with CPR C & AED from a recognized WSIB-provider, at the employee’s expense.
Able to support other areas within the facility team
Ability to travel between multiple recreation sites within the city for time-sensitive work-related travel.

title: Project Leader, Transportation
description:
Req ID: 28672
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 11/05/2026
Job Summary
Do you want to be part of the team that brings a cultural shift towards multi-modal transportation in Mississauga? If so, Transportation Planning is looking for a Project Leader that will create and implement long-range transportation plans and establish a city-wide framework for multi-modal transportation.
Duties and Responsibilities
Under the direction of the Manager, Transportation Planning, this position will:
Undertake multi-modal transportation projects to implement the City’s Transportation Master Plan (TMP) in partnership with the appropriate City staff, other transportation agencies, funding partners and/or stakeholders
Undertake Corridor Transportation Master Plans, City-wide transportation studies and area-specific transportation reviews
Initiate the development and monitoring of City-wide transportation policies for the City’s Official Plan, ensuring the necessary supporting research and technical analysis is undertaken
Undertake the Development Charges Transportation Background Study in consultation with other sections, divisions and departments
Provide support for the annual budgeting process as it relates to section, divisional and departmental projects
Review local, national, and international best practices on transportation planning matters, with a view to guiding the development and advancement of the City’s transportation system
Represent the section and/or department on inter-departmental and inter-agency projects, attending public meetings, giving presentations and answering questions
Prepare presentations, briefing memos, corporate reports and other correspondence for senior city staff and members of City Council and Committees of Council on transportation planning matters
Perform other related duties as assigned
Skills and Qualifications
A graduate from a recognized university program in transportation planning, civil engineering or related program with a minimum of 5 years of experience
Membership or eligibility for membership as a professional engineer or in the Ontario Professional Planners Institute
Demonstrated strong project management and ability to multi-task, prioritize and adapt quickly to change
Key job competencies are acting with integrity, communicating effectively, driving continuous improvement, serving customers, resolving conflict, driving projects to completion and thinking broadly
Good working knowledge of transportation planning theories, principles and analysis techniques
Strong working knowledge of related disciplines such as the environmental assessment process, land use planning and traffic and transit operations is an asset
Understanding of Provincial, Regional, GTA and City transportation policy context and key trends that influence and shape the city

description:

To be considered for this competition, applicants must be enrolled in a recognized post‑secondary co-op program and be eligible to complete a Work Term during the specified period. Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Canada. Proof of enrolment in a related program must be uploaded when completing the application.
Job Summary
Supports the Facilities Maintenance team by leading day-to-day improvements to its SharePoint environment. The role focuses on improving site navigation, content organization, document management, and access to information, including Power BI reports and dashboards. The position may also support other Facilities Maintenance activities, such as physical asset audits and inspections, CMMS database cleanup and validation, reporting, and standard operating procedures.
Duties and Responsibilities
Key duties and responsibilities include:
•    Improve and maintain the Facilities Maintenance SharePoint site, with emphasis on intuitive navigation, logical information architecture, usability, searchability, and consistent page design.
•    Create and update SharePoint pages, document libraries, lists, folders, metadata, views, links, permissions-related content requests, and other site content in accordance with established standards.
•    Review, reorganize, and maintain files and folders; identify outdated, duplicate, or misplaced content; and recommend practical improvements to document management.
•    Embed and organize Power BI reports and dashboards in SharePoint so operational and performance information is easy to find and use.
•    Gather user feedback, document business requirements, and implement practical improvements that increase SharePoint adoption and effectiveness.
•    May need to validate and update asset, equipment, location, and maintenance data in the CMMS, correcting incomplete, duplicate, outdated, or inconsistent records.
•    Support reports, dashboards, standard operating procedures, work instructions, templates, and other process documentation.
•    Conduct physical asset audits and cycle counts, compare findings with CMMS records, and reconcile identified discrepancies.
•    Perform other related duties in support of the Facilities Maintenance team as assigned.
Skills and Qualifications
•    Currently enrolled in a university or college program related to information management, business technology, data analytics, asset management, engineering, facilities management, public administration, or a related field.
•    Good understanding of SharePoint, Power BI, database management. CMMS applications, maintenance planning, asset management, or data analysis is an asset.
•    Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and commitment to data accuracy.
•    Ability to research, analyze, validate, and compile information into clear and usable formats.
•    Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications; experience with SharePoint, Power BI, Excel, or similar reporting and collaboration tools is an asset.
•    Ability to organize digital information logically and consider the end-user experience when developing pages, libraries, folders, and navigation.
•    Strong written communication skills and the ability to assist in preparing reports, procedures, guides, and presentations.
•    Strong customer service, interpersonal, and verbal communication skills.
•    Ability to work independently, manage assigned tasks, exercise sound judgement, and collaborate effectively as part of a team.
Working Conditions
•    Primarily office-based, with regular use of computers and Microsoft 365 applications.
•    Periodic field work at City facilities, including site inspections, physical asset verification, and cycle counts.
•    May require walking through mechanical, electrical, operational, storage, or other facility areas and light lifting of supplies or identification materials.

description:

Job Summary
As a DevOps Specialist, you will work with technical teams across the organization to implement DevOps strategies and automate applications and infrastructure across on-premise and cloud environments. You will be responsible for understanding requirements and designing, documenting, supporting and delivering secure, scalable and reliable solutions within a defined framework.
The successful candidate will collaborate with software development teams, project managers and infrastructure architects to design, build, deploy, operate and monitor enterprise applications and services. Responsibilities include implementing Infrastructure as Code (IaC), cloud automation, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring solutions and operational best practices.
This role requires hands-on experience with AWS services including ECS, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Route 53, CloudWatch, IAM and networking services, as well as Windows and Linux administration. Experience with Azure DevOps, scripting, AI-assisted tools and automation is also desirable. Occasional work outside regular business hours is a requirement of the position. The role follows a hybrid work model, requiring employees to be onsite in the office 3 days per week and allowing remote work for the remaining days. Specific in-office days may be set by the team or department to support collaboration and business needs.
Duties and Responsibilities
Design, implement and support DevOps practices, cloud infrastructure, automation solutions and CI/CD pipelines.
Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code and configuration management solutions using Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, Ansible or similar tools.
Configure, manage and troubleshoot AWS services including ECS, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Route 53, CloudWatch, IAM, VPC and Elastic Load Balancing.
Develop and support containerized applications using Docker and Amazon ECS, and administer Windows and Linux environments across cloud and on-premise infrastructure.
Develop automation and integrations using PowerShell, Python, YAML, REST APIs and related technologies.
Implement monitoring, alerting, logging and performance optimization solutions for applications and infrastructure.
Investigate and resolve application, infrastructure, networking, security and deployment issues.
Collaborate with development, infrastructure, security and business teams to deliver production-ready solutions that comply with City standards and industry best practices.
Develop and maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, operational procedures and recovery plans.
Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI-assisted DevOps tools and Microsoft Power Platform, to improve operational efficiency and service delivery.
Provide technical guidance, training and knowledge transfer to staff and project teams.
Participate in after-hours support, maintenance activities and emergency response as required.
Skills and Qualifications
Post-secondary degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related discipline, or possess an equivalent combination of education, certifications and experience
3+ years of experience as a DevOps Engineer, DevOps Specialist, Cloud Engineer or in a similar role.
Strong understanding of Agile methodologies, DevOps principles, source control and CI/CD practices.
Experience designing and implementing CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Jenkins or similar platforms.
Strong experience configuring and supporting AWS environments, including ECS, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Route 53, CloudWatch, IAM, VPC and load balancing services.
Experience with Infrastructure as Code and configuration management tools such as Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, Ansible, Chef or Puppet.
Experience with Docker, Amazon ECS and containerized application delivery.
Strong scripting and automation skills using PowerShell, Python and YAML.
Related IT certifications are an asset. AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, AWS Solutions Architect or equivalent is preferred.
Advanced hands-on experience with Windows and Linux administration, monitoring, logging and troubleshooting.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, collaboration and documentation skills, with the ability to work independently or within cross-functional teams.
Experience with Microsoft Azure or other cloud platforms would be considered an asset.
Experience evaluating and implementing AI-assisted tools for software development, infrastructure operations and DevOps workflows would be considered an asset.
Experience with Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps and Power Automate, would be considered an asset.
May require light lifting of supplies or materials and prolonged use of computer keyboards and screens in a primarily office-based environment.

description:

Job Summary
MiWay is seeking experienced and motivated leaders to supervise the day-to-day maintenance of transit buses and non revenue fleet vehicles.
Reporting to the Assistant Manager, Transit Maintenance, the Supervisor is responsible for leading skilled trades staff in a unionized, safety critical environment to ensure vehicles are safe, compliant, and ready for service. This position plays a key role in supporting daily service delivery, fleet availability, and MiWay’s commitment to safety, reliability, and customer service.
Guided by a forward thinking strategic plan, MiWay’s vision is to be a transit system that makes Mississauga proud by providing a safe, reliable, and efficient transit system built on strong traditions of safety, service, and courtesy.
Why Work for MiWay
Full time, permanent employment
Competitive salary
Annual performance and economic adjustment reviews
Career advancement opportunities
Four (4) weeks of paid vacation
Comprehensive benefits package
OMERS pension plan
Overtime premiums
Skilled trades premiums - $1.75/hour
Afternoon shift premiums - $2.00/hour
Overnight shift premiums - $2.75/hour
And more.
Note
: This position requires a valid 310T Truck and Coach certificate and flexibility to work different hours, shifts, and days off to be considered.
Duties and Responsibilities
Under the direction of the Assistant Manager, Transit Maintenance, the successful candidate will:
Supervise the day to day activities of Transit Maintenance staff to ensure the safe, efficient, and timely inspection, repair, cleaning, and servicing of transit buses and non revenue fleet vehicles.
Assign work, allocate personnel and equipment, and adjust priorities to support daily fleet availability and service requirements.
Schedule maintenance activities and prepare work orders using a computerized maintenance management system.
Ensure all maintenance work complies with Ministry of Transportation legislation, applicable safety regulations, manufacturer specifications, and MiWay policies and procedures.
Provide front line leadership by setting clear performance expectations, monitoring work quality, and supporting staff through coaching and feedback.
Manage staffing requirements, attendance, overtime, and shift coverage in accordance with operational needs and collective agreements.
Work collaboratively with management, Human Resources, and union representatives to address employee relations matters and support effective labour relations.
Respond to service impacting failures, road calls, incidents, and urgent maintenance issues as required.
Ensure staff are properly instructed in safe work practices, approved methods, procedures, and performance standards.
Support the onboarding, orientation, and ongoing development of MiWay  Maintenance staff.
Support and, when required, supervise the operation of bus wash area, fueling stations, and bus cleaning activities.
Monitor and manage records including absences, overtime, incident reports, and operational data.
Assist with identifying warranty issues, tagging defective components, and ensuring warranty claims and supplier commitments are upheld.
Ensure tools, parts, materials, and cores are properly handled, stored, returned, or disposed of in accordance with procedures.
Conduct technical investigations, inspections, and procedural or quality audits as required.
Promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace that is free from harassment and discrimination.
Support MiWay’s commitments under the Ontario Human Rights Code (OHRC), the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, and related corporate policies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
Skills and Qualifications
Minimum grade 12 - Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD) or verified equivalent, is considered an asset.
Valid 310T - Truck and Coach Technician Certificate of Qualification, issued by Skilled Trades Ontario and maintained in good standing.
A minimum of five (5) years of experience as a Journeyperson following attainment of trade certification, with exposure to the full range of transit bus maintenance activities or an equivalent combination of education / certifications and experience.
Three (3) years of progressive experience demonstrating leadership responsibility, including supervision or acting supervisory duties is preferred.
A valid 310S Automotive Service Technician Certificate of Qualification, issued by Skilled Trades Ontario, is considered an asset.
Valid Ontario Class G Driver’s Licence with an acceptable driving abstract; a Class C licence with Z endorsement is preferred.
Ability to work various shifts including days, afternoons, nights, weekends, and statutory holidays.
Strong working knowledge of heavy vehicle maintenance, diagnostics, and manufacturer specifications.
Knowledge of shop management practices, preventative maintenance programs, and applicable OHSA, MTO, MOL, and MOE legislative requirements.
Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and support employees in a unionized environment, with a focus on safety, collaboration, consistency, and respectful workplace practices.
Strong interpersonal, organizational, and written and verbal communication skills.
Experience or exposure to battery electric buses or alternative propulsion technologies is considered an asset.

AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY:
Reporting directly to the Treasurer, this role provides strategic direction and expert advice to the Finance Division on financial planning, budget review, and ensuring fiscal efficiency. The role involves preparing detailed assessments, aligning departmental proposals with the City’s Strategic Plan, and ensuring financial and legislative compliance. This position also plays a critical role in City-wide strategic planning, fostering a collaborative environment that values trust, diversity, and inclusivity.
Stakeholder Relationships
Collaborate with stakeholders to identify improvement areas, facilitate solutions, and promote a culture of fiscal responsibility and innovation. •    Build effective working relationships at all levels, particularly with senior leaders in client departments across the City, ensuring the highest possible level of client satisfaction and being established as a trusted advisor. •    Build and foster strong working relationships and collaborative arrangements with internal and external customers, stakeholders, business and community leaders, sponsors, public and the media.
Operation Strategy
Lead initiatives that enhance operational excellence, setting goals and implementing policies to support Council priorities. •    Identify and manage complex, interdependent projects, ensuring alignment with relevant strategic goals. •    Provide the Treasurer with recommendations on managing critical issues and risks. •    Ensure a high standard of financial planning, budget, management reporting, and analytical support is delivered consistently to their department portfolio. •    Establish clear goals and create policies that support the Council’s priorities and the City’s strategic vision. •    Regularly review and report on the status of strategic initiatives to ensure continuous alignment with strategic goals.
Financial Analysis & Strategic Planning
Provide financial analysis, support the annual budget process, and prepare short to long-term capital funding analysis. •    Advise on financial impacts of budget proposals and submit recommendations to the leadership team and Council. •    Participate in strategic planning at both the sectional level as well as the provision of expertise to the broader City-wide strategy. •    Prepare detailed financial reports that include analysis, projections, and recommendations. •    Assist with the annual budget planning process, ensuring it meets the City’s financial requirements and strategic objectives.
Policy & Legislative Support
Interpret legislation, monitor trends, and use research and data analytics to inform policy and strategy decisions. •    Maintain knowledge of all laws, regulatory, judicial mandates, ordinances, legislative various acts, codes and by-laws set out by Federal, Provincial or Municipal levels of government. •    Continuously update policies and procedures to reflect legislative changes and best practices.
Financial Modelling & Advice
Develop financial models and provide insights to support decision-making, collective bargaining, and resource management. •    Offer guidance to finance staff across City departments. •    Provide financial analysis, support the annual budget process, and prepare short to long-term capital funding analysis. •    Provide expert advice on the financial implications of various budget proposals to the leadership team and Council.
Communication and Reporting
Prepare and present complex financial reports and recommendations, keeping leadership informed of key activities and initiatives. •    Develop comprehensive financial reports that accurately reflect the City’s financial status and projections. •    Regularly update the leadership team on key financial activities and initiatives. •    Maintain a high level of transparency in all financial communications to build trust and credibility.
SELECTION CRITERIA:
Education:
Post-secondary degree in Economics, Business, Public Administration or other relevant discipline. •    CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) or CFA or MBA is preferred.
Experience:
Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in finance or public administration, preferably within a municipal or similarly complex organization, with significant responsibility for strategic and financial analysis, multi-year operating and capital budgets, funding strategies, and business case development. •    Proven experience advising senior leadership, leading and facilitating complex cross-departmental initiatives, and applying legislative and policy analysis to support financial, strategic, and organizational decision-making.
Other Skills and Assets:
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving abilities, with proficiency in Microsoft tools. •    Ability to handle sensitive situations with discretion and maintain strong internal and external relationships. •    Strong knowledge of financial planning, budget management, and capital funding analysis. •    Excellent written and verbal communication skills for preparing and presenting complex financial reports and recommendations. •    Expert knowledge of Municipal, Regional, Provincial and Federal Governments, applicable Legislations and awareness of current social, economic and political priorities •    Ability to prioritize highly complex tasks with critical deadlines •    Experience developing policies and procedures and ensuring compliance

POSITION DUTIES:
Reporting to the Director, Cultural Services, this position provides senior-level strategic and operational leadership to advance the City of Brampton’s readiness for the future transfer of the Peel Art Gallery, Museum and Archives (PAMA), effective January 1, 2028, through the design and integration of a new Museums & Collections line of business.
The role operates within a multi-party governance structure where the PAMA Transition Board provides strategic direction and oversight, the Region of Peel maintains operational responsibility during the transition period, and external advisors (including KPMG) support operating model development.
Within this context, the position is accountable for leading the City’s internal planning, integration, and operational readiness work, translating Transition Board direction and consulting outputs into City-ready service models, implementation plans, and decision frameworks. The role ensures that the City is prepared to assume operations with a cohesive, financially sustainable, and operationally viable Museums & Collections service
Museums & Collections Strategy and Service Model Development
Lead the development of an integrated Museums & Collections service framework, including mandate, scope, and service delivery model
Define how PAMA, gallery and exhibition functions, heritage sites (including Bovaird House and Alderlea), and programming operate as a coordinated municipal service
Establish clear roles, relationships, and workflows between collections stewardship, curatorial practice, exhibitions, and public programming
Align the Museums & Collections service with existing Cultural Services lines of business while defining a distinct and sustainable service identity
Ensure alignment between external operating model work (including KPMG) and the City’s broader Cultural Services framework
Identify service delivery options, including governance considerations, programming approaches, and partnership opportunities
Develop long-term vision and positioning for municipal museum and gallery services in Brampton
Prepare briefing materials, business cases, and strategic recommendations for senior leadership and Council
Align work with broader corporate initiatives and transition-related studies
PAMA Transition Planning and Readiness
Lead Cultural Services’ role in transition planning to support the future transfer of PAMA
Translate Transition Board direction into actionable City requirements, including service delivery expectations and operational implications
Develop and maintain a City-focused transition roadmap, including key milestones leading to January 1, 2028
Identify and document readiness requirements, dependencies, and constraints across systems, staffing, and operations
Establish and monitor readiness frameworks and validation criteria to ensure preparedness for transfer
Identify, assess, and escalate risks to the City’s future assumption of operations, including financial, operational, and reputational risks
Coordinate cross-functional planning across Finance, HR, Legal, IT, Planning, Communications, and Facilities
Support development of implementation plans, timelines, and resource requirements
Provide ongoing updates, analysis, and advisory support to senior leadership
Bovaird House Collections and Strategic Positioning
Lead a comprehensive review of collections, assets, and current operations at Historic Bovaird House
Develop and oversee implementation of a collections management and rationalization strategy, including retention, deaccessioning, and transfer
Establish or refine collections management standards, documentation practices, and risk mitigation protocols
Develop recommendations for the future role, function, and positioning of Bovaird House within the Museums & Collections portfolio
Align site operations and programming with the future integrated service model
Oversee development of an interim programming and operating approach during the transition period
Ensure collections and curatorial decisions support long-term exhibition, programming, and public engagement outcomes.
Operational Planning and Financial Modelling
Translate operating model concepts (including external consulting work) into practical, implementable City operating plans
Develop costed operating models, including staffing requirements, budget forecasts, and infrastructure needs
Define future-state workflows, procedures, and service delivery standards across all sites and functions
Establish alignment between collections management, curatorial development, exhibitions, and programming delivery
Identify resource requirements, gaps, and financial pressures, and propose mitigation strategies
Support development of multi-year implementation and operational plans leading to the transfer date
Ensure alignment between strategic direction and operational feasibility
Inform long-term financial sustainability planning for the Museums & Collections service
Stakeholder Coordination and Strategic Advisory
Provide senior-level strategic advice to the Director, Cultural Services and Community Services Management Team
Support coordination between City staff, the PAMA Transition Board, and external consultants
Liaise with internal departments, including Finance, Budget Office, Legal, HR, Planning (Heritage), Communications, IT, and Facilities
Ensure the City’s interests and requirements are clearly represented in transition planning processes
Engage with heritage stakeholders, community organizations, and cultural sector partners
Prepare reports, briefings, and presentations for internal and external audiences, including Council
Identify and communicate risks, issues, and mitigation strategies
Build relationships and influence across divisions to advance complex, cross-functional work
SELECTION CRITERIA
Education:
Post-secondary degree in Museum Studies, Cultural Heritage Management, Arts Administration, Public Administration, or a related field.
Experience:
Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in museum operations, cultural planning, or heritage management
Experience in service model development, organizational planning, or transformation initiatives
Experience supporting large-scale organizational transition, service integration, or implementation initiatives
Experience contributing to operating model development, budgeting, or financial analysis in a public or institutional context
Experience working within a municipal or public-sector environment preferred
Demonstrated experience with collections management and curatorial practices
Experience working in complex, multi-stakeholder environments
Special Requirements:
Strong knowledge of museum standards, collections management, and curatorial practices
Strategic thinking and ability to translate high-level direction and operating model concepts into practical, implementable service and financial plans
Strong project leadership and coordination skills
Ability to provide strategic advice within complex governance structures, including boards and senior leadership environments
Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and evolving environments
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
Strong written and verbal communication skills for executive audiences
Ability to build relationships and influence without direct authority

:
Reporting to the Manager, Internal Audit, (or to the Director, Internal Audit on solo projects) this position plans, performs internal audit assurance and advisory engagements of moderate complexity for the City of Brampton in accordance with the Internal Audit Charter and recognized Internal Audit Professional Practices and codes of professional conduct. This includes initiating, leading and conducting, risk based audits, operational effectiveness reviews, audits of compliance with applicable legislation, regulations, by-laws, City policies and procedures and working with management to develop effective and efficient risk mitigation strategies. Ability to work independently and objectively when conducting audit engagements of moderate complexity, preparing audit reports and evaluating management action plans. Supports the Director in planning, coordinating and management of audit resources, including third party consultants. Participating in the development of the audit function’s strategic plan and multi-year and annual internal audit work plan.  The role is an ambassador for risk management and continuous improvement of the control environment, and brings innovative ideas and methods to increase awareness and buy-in from management.
Conducts operational audits in accordance with professional audit standards in the role of lead auditor, team member or working independently on some projects, with responsibility to supervise more junior project staff
Performs assigned projects of moderate complexity (or work with a Manager, Internal Audit on complex audit engagements) and deal with high dollar values and confidential and sensitive information affecting the City operations, assets and resources
Develops a solid understanding of the audit entity or subject matter by conducting background research accomplished through use of the internet, discussion with the auditee, site visits, the review of relevant documents such as multi-year business plans, consultant reports, statues, regulations or standards, committee and council minutes, previous year’s audited financial statements and management letters, contact with other professional and municipal organizations
Develops (independently or in collaboration with the Manager, Internal Audit) the project plan including determining audit objectives, scope and methodology; assessing risk and internal controls; establishing budget and reporting timelines
Prepares (independently or in collaboration with the Manager, Internal Audit) the audit program and /or evidence collection plan which includes defining of audit criteria by performing extensive research of sources such as recognized bodies of experts, applicable laws, regulations and other authorities, other bodies or jurisdictions delivering similar programs and services, internal policies and procedures and applicable criteria successfully applied in other audits or reviews done internally and externally; developing audit procedures and tests; and determining what evidence is needed, how the evidence can be collected, will be analyzed, interpreted
Complete assigned audit procedures (interviews, analysis, examination of documentation, site visits, and other testing) in accordance with the project plan and adapts /expands audit procedures, as necessary, based on issues identified as the audit progresses
Conducts thorough assessment and analysis and obtains sufficient and appropriate evidence
Identifies significant audit issues and improvement opportunities, quantifying cost savings / revenue opportunities, and illustrating non-financial impacts
Develops practical and meaningful audit recommendations that will help improve City services or operations
Prepares and / or reviews audit working papers (audit project files) that contains evidence supporting the findings, conclusions, and recommendations and ensures that they adhere to professional auditing standards and Internal Audit’s office guidelines and audit manuals.
Evaluate audit results and prepares a written summary of major audit issues (audit observations, conclusions, and recommendations) independently or in consultation with the Manager, Internal Audit or the Director of Internal Audit
Demonstrate critical thinking skills in all aspects of work (audit planning, fieldwork, audit finding evaluation, and reporting)
Prepares draft audit reports or parts thereof, for review by the senior management of Internal Audit prior to submission to auditee, Audit Committee and /or other standing committees
Makes presentations to auditee personnel to communicate audit recommendations, as required.
Evaluates action plans in response to recommendations
Keeps Director/Manager, Internal Audit informed of audit progress, any emerging issues and /or significant areas, and recommends appropriate action and /strategies to meet planned project objectives and audit reporting deadlines
Attends Audit Committee meetings and makes presentations on audit project(s) as required
Performs special audits and investigations including fraud reviews and forensic audits, as required
Maintains good auditee relationships and acts at all times in a professional manner
Liaises with and keeps current of the operations of assigned departments with particular reference to audit concerns and issues
Contribute to effective teamwork and communication, high standards of work quality and organizational performance and continuous learning
Participates in development and implementation of Internal Audit’s corporate initiatives, including coordinating training, IT system applications, continuous process improvement projects etc)
Contributes to the Internal Audit’s strategic planning process, such as the City-wide risk assessment, and annual and long-term work plan
SELECTION CRITERIA
Education:
University Degree, with a professional Accounting Designation (such as CPA, CA; CPA, CGA; or CPA, CMA); or designation as an auditing professional (CIA, CGAP, CRMA, CISA).
An equivalent combination of education, skills and considerable experience in the field of performance auditing, operational and control auditing, and other audit projects will be considered.
Fraud certifications Audit certifications (such as CFE) are an asset.

A minimum of 5 years of practical experience planning, performing, and reporting on value-for-money/performance audits, operational/control audits, and other audit projects, with at least 2 years of leading experience with audit professionals. Public sector internal audit experience is desirable.
Comprehensive in-depth knowledge of all aspects of audit principles, practices, techniques and standards (including the IIA Standards and the Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards.)

Sound organizational, interpersonal, oral and written communications skills.
Sound project management, analytical, excellent initiative, and problem solving skills.
Ability to deal courteously and effectively with all levels of staff, management and members of council, and build consensus.
Ability to work independently and with minimum supervision.
Ability to work in a multi-disciplinary setting and team environment.
Computer proficiency in MS Office Suite and audit applications such as TeamMate or Pentana.
Experience with data analytics applications (such as ACL, TeamMate Analytics) and performing data analytics as part of audits or other special projects which assist in the collection and analysis of electronic data would be asset.
Experience with Pentana, TeamMate or other audit software is strongly preferred.

University Degree in relevant fields (business, accounting, management), coupled with an accounting designation (CPA, CA or CPA, CMA or CPA, CGA); or and auditing designation such as CIA, CISA.
A minimum of 5 or more years practical experience planning, performing, and reporting on value-for-money (performance) audits, operational/control audits,  and other audit projects, with at least 2 years of leading experience with audit professionals.

Training on the Highway Traffic Act and Health and Safety Act as it relates to the job and City policies and procedures is provided to all School Crossing Guards by the City.

POSITION DUTIES:
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Revenue, responsible for the management and direction of all collection activities for defaulted Provincial Offence Act (POA) fines, non-parking Administrative Monetary Penalty (AMPS), tax accounts in arrears, and miscellaneous receivables owed to the City.  In addition, this position is responsible for all administrative aspects of the Tax Collection, POA, and General Receivables sections. This individual provides leadership, strategic direction, and overall staff development within the Corporate Collections area.  The individual will be required to either personally represent the Corporation or co-ordinate representation in dealings with external agencies, various clients, legal proceedings and appeal hearings.  Provides direction, guidance and skills development to non-union and union staff.
Manage all operational and administrative aspects of the tax arrears, defaulted POA fines, Non-parking AMPS and general accounts receivable billing and collection processes including supervision, hiring, guidance and direction of staff; •    Review and initiate staff development activities; •    Monitor/ coach area supervisory staff to ensure that proper priorities and service levels are established and maintained; •    Recommend, plan, develop and implement new or innovative procedures to improve efficiency and the overall success of collection activities; •    Recommend and implement changes to Corporate Policies and Standard Operating Procedures as required; •    Provide leadership to ensure high productivity to realize corporate priorities; •    Manage debt collection activities undertaken by both internal staff and on behalf of the City by external service providers, such as collection agencies and bailiffs; •    Ensure accuracy of commissions paid to external collectors; •    Ensure that all collection activities are compliant with applicable legislation, Municipal Act,  City policies and By-laws, and Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of the Attorney General for POA fine activities; •    Manage the Tax Sale process in strict compliance with the requirements of the Municipal Act, Ontario Regulations, and court precedent; •    Represent the Department/City in meetings with internal and external customers, suppliers, tribunals, legal proceedings, professional associations, and municipal and provincial governments; •    Responsible for the accuracy and balance of the Accounts Receivable system ; •    Ensure a proper system of internal controls are in place for entries to TXM 2000 tax system, CAMS, the Integrated Court Offences Network (ICON), the Accounts Receivable system and related General Ledger entries; •    Review and authorize cheque requisitions and reconciliations for the distribution of the POA fines collected on behalf of other municipalities and government agencies; •    Responsible for the approval and posting to the general ledger of journal entries for POA revenue and general accounts receivable. •    Review doubtful accounts and make annual financial provision for doubtful allowance in the general ledger. •    Responsible for identification of uncollectable accounts (POA, property tax and general accounts receivable) and preparation of Council reports for write-off of accounts. •    Prepare reports as required for Council information and approval •    Prepare and monitor the annual budget for all accounts under Corporate Collections responsibility. •    Prepare related schedules of annual Financial Information Return (FIR) as needed; •    Establish and maintain a high level of professional customer service in balance with  effective collection processes; •    Responsible for managing the procurement process (Request for Proposal, Request for Quote) and administer contracts with external vendors related to the operation of the Collections unit. •    Collaborates with systems administrators and vendors in preparation of business requirements, testing and deployments of any new software for the Collections unit. •    Establish and maintain a high level of professional customer service in balance with effective collection methods; •    Provide assistance/backup to Supervisor of Tax Collection and Collections Group Leader as required; •    Ensure that records retention is in compliance with legislative and by-law requirements.
SELECTION CRITERIA:
EDUCATION:
Post secondary degree in Business Administration or other relevant discipline.
EXPERIENCE:
5 years senior supervisory experience in a unionized environment •    Collection experience is required
OTHER SKILLS AND ASSETS:
Completion of a CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) is considered an asset •    Sound knowledge of The Municipal Act with exceptional understanding of Taxation and Tax Collection requirements •    Knowledge of public sector operations and PeopleSoft financials modules are an asset •    Excellent organizational skills with acute attention to detail •    Exceptional communication skills along with superior report writing, performance and work record.

Answers queries and communicates with members, union representatives, HR and outside agencies re employee information, administration procedures, or interpretation of plan provisions. Drafts and distributes correspondences for employee requests related to RRSP transfers, OMERS purchase, and disability elimination periods. • Maintains Payroll/OMERS records using Versatile/BRIMMS Systems. • Stuffs, seals and sorts pay statements for all payroll groups. Creates new files for new employees.
