My Community. My Lifestyle. My Career.
Firefighter Opportunity
Are you interested in helping to build a safe community? If so, City of Brampton Fire and Emergency Services may be the right place for you....
Bring your talents and step into a firefighter career where serving our diverse community and the opportunities to make a difference are endless. Our Brampton Fire and Emergency Services team are driven by exceptional service delivery. As a member of our team, you will feel the pride of values-driven achievements and will experience life-long supportive relationships. Be a part of a fast-paced and rewarding environment where you can contribute to building a safe community, improving Emergency Response, Public Safety and Public Education for the citizens of Brampton.
In this highly visible role, you will:
Serve as a highly valued and respected member of the community;
Feel the excitement that comes with serving the community. Every shift has a different challenge or situation requiring a diverse set of skills;
Respond to all emergencies when called upon;
Combating fires;
Performing rescue operations and providing medical assistance in an emergency environment;
Handle routine maintenance of firefighting equipment/ department property;
Public fire safety education and inspect properties and equipment for fire hazards;
Handle state of the art apparatus and modern equipment;
Have the ability to help your community and network as an ambassador at charity and community events;
Participate in continuous learning to advance your knowledge and skills;
Be part of a culture that values the personal and professional growth and development; and
Perform other similar and related duties as assigned.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Ontario Secondary School Diploma or academic equivalent.
Minimum of 18 years of age or older
Legally entitled to work in Canada.
National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1001 Firefighter I & II and NFPA 1072 (NFPA 472) Hazardous Materials Awareness/Operations certifications or equivalent as recognized by the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) (must have proof of Pro Board or IFSAC).
Possess a valid and current Standard First Aid and CPR "C" certification
Possess a valid and unrestricted Ontario Class “D” driver’s license with a “Z” endorsement or equivalent (deemed equivalent by Ontario Ministry of Transportation) and a driving record that is acceptable to the City of Brampton.
Provide a satisfactory Police Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening
Completion of the Ontario Fire Administration Candidate Testing Program Stage 2
OR
Completion of the York University Firefighter Fitness Testing
NFPA 1006 Certified in Surface Water Rescue – Level II (2013 Standard) or Operations Level (2021 Standard)
OR
Completion of OFAI Swim Test (as verified by possession of a current and valid certificate)
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in English, with the ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and professionally across a variety of situations and audiences.
Ability to work rotating 24-hour shifts, including nights, weekends, statutory holidays, and other scheduled shift assignments.
Demonstrated ability to swim proficiently and successfully complete the required swim assessment.
Candidates must meet the vision requirements established by NFPA 1582
Demonstrated ability to safely perform the intense and sustained physical activities associated with firefighting, including working in physically demanding and stressful environments.
The ability to attain certifications within 18 months from the date a conditional offer of employment
BENEFICIAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE:
College diploma or university degree from a recognized and accredited post-secondary institution.
Commitment to volunteerism humanitarian, or community service.
Act with integrity, exercise sound judgment, solve complex problems, support continuous improvement, and consistently provide professional and respectful service to the community.
Accepts direction, work effectively within a team environment, establishes and maintains a positive professional relationships, and demonstrate compassion, respect, and empathy toward others.
Maintains confidence, professionalism, and composure when responding to stressful, challenging, or traumatic situations.
Demonstrate effective strategies for managing occupational stress, maintaining personal well-being, and supporting a healthy work-life balance.
Demonstrate resilience, tenacity, and perseverance when faced with difficult or changing circumstances, while maintaining a positive and solution-focused approach.
Previous experience working in customer service, public service, or other roles involving regular interaction with members of the public.
Trade apprenticeship or a minimum of one year of experience in a skilled trade recognized in Ontario.
Minimum of one year of previous experience as a volunteer, part-time, or full-time firefighter.
Minimum of one year of previous experience in an emergency services environment other than fire suppression.
Minimum of one year of experience operating large or heavy vehicles and/or heavy machinery.
Minimum of one year of experience as an elevator technician, fire alarm technician, fire and life safety technician, member of the military, or member of the Canadian Coast Guard.
National Lifeguard Certification: Possession of a current National Lifeguard (NL) certification.
Occupational Health and Safety: Completion of occupational health and safety training or certification, such as Joint Health and Safety Committee (JHSC) Part 1 and Part 2 certification.
Possession of a current Emergency Medical Responder (EMR) certification.
Previous experience, training, and/or (Operations or Technician) certification in technical rescue disciplines, including water, ice, trench, rope, or confined space rescue, consistent with the competencies identified in NFPA 1006.
Previous experience in hazardous materials removal, environmental remediation, or private-sector disaster management, including chemical spills, environmental clean-up, mould, asbestos, biohazard, or contamination remediation.
Demonstrated ability to work with diverse communities (race, culture, ability, mental health, sexual orientation, faith, gender identity and all diverse identities)
Multilingual skills preferred

Make a difference in the community
Receive advanced training and the latest technology in Fire Services

Prepare financial reporting that highlights performance, trends and cost savings for review by Transit Management.
Compile data for surveys from external agencies such as CUTA , APTA, OPTA and Stats Canada.
Work with internal and external auditors during interim and year-end financial audits and various government audits. Ensure adherence to Corporate Policies and Procedures, Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) guidelines, ATU Collective Agreements, as well as Federal and Provincial Legislation in all financial matters.

Position Summary
Reporting to the Manager of By-law Policy and Adjudications, the Licensing Clerk is responsible for the administration and coordination of the City's business licensing and animal licensing programs. The position provides customer service, processes licence applications and renewals, coordinates licensing-related inspections and compliance reviews, investigates licensing concerns through administrative review, and liaises with By-law Education and Enforcement staff to facilitate inspections and enforcement action where required.
The Licensing Clerk serves as the primary point of contact for licensing applicants, licence holders, and members of the public regarding licensing requirements and processes. The position plays a key role in ensuring applications are complete, licensing requirements are met, and matters requiring enforcement attention are appropriately referred and tracked.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Licensing Administration
Receive, review, process, and issue business licence applications, renewals, and amendments in accordance with applicable by-laws and procedures.
Administer pet licensing programs including the review of applications, issuance of licences, and maintenance of records.
Coordinate all aspects of licence application processing, including circulation to internal departments and external agencies where required.
Maintain accurate licensing records, databases, files, and reporting systems.
Create and maintain licence-related identification cards, badges, and associated documentation as required.
Coordinate licensing and Dangerous Dog Hearings hearings and provide administrative support related to appeals and committee proceedings.
Customer Service and Public Education
Provide front-line customer service and technical guidance regarding licensing requirements, by-laws, policies, procedures, and application processes.
Respond to telephone, email, and in-person inquiries from residents, businesses, contractors, and other stakeholders.
Interpret licensing requirements and explain compliance obligations to applicants and licence holders.
Prepare correspondence related to licensing matters, including approvals, deficiencies, requests for information, and compliance notices.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Manager of System Planning and Management, the Supervisor of Policy and Planning provides strategic leadership to a team of policy professionals responsible for supporting Halton Region's role as Service System Manager for Early Learning and Child Care.
The Supervisor leads the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of local policies, strategic initiatives and planning frameworks that support a high-quality, accessible, affordable and responsive early learning and child care system. This position is responsible for translating provincial legislation, regulations, funding guidelines and strategic priorities into local policies, programs and implementation strategies that respond to the evolving needs of children, families, service providers and communities across Halton. Drawing on data, research, sector knowledge and stakeholder engagement, the Supervisor ensures policy and planning decisions are evidence-informed, innovative, position the Region for future success and aligned with Regional priorities.
Duties & Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership and People Management
Provides leadership, direction, coaching and performance management to a team of professional staff responsible for policy development, strategic planning, research, performance measurement and special initiatives.
Establishes priorities, work plans and service standards to support divisional, departmental and corporate objectives.
Fosters a high-performing, inclusive and collaborative team culture built on trust, accountability, respect and shared purpose.
Creates a psychologically safe workplace where employees feel supported, valued and empowered to contribute their perspectives and ideas.
Promotes employee engagement, professional growth, succession planning and talent development through ongoing coaching, mentorship and recognition.
Leads staff through complex policy, planning and system transformation initiatives while effectively managing change and uncertainty.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Manager of Strategic Initiatives, the Strategic Initiatives Coordinator (Innovation) serves as the Corporation’s subject-matter expert and internal catalyst for operational excellence, continuous improvement, performance management and innovation.
The role leads the design and deployment of Lean methods, continuous improvement practices and corporate performance measurement across the corporation to strengthen service delivery, reduce waste and improve outcomes.
The position partners with leadership and process owners to identify and improve critical processes by analyzing current-state performance; design and implement future-state processes; establish meaningful performance measures; and validate and sustain measurable benefits, including cost savings, cost avoidance, capacity creation, service improvements and other operational efficiencies.
The role will also establish meaningful KPIs and support a measurable culture of improvement, including full reporting of efficiencies. The role also leads corporate innovation mechanisms that evaluate, pilot and implement beneficial ideas contributed by employees.
Job Duties Include
The following responsibilities and duties of this position include but are not limited to:
Key Duties
Lead cross-functional continuous improvement and Lean initiatives to improve service delivery, reduce waste and strengthen organizational effectiveness.
Partner with leaders, managers and process owners to identify, assess and prioritize improvement opportunities across the organization.
Map and analyze current processes, identify root causes and design practical future-state processes and solutions.
Apply Lean and structured problem-solving methodologies to support process redesign, implementation and sustainable improvement.
Develop meaningful KPIs and performance measures to monitor process health, service outcomes and organizational performance.
Measure and report the results of improvement initiatives, including cost savings, cost avoidance, capacity created, cycle-time reductions and service improvements.
Develop clear dashboards, reports, presentations and decision-support materials for senior leadership and Council.
Design and deliver Lean and continuous improvement training to build organizational knowledge and capability.
Establish and support a network of Lean Champions, providing coaching, facilitation and guidance to teams undertaking improvement work.
Lead the Town’s Innovation Team and corporate employee idea process, from idea generation and evaluation through pilots and implementation.
Research leading practices, emerging approaches and benchmarking information to identify new opportunities for innovation and operational improvement.
Support strategic corporate initiatives involving service reviews, levels of service, performance improvement, risk-based thinking and organizational effectiveness
Qualifications & Skills
A university degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Operations Management, Business Analytics, Organizational Leadership, or an equivalent combination
Lean/Six Sigma Green Belt certification
More than three years and up to five years of relevant practical experience
Demonstrated experience mapping current and future-state processes and applying Lean principles and methodologies
Experience conducting business process reviews and program evaluations, including performance measurement, audits and benchmarking
Strong project management skills and demonstrated ability to lead work across functional and departmental boundaries
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex information into practical recommendations
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing reports, presentations and decision-support materials
Nice to Have
Black Belt certification is preferred
Business Process Management training or designation is considered an asset

Reporting to, and under the direction of, the Supervisor of Building Inspections, the Senior Building Inspector is responsible for performing legislated building inspections required by the Ontario Building Code while ensuring compliance with all applicable Laws, Town By-laws and the Ontario Building Code. Primary duties include, but are not limited to:
conducting inspections for Part 9 and/or Part 3 buildings as well as general inspections (footing, back fill, framing, insulation, and final);
coordinating approvals from other departments and outside agencies;
investigating unsafe conditions related to, but not limited to fire, explosions wind and/or vehicular damage;
issuing compliance orders under the Building Act Code;
reviewing drawings with site supervisor;
consulting with external clients such as engineers and architects to resolve on-site issues;
reviewing test and site reports;
preparing and maintaining accurate files and records of inspections;
assist clients with inquiries concerning the Ontario Building Code;
assessing building code complaints to ensure compliance; and;
other duties as may be assigned.

Our Building Services team is looking for an enthusiastic, solutions-oriented team player, with strong work ethic.  You are self-motivated, self-starting and utilize a proactive approach to work, while modelling positive and professional behaviour. You value partnerships. Your excellent communication and interpersonal skills coupled with your experience enables you to skillfully build, establish and maintain positive working relationships. You demonstrate tact, diplomacy and sound discretion when working with a broad range of partners.
You bring to the team your strong reasoning, analytical, numerical, research and presentation skills.  You solve problems by identifying, gathering and processing relevant information.  Using your knowledge and experience in the field allows you to navigate through difficult interpersonal situations in a positive manner.  You demonstrate adeptness in conflict resolution and approach situations with the goal to improve communication, diffuse tension, resolve problems and build effective working relationships with all stakeholders.
What You Bring To Our Team
As the successful applicant, you must possess:
a post-secondary diploma or degree in Architecture, Architectural/Engineering Technology or a related discipline;
familiar with Part 3, 4, 9, 10 and 11 and Alternative Solutions of the Ontario Building Code
a minimum of three (3) years directly related experience;
qualification(s) as per the Ontario Building Code in the categories of:
General/Legal processes
House
Small Buildings
Large Buildings
Building Services
Building Structural
Complex Building
Plumbing (House)
HVAC (House)
Working at Heights certification;
basic level proficiency in MS Office (Word, Outlook, Excel) and AMANDA and
Successful candidates are required to hold and maintain a valid Province of Ontario Class "G" Driver's Licence and qualify for the Town’s Safe Driver Program criteria. This position drives a fleet vehicle.

Benefits and retirement plan offered in accordance to Corporate programs and/or the applicable Collective Agreement.
A hybrid work environment and flexible work arrangements where employees are empowered to do their best work in the way that works for them. This is designated as a Mobile Hybrid role. Mobile Hybrid recognizes that approximately 50% of job functions associated with the role are done from a Town vehicle. Some work not completed from a Town vehicle can be done remotely. Mobile Hybrid

Position Overview
The Street Lighting Technologist will support the City’s street lighting maintenance and asset management programs, applying innovative and creative problem-solving skills. The Technologist will also support the planning, design, and construction administration of street lighting capital projects.
The Technologist will ensure street lighting maintenance and improvements are efficiently planned, designed, implemented, and managed. Work must comply with municipal standards, Provincial legislation, and industry guidelines, and be delivered cost-effectively and on schedule. The technologist will correspond with the public, council and other stakeholders on lighting related items.
The Technologist will support the street lighting electrical capital construction program by providing technical services in design, engineering, site inspection, construction administration, document preparation, research, and methodology development. The Technologist will also guide and monitor contractors maintaining street, path, and alleyway lighting, with a strong focus on technical excellence, customer service, and public safety.
Responsibilities
o   Oversee the planning, design, and management of street lighting capital projects, including streetscape, roadway, path, and alleyway lighting, as well as associated power distribution systems, in compliance with relevant Provincial and municipal standards, legislation, and industry guidelines.
o   Direct the methodology, technical approach, design, and execution of capital projects, including the selection of appropriate lighting technologies and integration of energy efficiency objectives.
o   Develop budget estimates, project schedules, and cost recovery calculations. Identify and apply relevant rules, regulations, and codes, such as electrical codes, municipal standards, and traffic-related requirements, to all proposed work.
o   Conduct site visits to gather asset information, analyze collected data in relation to program requirements, and identify site opportunities, constraints, and required design modifications.
o   Evaluate projects through research and consultation with internal and external stakeholders. Develop innovative solutions, assess technical, operational, and financial feasibility, and recommend optimal options, utilize illumination design software and current best practices in roadway and area lighting design.
o   Develop conceptual plans and prepare and/or review detailed design and construction drawings, including lighting layouts, photometric plans and analysis, wiring diagrams, and electrical schematics suitable for tendering and construction.
o   Design and/or review lighting plans and specifications tailored to specific site conditions, road geometry, traffic volumes, pedestrian activity, and safety requirements.
o   Develop, review, comment on, and approve consultant tender and RFP documents for public-area street lighting and commercial or private development site lighting. Ensure all specifications, drawings, scopes of work, technical requirements, and performance criteria comply with industry, municipal, and Provincial standards.
o   Conduct regular field inspections during construction and maintenance activities as part of contract administration; analyze and recommend or approve on‑site changes; negotiate changes to the quantity and value of the contract; review and approve electrical payment requests; and prepare deficiency documentation.
o   Supervise, coordinate, and provide technical direction to contractors and consultants, including oversight of their work quality, adherence to timelines, and financial control and accountability.
o   Approve and sign all invoices received from electricity‑supply utilities, telecommunications providers, and private contractors (including contracts for new services), ensuring accuracy and compliance with contract terms and budget allocations.
o   Liaise with electricity utilities regarding power sources, service connections, metering, billing, and related arrangements; and coordinate with telecom providers regarding joint‑use of poles and associated design and safety requirements
o   Manage all aspects of the City’s street, path, and other lighting maintenance program, including oversight of the private contractor engaged to perform routine and emergency maintenance work.
o   Ensure maintenance activities are delivered efficiently and in accordance with Minimum Maintenance Standards (MMS) under applicable Provincial regulation, municipal policies, and contractor agreements.
o   Maintain records of work orders, completed work, outages, repairs, and upgrades using formal asset‑management and maintenance‑management software, contributing to the City’s broader asset‑management and lifecycle‑planning activities.
o   Assist in asset management including GIS and enterprise asset management systems, condition assessment, and other methods of asset data collection and reporting.
o   Measure and analyze lighting levels using specialized software and associated tools; assess compliance with design criteria and safety standards; recommend corrective actions (such as repositioning, upgrading, or converting fixtures); and follow through to project completion.
o   Prepare written reports, updates, and presentations for internal management, Council committees, and external stakeholders regarding project status, performance data, and proposed changes.
o   Receive, investigate, and respond to inquiries and complaints from the public, elected officials, City departments, outside agencies, other government levels, consultants, contractors, and vendors regarding street lighting performance, outages, and proposed changes, providing factual, clear, and timely responses and follow‑up.
o   Liaise with film and television production companies to assess temporary lighting requirements, approve temporary installations, and ensure that any work carried out complies with safety regulations and contractual terms.
o  Participate in the selection and supervision of co‑op students or temporary technical staff working in the street lighting section, providing on‑the‑job training and mentoring.
o   Work in accordance with applicable health and safety legislation, including the Occupational Health and Safety Act, and all corporate and departmental policies and procedures related to occupational health and safety.
o   Provide day‑to‑day technical support and, as required, coverage for the Street Lighting Supervisor, assisting with prioritization of work, operational decision‑making, and coordination of emergent or time‑sensitive requirements.
o   Perform other duties as assigned that are directly related to the major responsibilities of the position, including participation in City‑wide initiatives, technology trials, and asset‑management planning.
Requirements
Proven knowledge of Electrical Street Lighting systems normally acquired by obtaining a Diploma from a three-year Community College in Electrical/Power Technology or Degree in Electrical Engineering. Member of or eligible for certification with respective professional organizations, i.e. Ontario Association of Certified Engineering Technicians and Technologists (OACETT). Must have considerable diversified professional experience in electrical engineering with a specialization in street lighting preferred. Must have extensive technical knowledge of the principles and practices of electrical engineering, including power distribution.  Knowledge of all forms of lighting (design and maintenance) is considered a distinct asset.  This would include knowledge of all related rules and regulations governing the design, construction and maintenance of street lighting systems. Must be able to communicate effectively in oral and written form, including the ability to deal diplomatically with all aspects of the public, staff and elected officials. Must have advanced computer skills and a working knowledge of work processing, spreadsheets and databases.
Must have a valid class “G” driver’s license. This position will require occasional travel between sites and/or City facilities and must provide own transportation.

Plans, organizes, instructs and leads chess lessons for participants from children through to adults. Ensures a positive and safe environment for participants and peers.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Facilitates, leads and supervises the program.
Organizes and writes lesson plans to be handed in by week two of the program. Develops lesson plans specific to the abilities of each group. Reviews lesson plans with the Recreation Supervisor/Program Coordinator prior to class and submits at the end of each session.
Prepares and organizes program equipment and supplies, maintaining an inventory of supplies, reporting to the Program Coordinator/Recreation Supervisor any items needing replacement.

Directly guides volunteers and PT Program Assistants as required.
Advises Program Coordinator/Recreation Supervisor of any customer service issues, complaints or inquiries.
Ensures safety at ALL times, enforcing safety regulations as set out by the City of Markham leisure programs policies and procedures.
Ensures the site, equipment and supplies are appropriate to the activity and environment to reduce and minimize risk to other staff and participants.
Children between the ages of 6 – 12 years must use the buddy system when going to the washroom. Escorts preschool children to the washroom or change room, ensuring that preschool children are never left in the sole attendance of a volunteer.
Unlocks and locks-up the facility/program location as required.
Qualifications
Minimum High School Diploma.
Minimum ages of 16 years old at the start of employment.
Minimum of 2 years of previous experience working with individuals or groups to teach the basics of chess to people of all ages.
At least 3 years of prior experience developing chess skills and strategies.
Knowledge of Basic Chess principles
Knowledge of the operation and maintenance of Chess equipment and facilities.
Current certifications in Standard First Aid OR Intermediate First Aid with CPR C and AED.
High Five Certificate and adherence to the principles of Healthy Child Development (Children ages 6 to 12 years).
Ability to read, understand, follow, and enforce safety procedures.
Excellent verbal/written communication skills, leadership skills, customer service skills and sensitivity to interact with a diversity of patrons, parents and staff in a courteous and efficient manner.
Must be able to work with kids and adults of different ages and abilities to teach the game of chess, as well as help the learners understand the various strategies used including chess notations, tactics and endgame. The City of Markham is seeking a Senior Financial Analyst/ERP Support Analyst within the Financial Planning Division of the Finance Department. Reporting to the Senior Manager, this dual role is responsible for the preparation, analysis, implementation and monitoring of the departmental operating and capital budgets, following both corporate budgetary policies and generally accepted accounting principles and practices. The role will also support ERP implementation and act as a representative of the Finance Planning group to configure, test and rollout Workday Budgets, Project SKUs and Asset Management (TCA) modules.
Job Summary:
You are a results-oriented professional with proven ability to complete tasks with minimal oversight, coupled with demonstrated high level critical thinking and the ability to perform in a proactive and strategic manner. Your analytical, collaborative and organization skills enable you to build trusted partnerships with clients, extract and document process information into Workday configurations, and support the seamless migration of data and workflows from current systems into Workday to ensure Phase 1 deliverables are implemented successfully. Your ability to be flexible and resourceful will be necessary to pivot between competing mandates including ERP and City priorities.
This is a 1-year contract role with potential to be extended for subsequent implementation phases.
Key Duties and Responsibilities:
Performs analysis and investigation of budget variances including both high level and activity level analysis of expenditures, revenues, complement, and other performance measures; forecasts expenditure and revenue patterns; highlights to management relevant financial issues with strategic and operational impacts; recommends options towards resolution of issues.
Develops financial models and sensitivity scenarios, and evaluates financial alternatives and business cases for programs, projects and other initiatives based on a clear understanding of program needs and resource constraints.
In conjunction with the business unit and procurement staff, prepare and analyze tenders/quotes/request for proposal reports, rationalizing budget to actual variances and long term financial impacts.
Participate in the planning, coordination and preparation of long range operating and capital strategic plans, including managing and updating fee funded financial models.
Research, analyze and interpret information and make recommendations for financial plans and special projects undertaken by the City.
Contribute to the creation of financial policies and procedures by participating in multi-discipline projects that address the operational and financial requirements of the City.
Identify opportunities for continuous improvements and compliance with corporate, financial and administrative directions and policies.
Ability to work extended hours during budgeting season or as occasionally required.
Actively participate in requirements workshops to communicate functional needs related to operating budgets, capital projects, asset management (TCA and asset registry).
Assist with set up and configuration of Workday modules, including budget structures, rules, and control frameworks such as: mapping chart of accounts, cost centres, and funding sources.
Prepare and validate data for migration, execute test scripts for UAT, assist with creation of training materials and process documentation.
Qualifications:
Successful completion of a degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Economics and a Chartered Professional Accountant designation/MBA, or a combination of education and experience in a related discipline at an equivalent competence.
At least seven (7) years of practical experience in senior financial planning and analysis positions, and/or Workday Implementation Roles, preferably in a multi-divisional organization.
Hands‑on experience with Workday Financials, specifically: Workday Budgets, Workday Projects (SKU), Workday Asset Management / TCA
Experience supporting ERP implementations or Workday deployments
Familiar with EIB templates, business processes, and Workday configuration concepts
Ability to deal with conflict using tact and persuasion, exhibiting professionalism.
Presents information logically and objectively, and comfort dealing with ambiguity.
Knowledge of accounting and economic principles including strategic and financial planning
Ability to read, interpret and apply complex legislative texts such as the Municipal Act.
Experience with municipal budgeting, capital project structures, and asset accounting is an asset
Experience in a public sector organization including knowledge of municipal funding sources, such as Development Charges, Provincial and Federal funding, Canada Community-Building Fund (CCBF) and provincial/municipal statutes and regulations is an asset.
Excellent oral and written communication.
Detail‑oriented, organized, and comfortable supporting technical and functional teams.

Working in an Incident Command System, the Firefighter’s role is to protect life and property through firefighting, emergency medical and other types of emergency incidents, often performed under conditions requiring strenuous physical and mental exertion. Firefighters are also expected to provide excellent customer service as well as being leaders in public fire safety education. Firefighters are active participants in ongoing training in all phases of emergency response, including suppression, inspection, emergency operations, rescue, and providing medical assistance.
Key Responsibilities
Respond to fires, rescue, and medical emergencies in a safe and efficient manner.
Perform firefighting, hazardous materials response, and technical rescue operations.
Collaborate effectively with your crew and other first responder agencies while upholding the highest standards of professionalism.
Complete reports, record keeping and administrative duties.
Participate and support fire prevention and public education activities.
Participate and complete all training as assigned.
Clean, inspect and maintain equipment and apparatus conducting full maintenance and safety checks.
Ensure facilities, equipment, and grounds are clean and orderly.
Perform other similar and related duties as assigned.
Minimum Qualifications
Legally entitled to work in Canada.
Grade 12 level education or equivalent (e.g. General Education Diploma).
NFPA 1001 Fire Fighter I and II certified from an accredited program from a recognized institution, accredited by the International Fire Service Accreditation Congress (IFSAC) or Pro Board.
Possess valid Ontario Fire Administration Inc. (OFAI) Candidate Testing Service Stages 2, 3 (FPAT only) and swim test certificates.
Valid Ontario driver's license with a good driving record (no more than six (6) demerits).
Valid Class “D” license with a “Z” air brake endorsement by hire date.
Emergency Medical Responder (EMR) Certificate.
Medical clearance by a physician.
Clear Vulnerable Sector Security Check.

title: Crossing Guard
description:
We’re looking for a Crossing Guard to join Clarington’s Public Services team!
Why Clarington?
Clarington is a community full of possibilities.
As one of the fastest-growing municipalities in Durham Region, Clarington is home to over 107,000 residents across four urban centres and 14 hamlets. With our population expected to double by 2051, Clarington offers a perfect blend of urban living and small-town charm. We’re known for our thriving energy and agricultural sectors, vibrant historic downtowns, and exceptional quality of life.
Our team thrives in a collaborative environment that promotes work-life balance and meaningful community impact. We value accountability, integrity, and respect, and we are deeply committed to fostering equity, inclusion, and diversity in the workplace. Together, we’re building a stronger Clarington — for today and for future generations.
The future is bright – and working with the Municipality of Clarington means you can help shape it. How will you make your mark?
About the Role
Vacancy Statement:
Unless specifically stated, all job postings at the Municipality of Clarington are to fill existing vacancies within our organization.
Work Model:
Front Line
If you have safety in mind, are outgoing, if you like working in an outdoor environment in all weather conditions and would enjoy keeping children safe on their way to and from school, you may be suited for this position. This position works under the direct supervision of the School Crossing Guard Coordinator.
Key Responsibilities
Controlling the flow of traffic to allow for the safe, supervised crossing of students and pedestrians.
Communicating clearly and effectively using spoken commands and hand signals.
Instructing students and other pedestrians in safe crossing procedures.
Exercising sound judgement in determining safe opportunities to cross students, based on weather conditions, road conditions, distance and speed of traffic, gaps in traffic and distracted driving.
Perform other duties as assigned, including those specific to the department.
What you bring
Good Vision – you must be able to see vehicles, different colours (stoplights), children and signal indications from close and far distances.
Good Hearing – you must be able to communicate with children, motorists, parents and be able to hear vehicles approaching, honking, etc.
Physically fit – you must be able to climb, stretch, carry and lift items weighing approximately 4 lbs, stand, walk and twist for periods of up to 1.5 hours daily in all weather conditions.
Must be able to report for work at the designated crossing locations and times as scheduled.
As the nature of this position is to ensure the safety of children and pedestrians, Crossing Guards may need to be reassessed from time to time to ensure they are fit to perform the necessary duties.
Must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
What we offer
Rate of pay: $557.36 bi-weekly (2026 rate)
Hours of work: School Crossing Guards work during the school year (September to June, excluding holidays and PA days) and must be able to work for a half hour in the morning between the hours of 7:00 am and 8:00 am and a half hour in the afternoon between 3:00 pm and 4:00 pm Monday to Friday. Exact times are based on crossing guard location. School crossing guards are required to be at their assigned crossing site in the morning and after school.
Compensation for all scheduled school PA days (5-7 average a year), Christmas and New Year Break (approximately 2 weeks), March Break (1 week), all statutory holidays.
Compensation for all mandatory scheduled trainings and meeting (2-4 meetings a year during daytime hours).
Rain suit and other equipment provided.
Boot allowance offered (currently $100 per year).
Additional Information
A satisfactory criminal record check with a vulnerable sector screening and proof of qualifications will be required for the successful candidate.
How to Apply
To learn more about employment with the Municipality of Clarington and to apply for this exciting and challenging opportunity,
visit:
www.clarington.net/careers
.

Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005

title: Assistant Town Solicitor
description:
Job Details
Permanent Full Time (Non-Union)
Posting Status
Open to all current Town of Oakville employees and external applicants
Closing Date
Applications for this position must be received at
oakville.ca
by no later than 11:59 p.m. on
November 1, 2026
This job posting is for an existing vacancy and therefore will be filled accordingly.
We offer:
A hybrid work schedule
A defined benefit pension plan (OMERS)
Comprehensive health plan complemented with life and disability insurance
A progressive work environment that promotes a work/life balance and strives to be a great place for great people to do great things
Reporting to the Town Solicitor, as a member of the in-house Legal Department, the Assistant Town Solicitor serves to safeguard and advance the public interest of the municipal corporation by providing legal services and advice to staff and Council, including representing the Town in litigation and hearings, providing oral and written legal opinions, drafting and reviewing legal documents, including agreements and by-laws, preparing and reviewing reports, and attending Council meetings.
What can I expect to do in this role?
Responsible for providing timely and strategic legal services and advice relating to all facets of municipal and planning law to Town staff and Council.
Represent the Town in arbitrations, mediations, and litigation proceedings before the courts and administrative tribunals, including the Ontario Land Tribunal.
Negotiate and draft legal documents that reflect applicable policies.
Develop legal strategies, gather and prepare evidence, conduct legal research, and prepare and present legal arguments and opinions.
Make and explain decisions with respect to interpretations of legislation and by-laws.
Act as instructing counsel to external solicitors.
Work with multi-disciplinary groups to determine the best way to regulate matters and deliver municipal services.
How do I qualify?
A Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) or Juris Doctor (J.D.) and qualified to practice law in Ontario.
A member in good standing with the Law Society of Upper Canada with a minimum of 8 years’ related experience in municipal and planning and development law.
Experience in advocacy before the Ontario Land Tribunal is considered an asset.
Experience providing legal services and advice to municipal and/or broader public sector clients.
Experience negotiating, structuring, drafting, interpreting, and providing legal counsel and services on various types of legal documents, including agreements and by-laws.
Your strengths include demonstrated leadership, interpersonal, communication, and advocacy skills, as well as the ability to manage multiple tasks effectively amidst conflicting demands and tight timelines.
Ability to work both independently and as a collaborative member of a hard-working and collegial team of professionals with a commitment to excellence and client satisfaction.
Strong negotiation, facilitation, mediation, and presentation skills, adaptable for a diverse audience.
Advanced analytical, problem-solving, research, and decision-making abilities.
A well-developed capacity to interpret, anticipate, and convey complex, technical, and abstract information is crucial.
Ability to exercise authority and influence while handling sensitive information and highly confidential matters.
The successful candidate must hold a valid and unrestricted Ontario Driver’s License Class G minimum and will be required to supply their own personal vehicle for performing job duties/corporate business.
Please note that this position requires a satisfactory
criminal record and judicial matters check (CRJMC)
dated within the last 60 days as a condition of employment.
Core Knowledge Required for Success
You have good knowledge of municipal and planning law legislation, including the
Municipal Act, 2001
,
Planning Act, Building Code Act,1992, Development Charges Act, 1997,
and other statutes and regulations pertaining to the work of a municipal lawyer, good knowledge of applicable common law, and an ability to learn and apply corporate and departmental policies and procedures.
In addition, your experience demonstrates the following leadership competencies:
Strategic Thinking
– thinking things through
Engagement
– working effectively with people, organizations, and partners
Management Excellence
– delivering results through own work, relationships, and responsibilities
Accountability and Respect
– serving with integrity and respect
Corporate Values:
Teamwork, accountability, dedication, honesty, innovation, and respect

Reporting to the Maintenance Supervisor, this position is being offered as a full-time permanent staff compliment to the Transit Department (Maintenance Division). Duties will include but not be restricted to:
Lays out, builds, tests, troubleshoots, repairs and modifies developmental and production electronic components, parts, equipment, and systems, such as Smartbus technologies, destination signs, communication equipment, fare collection equipment and other Transit related equipment and systems.

title: Senior Project Manager, Capital Projects
description:
One Team. One Vision. Infinite Possibilities

Employment Opportunity
The City of Pickering is committed to creating an equitable, diverse and inclusive workplace and
strives to foster a sense of belonging, empowerment and respect among all employees and
community members. We recognize and value that diverse perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and
lived experiences contribute to the growth and strength of our organization and community. As such,
we welcome and encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples and equity-deserving communities
including women, persons with disabilities, racialized persons, persons who identify as 2SLGBTQI+,
and other diverse communities.

Senior Project Manager, Capital Projects
Department: Community Services
Classification: 1 Full-time, Permanent
Affiliation: Non-Union
Vacancy Reason: Vacant Existing Position
Shift/Hours: Monday to Friday, 35 hours per week
Salary Range: $137,992.40 to $152,952.80, annually
Work Location: 2460 Brock Road, Pickering, ON
Apply to: Elizabeth Nimmo – Human Resources Generalist, Learning & Development
Date Posted: Thursday, October 15, 2026
Deadline to Apply: Thursday, November 5, 2026 by 12:00 noon

Job Summary
The City of Pickering is seeking a dedicated and motivated individual to join our team in the role of
Senior Project Manager, Capital Projects.

The incumbent is responsible for coordinating and managing the construction administration of major
facilities-related capital projects, including development of budgets, preparation and evaluation of
procurement documents, and preparation of related and administrative studies, memos and reports.
The incumbent also directly assists the Manager, Facilities Capital Projects in the long-term planning
and implementation of major facilities-related construction projects and related Corporate initiatives.

Primary Responsibilities
• Manages assigned major facilities capital projects and related work, serving as primary point of
contact and ensuring compliance with the Corporation’s standards, industry best practices and in
accordance with applicable laws.

• Assigns work and provides supervision, technical advice and direction to staff regarding facilities
capital projects and related work. Checks work in progress and upon completion, ensures
compliance with project close out procedures.

• Defines and develops required scopes of work and services. Manages all project-related
procurement work required within approved schedules and budgets.

• Provides technical advice, written and oral reports, presentations, project resources and
assistance on facilities assets and capital projects to other work groups and departments
throughout the corporation, occasionally including Mayor and Council, stakeholder groups and
members of the public.

• Provides support and input to annual and forecast capital budgets for facilities-related projects.

• Ensures that the planning, scheduling and execution of assigned facilities capital projects aligns
with the Corporation’s needs, strategic goals, policies and procedures, including the timely
submission of draft reports to Council and committees.

• Oversees the work carried out by consultants and contractors on assigned facilities-related
construction projects, including participating in and/or leading related site, construction and
consultant meetings.

• Participates in and/or conducts meetings with residents, community interest groups, members of
the general public, staff stakeholders, consultants and contractors on project-related matters.

• Facilitates and coordinates with authorities having jurisdiction to obtain all required approvals for
assigned projects.

Additional secondary responsibilities may apply and will be outlined in the Job Description, which will
be provided to candidates selected for an interview.

Education and Experience
• Post-secondary Degree in Project Management, Architecture, or any combination of education,
workplace training and experience deemed to be acceptable by the Corporation.
• Membership in the Ontario Association of Architects (OAA) or related, accredited professional
association is an asset.
• Five years of progressively more responsible work-related experience in capital projects, to
include at least three years at a supervisory level, preferably in a municipal environment.
• Proven competence and technical knowledge of various trades and systems involved with
building construction (architectural, structural, civil, mechanical and electrical), building
technologies and related infrastructure.
• Awareness of sustainable construction practices, standards and technologies is an asset,
including related designations.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
• General knowledge of construction-related applicable law, including awareness of health and
safety legislation and regulations applicable to facility operations.
• Proficient in the use of PC equipment and related software applications (MS Office Suite and MS
Project). Working familiarity with graphic editing software (AutoCAD, Adobe Photoshop, etc.) is an
asset.
• Strong leadership, planning, organizational and public relations skills to establish and maintain
effective business relationships with all levels of employees, contractors and vendors.
• Ability to work with multiple priorities in an active and dynamic environment.
• Extensive and comprehensive working knowledge of construction administration, standard forms
of contracts, multiple project delivery methodologies and applicable law.
• Ability to read, understand, navigate and communicate proficiently regarding technical drawings,
specifications and details for building construction and renovation projects.
• Demonstrated ability to exercise effective budget control.
• Must be medically and physically fit to perform the duties of this position.
• Must be prepared to undergo a Criminal Reference Check as a condition of employment.
• Must hold, or acquire within six months, current Standard First Aid and Basic Rescuer CPR-C
certificates.
• Must have a personal vehicle for use in the performance of duties and possess a valid Class “G”
Ontario Driver’s Licence. Must provide consent to conduct regular driver’s abstracts through the
Ministry of Transportation. A clean driving record is preferred
Additional knowledge, skill and abilities may apply and will be outlined in the Job Description.

Compensation also includes a comprehensive benefits package, and an OMERS pension plan.

Qualified candidates may complete an online application form where you will be required to
upload your resume and cover letter (PDFs only). We thank all applicants for their interest, however,
only those selected for an interview will be contacted. In accordance with the Municipal Freedom of
Information and Protection of Privacy Act, personal information is collected under the authority of the
Municipal Act and is used for the purpose of candidate selection.

The City of Pickering is committed to inclusive and barrier-free employment practices, and to creating
a workplace that reflects and supports the diversity of the community we serve. Accommodations are
available throughout the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with
Disabilities Act. Accessible formats and supports can be requested. For assistance, please contact the
Human Resources Department at 905.420.4627 or hr@pickering.ca.
Pickering: A complete, world-class city… inclusive, connected, caring and prosperous.

Experience operating tandem trucks for snow plowing and sanding operations.
Experience operating heavy equipment is considered an asset.
A valid AZ Driver’s Licence is considered an asset.

title: Manager, Human Resources
description:
Full-Time Employment Opportunity
Manager, Human Resources
Salary Range: $115,356-$134,950

Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer, as a member of the senior management team, this position is
responsible for overseeing all Human Resources functions within the organization. The Human Resources
Manager provides leadership and subject matter expertise to management and staff in a variety of areas such
as employee and labour relations, policy & collective agreement interpretation, coaching, organizational design,
staffing, investigations, attendance management, and training and development. The HR Manager also has
functional oversight of the following corporate HR programs: health, safety and wellness; disability management
and attendance support; recruitment and onboarding; employee engagement; and performance management.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

A. Staffing:
• Corporate recruitment processes including staffing needs analysis, attraction methods (job postings,
advertising, etc.), screening, interviewing, selection, pre-employment assessments, and preparing offers
of employment. Coordinate with external staffing agencies, as required.
• Provide coaching and support to hiring managers through staffing, recruitment and on-boarding
processes.
• Work collaboratively at department and divisional levels to help design new structures and jobs to meet
the ongoing operational needs, including development of organizational charts and job descriptions.
• Oversight of succession plan for the Township.
• Provide expertise and guidance to managers and staff on disability and other accommodation requests.

B. Compensation and Benefits:
• Lead job evaluation processes, including maintaining current job descriptions and job evaluation records.
• Lead attendance support programs including managing short term disability and long-term disability
claims, return to work plans, accommodation and modification.
• Negotiate salaries based on the current salary grids.
• In coordination with the Finance Department, administer pay practices as per the collective agreement.
• Answer basic benefit inquiries from staff and management regarding entitlements.
• Answer questions on sick leave administration.

C. Organizational Development:
• Conduct needs analysis for departments and prescribe training and development.
• Recommend external training programs, trainers and/or methods to respond to department training
needs.
• Coordinate and lead instruction on various topics including but not limited to: leadership development,
change management, Personality Dimensions, team development, crisis intervention, and dealing with
difficult people.
• Oversee performance management and employee development programs.
• Provide project management for organization-wide-people initiatives.
• Chair the Engagement and Wellness staff committee; organize and facilitate events and team
engagement activities.

D. Employee Relations:
• Conduct investigations, advise on policy violations, and make recommendations for corrective actions.
• Assist managers to implement performance improvement plans.
• Provide advice on disciplinary matters such as past practices, the appropriate level and type of
discipline, and whether or not to discipline.
• Develop comprehensive reports and present the findings and conclusions to senior management,
Council, and the employee(s) involved.
• Conduct terminations as needed.

E. Labour Relations:
• Lead negotiations for the Township on collective agreement contracts, grievances, hearings,
memorandums of understanding, etc.
• Liaise with the various provincial ministries, boards, external lawyers, consultants, insurance brokers &
carriers, and other municipalities as needed.
• Provide advice and guidance on matters pertaining to collective agreement administration.
• Advise management staff of Memorandum of Settlements and how they affect their department.
• Provide advice on legislation-related issues such as the Employment Standards Act, Labour Relations
Act, Human Rights Code, etc.
• Attend grievance meetings, mediation and arbitration hearings.
• Implement grievance or arbitration settlements.
• Ensure the grievance process is conducted in accordance with the relevant collective agreement,
legislation, and arbitral jurisprudence.

F. Policies and Procedures:
• Identify and develop HR policies and procedures for the Township.
• Examine past/current practices to ensure consistency within department/Township, and identify issues
that may lead to policy development, training, etc.
• Review and recommend changes to current HR policies.

G. Leadership
• This position oversees the HR Advisor role and provides guidance and support, coaching and counseling;
feedback and performance appraisal.
• Sets goals for the department in collaboration with the HR Advisor and evaluates progress.
• Ensure quality service is delivered to all staff.

H. Additional Responsibilities:
• Oversee the Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, Accessibility staff committee
• Responsible for oversight of Health and Safety for the Township; accountable for policies regarding the
safety and security of employees and facilities and ensuring that employees work safely and in
compliance with the relevant statutes, regulations, and safe work procedures and directives as established
by the Township.
• Undertake special projects and perform other related duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor’s Degree in Labour Relations and/or Human Resources or Bachelor’s Degree and post-graduate
Diploma in Labour Relations and/or Human Resources.
• A minimum of five (5) years’ experience in a HR management role in a unionized setting.
• Labour relations and collective bargaining experience in a municipal or public sector environment.
• Demonstrated experience in benefits, staffing, compensation, and first line collective agreement
administration.
• Thorough knowledge of employment legislation; collective agreements; Occupational Health and Safey
Act; Ontario Human Rights Code; Township Policy Manual; and HR policies and procedures.
• Certified Human Resources Leader (CHRL) designation is an asset.
• Adult Educators Certificate is an asset.
• Valid Class “G” Ontario Driver’s License, with regular access to a vehicle for corporate matters.

COMPETENCIES REQUIRED:
• Extensive mediation and negotiation skills.
• Demonstrated problem-solving and conflict/dispute resolution skills.
• Sound decision-making skills and the ability to think strategically to solve complex issues and create
innovative solutions.
• Superior consultative and written/verbal communication skills, including dealing with difficult
people/situations.
• Training, facilitating and presentation skills.
• Coaching and mentoring skills, and the ability to build effective teams and develop others.

• Strong organizational and time management skills.
• Ability to establish credibility with clients, both internal and external and effective interpersonal
communication.
• Knowledge of computer and related software programs.

A full job description is available upon request. Please email resumes@scugog.ca to request a copy.

The successful candidate must provide, prior to commencing employment, a satisfactory criminal reference
check from Canadian Police Information Centre.

Note: As part of the selection process, applicants may be required to complete a written and/or oral and/or
practical test.

Please submit a cover letter and resume outlining current experience, background, and education, no later than

resumes@scugog.ca .

title: School Crossing Guard, Regular and Spare

School Crossing Guard (Regular and Spare)
Community Services Department

The Township of Scugog is hiring regular and spare School Crossing Guards for the 2025/2026

• Be courteous and have the ability to deal effectively with children, school staff and the public;
• Endure varying weather conditions;
• Be punctual and stay for the entire scheduled shift time; and

Canadian Police Information Centre

title: Recreation Staff
description:
Student Employment Opportunity
Part-Time Student Recreation Staff
September 2026 to June 2027 – schedules will vary
$17.95 to $18.45 per hour
PUBLIC WORKS AND RECREATION DEPARTMENT

Reporting to the Recreation and Culture Coordinator and Recreation Programmer, the Recreation Staff will be
responsible for supervising, facilitating, and assisting with recreation and culture programming and events.
The responsibilities of this position are as follows:
• Demonstrate superior customer service and communication skills to deal effectively and courteously with the
public, participants, parents, and staff
• Ensure the safety, enjoyment, and care of participants
• Facilitate various recreation programs, workshops, school break camps and birthday parties
o Recreation programs include but are not limited to learn to skate, dance, sport, gymnastics, art,
leadership and general recreation activities
• Supervise, monitor capacities, and take admissions for various drop-in recreation programs
• Assist with recreation and culture events
• Set up, take down and cleaning of program areas
• Report all incidents, accidents, issues, and concerns to the Recreation and Culture Coordinator
• Complete paperwork as required
Qualifications and Skills:

• Candidates must be at least 15 years old and be enrolled in high-school, or post-secondary education
• Ability to work shifts, including evenings, weekends and holidays as required at the Scugog Community
Recreation Centre, Blackstock Recreation Complex, and schools in the Scugog area
• Possess and keep current Intermediate First Aid/CPR ‘C’
• Provide a current Criminal Information Request prior to employment start date (applicants 18 years and older)
• Experience working or volunteering with children between 2 to 12 years of age
• High Five Principles of Healthy Childhood Development or willing to obtain
• Ability and knowledge of ice skating would be considered an asset
